**Anamorphosis.** When you write, draw, or paint something, you can make it legible only to creatures you choose; anyone else sees a smear, a landscape, or a different picture of your choice. *Detect Magic* shows it as magical, but only *True Seeing* or your permission reads it.

features.name: Perspective
features.text: As a Bonus Action, you can spend 1 Ease to choose a point you can see within 60 feet of you. Until the start of your next turn, the space within 30 feet of that point is drawn to it: each creature of your choice moving toward the point moves 10 extra feet when it moves, and every other creature in that space treats it as Difficult Terrain when it moves away from the point.

features.name: The Masterpiece
features.text: You make the one great work of your career: a painting, a ceiling, a garden, or a building, made over at least a month of downtime. While it stands, the house that holds it can't be perceived through divination magic unless you allow it, and you always know the direction and distance to it. Anyone who has stood before it and been moved by it treats you as a friend the first time you meet.

subclasses.name: Grace
subclasses.lead: * Montaigne's essays, Gracián's art of worldly wisdom, the salon, the tea ceremony: life itself as the art worth mastering. Its emblem is the crane standing watch with a stone in its raised foot, so that if it sleeps the stone falls and wakes it: Europe's old sign of vigilance, and the same bird Kyoto paints on its screens. Grace's work is the evening itself: who sits where, who speaks, and who goes home pleased. Grace forgoes no art, so only a Courtier of Grace can reach a Regard of 5.*

features.name: Conversation
features.text:
When you spend at least 1 minute in conversation with a creature that can understand you, outside combat, you can spend 1 Ease to change its attitude toward you by one step (from Hostile to Indifferent, or from Indifferent to Friendly) without a check. It doesn't realize anything has been done to it. You can't use this feature on the same creature again until you finish a Long Rest.

**The Hostess.** You can use With Ease on a Charisma check made by an ally who can see or hear you, spending your own Ease. You set up the bard's plea or the soldier's clumsy toast, and it lands.

**Evenings.** Hosts everywhere want the evening that goes right, and the ones who can't manage it ask you. Roll on the table below when you're between engagements.

features.name: Composure
features.text: While you aren't Frightened, you and your allies within 10 feet of you have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Frightened condition. In addition, when an ally you can see within 30 feet of you fails a saving throw, you can use Make It Look Easy on its roll as if it were yours.

features.name: A Maxim a Day
features.text: At dawn, speak a maxim aloud: one from the table below, or one of your own. Once before the next dawn, when you or an ally who heard it acts on the maxim, that creature has Advantage on the D20 Test it's making; or, if it's you and you're using an Ease option on that roll, the option can cost no Ease instead. The table gives samples and the moments they fit; a maxim of your own fits whatever moment the table agrees it does.

features.name: Poise Under Fire
features.text:
When an ally you can see within 30 feet of you gains the Charmed, Frightened, or Stunned condition, you can take a Reaction and spend 1 Ease to end that condition on it.

**A Word in Time.** You can use Not a Hair Out of Place when an ally you can see within 10 feet of you is hit by an attack roll, adding your Charisma modifier to the ally's AC against that attack instead of to yours. Your composure is catching: a hand on the arm, a word at the right moment, and the blow goes wide.

features.name: Reputation
features.text: In any settlement where you've spent at least a week, people of every rank know who you are, and your Regard counts as 1 higher there, even above 5 (so you Read one more creature, With Ease counts one higher, and so on). You're offered lodging in a good house without asking, invitations find you within a day of your arrival, and any host who receives you is honored to have done so.

features.name: The Life Is the Work
features.text: When you or an ally you can see within 60 feet of you would fail a D20 Test, you can make it a success instead. Whatever happened becomes a story people tell, at court and in taverns, and it's always told in your favor. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclasses.name: Psyche
subclasses.lead: * Le Brun's lecture on the expression of the passions (1668), Descartes's* Passions of the Soul *(1649), and the Ottoman hospitals that treat the troubled mind with music, water, and quiet.*

features.name: People, Not Canvases
features.text:
Your college forgoes Muses. In exchange, you gain proficiency in the Insight and Medicine skills (if you already have either, choose another skill instead), and the physicians of any hospital will let you work beside them.

**Real or Performed.** When a creature shows a passion in front of you (tears at a funeral, rage in a council, a lover's sigh), you know whether it's felt or performed.

**Cases.** Families, abbesses, and commanders send for you when the trouble is in someone's head and the physicians have run out of remedies. Roll on the table below when you're between cases.

features.name: Wanting and Fearing
features.text:
When you see a creature's face, you know which passion is strongest in it: fear, desire, grief, rage, or joy. As a Bonus Action, you can work on one creature you can see within 60 feet of you:

- *Stir.* A Hostile creature's passion rises: it has Disadvantage on the next attack roll or saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn. Stirring costs 1 Ease, or nothing if the creature has made an attack roll against you since the end of your last turn.
- *Settle.* For 1 Ease, a creature's passion subsides: it has Advantage on the next saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn, and if it has the Charmed or Frightened condition, that condition ends.

Stir spoils one roll for a foe, and anyone who has come at you is already halfway there; Settle steadies one roll for a friend.

features.name: Boundless Passion
features.text: When you Settle a creature, each other creature of your choice within 10 feet of it also gains Settle's benefit. When a creature you've Stirred makes an attack roll against you before the start of your next turn, it takes Psychic damage equal to a roll of your Telling Cut die, whether it hits or misses.

features.name: Catharsis
features.text: When you Settle a creature, or end a condition on a creature with a spell, it regains Hit Points equal to a roll of your Telling Cut die plus your Charisma modifier. (The creatures that Boundless Passion spreads Settle to don't regain Hit Points.)

features.name: Mastery of the Passions
features.text: You can work on a whole crowd's passions at once. Outside combat, you can spend 10 minutes among a crowd, a household, or a gathering of up to a few hundred people and choose one passion to Stir or Settle in all of them: a riot cools, a feud's two families can sit at one table for the evening, a frightened town takes heart, or a festive one turns ugly. The crowd doesn't know it was you. The effect lasts until the next dawn, and you can't use this feature again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclasses.name: Verse
subclasses.lead: * Shakespeare's heirs, Molière, the commedia, kabuki, kunqu, the Ottoman shadow play, the ghazal, the pulpit orator, the satire of the* filí*, Ireland's court poets.*

features.name: The Stage over the Field
features.text:
Your college forgoes Arms. In exchange, you gain proficiency in the Performance skill and with the Disguise Kit (if you already have either, choose another skill or tool instead), and you can perform anything you've seen performed, even once. The stage teaches one thing with a blade: you gain one Fighting Style feat of your choice. Accomplishments that list only Arms, the Fencing Style among them, stay closed to you.

**The Repertory.** A company or a patron will take you on for a season wherever plays are licensed, and some will hide you where they aren't. Roll on the table below when you're between engagements.

features.name: The Mask
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, you can spend 1 Ease to put on a mask and become an archetype for 1 minute. Until that minute ends, you can change to another mask as a Bonus Action without spending Ease, or take yours off (no action required). You can wear one mask at a time.

- **The Captain** (the painted-face general of Chinese opera) swaggers. The first time on each of your turns that you hit a creature with a weapon, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or have Disadvantage on attack rolls against you until the end of its next turn.
- **Harlequin** (the martial clown of Chinese opera, who fights in somersaults) tumbles. Your Speed increases by 10 feet, you can take the Dash or Disengage action as a Bonus Action, and climbing and jumping cost you no extra movement.
- **The Pedant** (Hacivat of the Ottoman shadow play, who has a learned word for everything) is always certain. You have Advantage on Intelligence checks, and on Wisdom (Insight) checks to tell whether a creature is lying.
- **Pantaloon** (the master of Japanese *kyōgen*, whom his servant Tarō-kaja is always outwitting) bargains. The first time on each of its turns that a creature that can hear you would attack you, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or offer you terms instead and lose that attack: it can't make the attack against you or anyone else, whether or not you accept its terms. The DM says what it thinks is a fair bargain; usually, its own safe passage out of the fight.
- **Columbine** (Hongniang, the clever maid of *The Western Chamber*) sees through everyone. Once on each of your turns (no action required), you can look closely at one creature or object you can see within 30 feet of you: you see through any illusion, disguise, or shape-change on it, and you know a shape-changer for what it is. This isn't Truesight: it doesn't show you what's invisible or what's on another plane.

Each mask goes by the commedia's name first and by other names wherever plays are staged; wear it under the name your court knows. Kunqu and kabuki cast by role type in the same way (kunqu's scholar, lady, painted-face general, and clown), and any company can cast all five.

features.name: The Aside
features.text:
You can speak to one creature you can see within 60 feet of you so that no one else hears you, even in a crowd or a fight. When you do, you can make your words land as if you'd had an hour with it: if it can understand you, you make one Charisma check against it with Advantage, and its attitude toward you can't worsen because of what you said. Once you make your words land this way, you can't do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

**The Cutting Line.** You know *Vicious Mockery*; if you already did, learn another cantrip from the Courtier spell list. When you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with a casting of *Vicious Mockery*, and Telling Cut applies to it when the target fails its save, as if you'd hit it with a weapon. The poet stabs once and insults once, and against a foe whose armor is thick and whose wits are thin, the insult goes deeper.

features.name: Satire
features.text: As a Bonus Action, you can spend 1 Ease to mock a creature you can see within 60 feet of you that can hear you. It takes Psychic damage equal to two rolls of your Telling Cut die plus your Charisma modifier, and it has Disadvantage on its next saving throw before the end of your next turn while everyone who heard you laughs.

features.name: All the World
features.text:
Your work is known: any company of players anywhere in the world will stage a play of yours, and any court that keeps a stage will receive you as its author.

You've played every part, and now you can play two at once: you can wear two masks at the same time.

multiclass.gains: Hit Point Die, proficiency in one skill of your choice, and training with Light armor
multiclass.text: You must have a Charisma score of 13 or higher. Gain the following traits from the Core Courtier Traits table: Hit Point Die, proficiency in one skill of your choice, and training with Light armor. Gain the Courtier's level 1 features, which are listed in the Courtier Features table. For multiclass spell slots, add half your Courtier levels (round up). If you have more levels in another class than in this one, your Ease maximum can't exceed your Courtier level, and you regain expended Ease only when you finish a Long Rest.

data.name: Mhizha
data.blurb: Int half caster. Mutapa’s artificer: magic through tools, and an Arc Gun in the fight.

traits.value: *Choose 2:* Arcana, History, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, Perception, or Sleight of Hand
Simple weapons, and Martial weapons that have the Ammunition and Loading properties
Tinker's Tools, and one type of Artisan's Tools of your choice
Light and Medium armor and Shields
*Choose A or B:* (A) Scale Mail, Shield, Dagger, Tinker's Tools, the Artisan's Tools you chose, Scholar's Pack, and 10 GP; or (B) 150 GP

features.name: Spellcasting
features.text:
You cast spells through the tools in your hands. See the rules on spellcasting for how spells work. The information below details how you use those rules with Mhizha spells, which appear in the Mhizha spell list later in the class's description.

**Cantrips.** You know two cantrips of your choice from the Mhizha spell list. *Guidance* and *Prestidigitation* are recommended. Whenever you gain a Mhizha level, you can replace one of your cantrips with another cantrip of your choice from the Mhizha spell list. When you reach Mhizha levels 10 and 14, you learn another cantrip of your choice from the Mhizha spell list, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Mhizha Features table.

**Spell Slots.** The Mhizha Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

**Prepared Spells of Level 1+.** You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Mhizha spells. *Cure Wounds* and *Faerie Fire* are recommended. The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Mhizha levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Mhizha Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Mhizha spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. If another Mhizha feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Mhizha spells for you.

**Changing Your Prepared Spells.** When you finish a Long Rest, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of the spells there with other Mhizha spells for which you have spell slots.

**Spellcasting Ability.** Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Mhizha spells.

**Spellcasting Focus.** You cast Mhizha spells through a tool: Tinker's Tools, Artisan's Tools you're proficient with, or your Arc Gun. You must be holding one of them to cast a Mhizha spell, even one with no Material component, and it serves as your Spellcasting Focus for that spell; the hand holding it can perform the spell's Somatic components.

features.name: Arc Gun
features.text:
You carry a weapon of your own design that throws lightning. The Arc Gun is a magic item that only you can fire.

**Firing It.** The coil holds one charge and a shot spends all of it, so firing the Arc Gun is the whole of your Attack action: make a ranged attack roll using Intelligence against a creature or object within 120 feet of yourself, adding your Proficiency Bonus. On a hit, the target takes Lightning damage equal to the dice shown in the Arc Gun column of the Mhizha Features table plus your Intelligence modifier. The dice step up at levels 5, 7, 15, and 20. Between 7 and 15 the gun grows through Arc Chain (level 11) and your subclass. You can fire the Arc Gun only once per turn. You must hold the Arc Gun to fire it, and it takes one hand, so you can fire it with a Shield on your other arm; you can draw or stow it as part of the attack, as with a weapon.

**What the Shot Is.** The shot is a ranged attack roll that is neither a weapon attack nor a spell attack.

- *What applies:* everything that applies to any attack roll or any ranged attack roll. That includes cover, Advantage and Disadvantage (including the Disadvantage for firing with an enemy within 5 feet of you), and Critical Hits, which roll the shot's dice twice.
- *What doesn't:* anything that calls for a weapon, an attack with a weapon, or a spell attack. That rules out weapon masteries, the Archery fighting style, Sharpshooter (*Player's Handbook*), Sneak Attack, and *Magic Weapon* cast on the Arc Gun, and it rules out riders on spell attacks.
- *Extra Attack:* the shot is the whole of your Attack action, so Extra Attack from another class adds nothing on a turn you fire.
- *Antimagic:* the Arc Gun is a magic item and doesn't fire in an Antimagic Field.

**Rebuilding It.** If the Arc Gun is lost (out of your possession for 1 hour) or destroyed, you can build a new one with Tinker's Tools over the course of a Long Rest; the old one stops working.

features.name: Tinker
features.text:
With Tinker's Tools and 1 minute of work, you can mend a single break or tear in a nonmagical object you touch, as the *Mending* cantrip does, or build a Tiny clockwork trinket that does one simple thing (ticks, chimes at a set hour, walks in a line, plays a few bars of music). A trinket stops working after 8 hours. You can have a number of trinkets equal to your Proficiency Bonus at a time; if you build another, your oldest stops working.

*Arc Lamp.* A trinket can be an Arc Lamp *(Electrical)*. It sheds Bright Light in a 30-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 30 feet, or Bright Light in a 60-foot Cone and Dim Light for an additional 60 feet. It has no flame, works underwater, and can be shuttered or opened as a Bonus Action.

*Retuning.* You can hear when a device has drifted. With Tinker's Tools and 10 minutes of work, you can retune a Mutapan curiosity (a self-lighting lamp, a stove, a pump, any small work that has fallen out of calibration) so it works as new. Anyone a Mhizha has taught can do the same in an hour; no one else can do it at all. Abroad, this pays: the owner of a drifting lamp is usually rich, often grateful, and sometimes talkative, and a retuning can get you through a door that a letter of introduction wouldn't. The going rate is a gold piece or two, or a favor, and Mutapa's merchant houses, who sell the same service abroad, keep a list of Mhizha who work for less.

features.name: Preparations
features.text:
You make your own smoke, slick, and flash. When you finish a Long Rest, you can spend 1 hour of it with Tinker's Tools to make the number of Preparations shown in the Preparations column of the Mhizha Features table. They last until you finish your next Long Rest, and only you know how to use them. Preparations aren't magical.

As a Bonus Action, you expend a Preparation and throw it at a point you can see within 30 feet of yourself, and choose which kind it is. Its saving throw uses your spell save DC.

- *Smoke.* A 10-foot-radius Sphere centered on that point is Heavily Obscured until the end of your next turn. A strong wind disperses it.
- *Slick.* A 10-foot square centered on that point is Difficult Terrain for 1 minute. Each creature in the square when it appears, and each creature that enters it or starts its turn there, makes a Dexterity saving throw; on a failed save, it has the Prone condition. (A Prone creature is easy for your friends' blades and hard to hit from range, your Arc Gun included.)
- *Flash.* Each creature in a 5-foot-radius Sphere centered on that point makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it has the Blinded condition until the end of its next turn.

features.name: Devices
features.text:
You build small devices that each do one thing well. You know every design under Device Designs, below, for which you qualify.

**Building Devices.** When you finish a Long Rest, you can spend 1 hour of it with Tinker's Tools to build devices, each of a different design. The number you build is shown in the Devices column of the Mhizha Features table. In the same hour, you make your Preparations (see above). When you build devices, any you built earlier stop working. You can use a device yourself or hand it to another creature; a device works for whoever wears or holds it.

*Reading the Job.* Build for what's coming. A Mhizha who hears tonight that the vault is under the canal builds the Breathing Helm and the Lockbreaker before morning, and a Mhizha's ears prick up at every hint about tomorrow.

**Magical and Electrical.** A device marked *Electrical* isn't magic: it runs on the current it has stored, enough to work where magic fails, so an Antimagic Field or *Dispel Magic* doesn't stop it. Every other device is a magic item that doesn't require Attunement; it stops working in an Antimagic Field or if you die.

**Durability and Loss.** A device is an object with AC 15 and 5 Hit Points; at 0 Hit Points it is destroyed. A device is lost if it has been out of your possession, and out of the possession of anyone you gave it to, for 1 hour.

#### Device Designs

**Charged Plate** *(Electrical)*. The plate isn't armor, and it can be worn with armor. When the wearer finishes a Short or Long Rest, the wearer gains Temporary Hit Points equal to your Mhizha level plus your Intelligence modifier.

**Clockwork Servant.** A Tiny clockwork figure that works as the servant created by the *Unseen Servant* spell, except that it's visible, it obeys a creature you designate when you build it, and it lasts until you build the device again.

**Lockbreaker** *(Electrical)*. A creature using it with Thieves' Tools adds your Intelligence modifier to checks to pick locks and disarm traps.

**Shock Gauntlet** *(Electrical)*. Once on each of its turns, when the wearer hits a creature with an Unarmed Strike or an attack with a melee weapon, the creature takes an extra 1d4 Lightning damage.

**Spring Boots.** The wearer's jump distances are tripled, and it takes no damage from a fall of 30 feet or less.

**Grapple Line** *(Electrical; Prerequisite: Mhizha level 5)*. Once on each of its turns, as a Bonus Action, the holder can fire the line at a solid surface within 60 feet of itself and be pulled in a straight line to an unoccupied space next to that point. This movement doesn't cost the holder any Speed, and it provokes Opportunity Attacks as normal.

**Night Lenses** *(Prerequisite: Mhizha level 5)*. The wearer has Darkvision with a range of 60 feet.

**Seeing Spectacles** *(Prerequisite: Mhizha level 5)*. The wearer sees creatures and objects that have the Invisible condition within 30 feet of itself as if they were visible, and has Advantage on Intelligence (Investigation) checks to discern an illusion.

**Breathing Helm** *(Prerequisite: Mhizha level 9)*. The wearer can breathe underwater and isn't affected by smoke or by gas that must be inhaled, and it sees clearly underwater. It doesn't let the wearer see through an area that is Heavily Obscured.

**Speaking Wires** *(Electrical; Prerequisite: Mhizha level 9)*. Two handsets joined by nothing anyone can see. Whoever holds one can speak in a whisper to whoever holds the other, if the two are within 1 mile of each other.

**Flight Pack** *(Prerequisite: Mhizha level 13)*. The wearer has a Fly Speed equal to its Speed. The wearer turns the pack on or off (no action required). The pack works for a total of 1 hour, in increments of 1 minute or more, and then not again until you build it again.

features.name: Mhizha Subclass
features.text: You gain a Mhizha subclass of your choice: the Chemist, the Constructor, the Gunner, the Lionskin, or the Mapmaker. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Mhizha levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Mhizha level or lower.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Mhizha levels 8, 12, and 16.

features.name: Overcharge
features.text: Once per turn, when you hit a creature with the Arc Gun, you can expend a spell slot to overcharge the shot. The creature takes an extra 2d8 Lightning damage, plus 1d8 for each spell slot level above 1.

features.name: Field Workshop
features.text: You keep a workshop in your pack. When you finish a Short Rest, you regain two expended Preparations (three from level 13), and with Tinker's Tools you can rebuild one device that was lost or destroyed since your last Long Rest, unless you destroyed it or gave it up on purpose.

features.name: Flare
features.text: When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to expend a Preparation and throw it as a Flash at the attacker before the roll; only the attacker is affected. It makes a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, it has the Blinded condition until the end of its next turn, including against the triggering attack.

features.name: How It Works
features.text: You can spend 1 minute handling an object to learn what it does. If it's a magic item, you learn its properties as if you had cast *Identify* on it. If it's a mechanism, a lock, or a trap, you learn how it works, and you have Advantage on ability checks to operate, open, or disarm it.

features.name: Arc Chain
features.text: When you hit a creature with the Arc Gun, lightning leaps from it to a second creature of your choice that you can see within 10 feet of it, which takes damage of the shot's type equal to your Intelligence modifier.

features.name: Master Artisan
features.text: Choose two of your tool proficiencies. You have Expertise with them. In addition, crafting a magic item takes you two-thirds as long and costs two-thirds as much as normal.

features.name: Overload
features.text: When you overcharge a shot, the creature Arc Chain leaps to also takes the Overcharge's extra damage.

features.name: The Sealed Art
features.text:
You can set glamour in platinum (*The Setting*, Characters, Wonders and Curiosities, Glamour). Here is what that means at the table.

- **A measure** is one handful of glamour, the raw stuff of the Hidden. It is gathered on thin ground (a place where the Hidden and the mortal world run together) or in the Hidden Realm itself, and an unset measure is gone by the next dawn. The gathering rule is in *The Setting*, at the reference above.
- **Setting a measure in platinum** takes you 1 hour, Tinker's Tools, and platinum worth 50 GP. A measure set in platinum keeps indefinitely.
- **A set measure** is a Common magic item that needs no Attunement. As a Magic action, its holder releases its property once, and it recharges at dawn.
- **Each measure has one property,** which the DM chooses or rolls when it is gathered:

| d8 | Property | Released |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Thorn** | A creature you touch makes a DC 13 Strength saving throw or is Restrained until the end of its next turn. |
| 2 | **Mist** | A 10-foot-radius Sphere of fog for 1 minute; you can see through it, and others can't. |
| 3 | **Light** | Bright moonlight in a 20-foot radius for 1 minute; it shows what is invisible or in a seeming. |
| 4 | **Step** | You teleport up to 20 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. |
| 5 | **Seeming** | An object you touch looks like another object of its size for 1 hour. |
| 6 | **Song** | Each creature of your choice within 15 feet makes a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw or is Charmed by you until the end of its next turn. |
| 7 | **Frost** | Water within 15 feet freezes solid enough to walk on for 10 minutes. |
| 8 | **Return** | For 1 hour it points the way to the nearest door into the Hidden. |

The Sealed Art brings three more things:

- **Living Devices.** When you build devices, you can set one platinum measure into one of them. While the device is worn or held, its holder can release the measure's property as a Bonus Action instead of a Magic action. It recharges at dawn, as any platinum measure does.
- **The Arc Remembers.** You can set one platinum measure into your Arc Gun. When you overcharge a shot, you can also release that property on the target as part of the hit, using your spell save DC in place of DC 13. A property that fills an area or reaches the creatures around you (Mist, Light, Song, Frost) is centered on the target, and Thorn affects the target as if you had touched it. A property that moves you or works on an object (Step, Seeming, Return) works as it normally does and doesn't affect the target.
- **A Door of Your Own.** Once per Long Rest, as a Magic action, you can open a door into the Hidden on any surface. It stays open for 1 minute and leads to a pocket that only you and creatures you choose can find again: a sealed room, 30 feet on a side, that keeps whatever you leave in it. It is the same room each time. It has air, and a creature can stay inside when the door closes. A creature inside can leave at any time and arrives where the door last opened.

features.name: Grounded
features.text: You have Resistance to Lightning and Thunder damage, and Advantage on Constitution saving throws to maintain Concentration.

features.name: Epic Boon
features.text: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Fate is recommended.

features.name: Lightning Itself
features.text:
The Arc Gun's damage (the shot's, including extra damage your features add to the shot) ignores Resistance, and a creature with Immunity to the shot's damage type has Resistance to it instead (the shot doesn't ignore that Resistance). Its damage rises to 5d10, as shown in the Arc Gun column of the Mhizha Features table.

> **Playing a Mhizha**
>
> You're the party's workshop. Each morning you build the day's devices and hand most of them out: the Shock Gauntlet and the Charged Plate to whoever stands in front, Spring Boots or the Grapple Line to whoever has to get up the wall.
>
> In a fight, the Arc Gun cracks every turn and your free hand is in the satchel: Smoke to cover a retreat, Flash in the eyes of whoever frightens you most, Slick to drop a crowd for your friends' blades. From 5th level, Overcharge turns a spell slot into a heavy hit; from 7th, Flare can blind an attacker before its roll.
>
> Keep a tool in your hand: every Mhizha spell is cast through one. Out of a fight, your hands open doors: you mend, retune and take things apart to see how they work.

features.name: Chemist Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Mhizha level specified in the Chemist Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Mhizha Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Cure Wounds*, *Ray of Sickness* |
| 5 | *Acid Arrow*, *Lesser Restoration* |
| 9 | *Gaseous Form*, *Stinking Cloud* |
| 13 | *Blight*, *Vitriolic Sphere* |
| 17 | *Cloudkill*, *Greater Restoration* |

features.name: Tria Prima
features.text:
You gain proficiency with Alchemist's Supplies; if you already have it, choose another type of Artisan's Tools. When you build your devices, you can also use Alchemist's Supplies to make a batch of three elixirs (four from level 10), each of a kind you choose as you make it, in any mix: Salt, Sulfur, or Mercury. An elixir is magical, and it lasts until you finish your next Long Rest. A creature can drink an elixir, or administer it to a creature within 5 feet of itself, as a Bonus Action.

- *Salt* (the body). The drinker regains Hit Points equal to 2d8 plus your Intelligence modifier.
- *Sulfur* (the soul). For 1 minute, once on each of the drinker's turns when it hits a creature with an attack roll, that creature takes an extra 1d6 Fire damage.
- *Mercury* (the spirit). For 1 minute, the drinker's Speed increases by 10 feet, and Opportunity Attacks against it have Disadvantage.

*Assay.* With Alchemist's Supplies and 10 minutes of work, you learn what a sample of metal, ore, or coin is made of and how pure it is: whether gold is good, whether silver has been cut, and whether a bar has been weighted with a gray metal that isn't silver. Merchants, mints, and moneylenders pay well for this, and the word of an assayer of the House of the Bird, Mutapa's bank, is accepted from Sofala to Surat. The House of the Bird licenses its assayers (a season in one of its assay offices, and a bond of 100 GP); an unlicensed Chemist's assay is just as right, but no bank has to honor it.

features.name: Nigredo
features.text:
You begin the Work by breaking matter down. When you fire the Arc Gun, you can have it deal Acid damage instead of Lightning damage; Lightning Itself applies to the shot whatever its damage type. When Arc Chain would leap from an Acid shot, you can instead have the acid keep working: the target takes Acid damage equal to your Intelligence modifier at the start of its next turn.

*Vitriol.* You can throw a Preparation as Vitriol, a fourth kind. Each creature in a 5-foot-radius Sphere centered on that point makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, it takes Acid damage equal to your Intelligence modifier and has a −2 penalty to Armor Class until the end of your next turn.

In addition, with Alchemist's Supplies and 10 minutes of work, you can dissolve a nonmagical object that fits in a 1-foot Cube and isn't being worn or carried (a lock, a hinge, a length of chain) into a black residue.

features.name: Albedo
features.text:
You purify what you have broken down. Your Salt elixir also ends the Poisoned condition and one disease on the drinker. You have Resistance to Poison damage, and you can purify food and drink you touch as the *Purify Food and Drink* spell does (no action required).

*Green Salt.* You know how to make the field dressing Mutapa's farms run on. During downtime, with Alchemist's Supplies, a week of work, and materials worth 50 GP, you can dress a farm's fields so that its next harvest is a good one, whatever else the season does short of drought, flood, or locusts. The owner pays in a share of the harvest unless you agree another fee; in a lean year that share is worth a great deal, and a village that's eaten through a famine on your dressing remembers you.

features.name: Citrinitas
features.text:
The Work wakes. Your Salt elixir restores 3d8 Hit Points plus your Intelligence modifier. In addition, when you make your elixirs, you can combine any two of them into a single draught (which uses up both), and it grants both effects when it's drunk.

*A Drop on the Tongue.* You can identify a potion, poison, or drug by tasting a drop of it over 1 minute. You learn what it is and what it does, and you suffer none of its effects from the taste.

features.name: Rubedo
features.text: You complete the Work. When you finish a Long Rest, you can also make the Stone, a red tincture that lasts until you finish your next Long Rest. A creature that drinks the Stone (a Bonus Action) is protected for 8 hours: the first time it would drop to 0 Hit Points without dying outright, it drops to 1 Hit Point instead, and the protection ends.

features.name: Constructor Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Mhizha level specified in the Constructor Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Mhizha Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Heroism*, *Shield of Faith* |
| 5 | *Magic Weapon*, *Warding Bond* |
| 9 | *Haste*, *Protection from Energy* |
| 13 | *Death Ward*, *Faithful Hound* |
| 17 | *Animate Objects*, *Mass Cure Wounds* |

features.name: Construct
features.text:
You build a companion. It uses the Construct stat block below and is Friendly to you and your allies. It shares your Initiative and takes its turn immediately after yours. It can move and use its Reaction on its own. On its turn, it takes the action you commanded with a Bonus Action on your turn (Dash, Disengage, Help, or Utilize); if you gave no command, it makes its Strike if you took the Attack action on your turn, and otherwise it takes the Dodge action. If you have the Incapacitated condition, it can take any action of its choice.

If it drops to 0 Hit Points, it stops working, but it isn't destroyed. When you finish a Long Rest, it starts working again if it had stopped, and it regains all its Hit Points. If your construct is destroyed (its works smashed, melted, or disintegrated) or lost, you can build a new one with Tinker's Tools over the course of a Long Rest. It's built light, to take the first blows meant for you: at low levels, expect it to stop in the day's first hard fight and wait for morning (from level 6, Field Repairs lets you restart it once).

**Construct**

- *Medium Construct, Neutral.* AC 15. Hit Points 2 plus your Intelligence modifier plus twice your Mhizha level. Speed 40 ft.
- *Abilities.* Str 14, Dex 12, Con 14, Int 4, Wis 10, Cha 4.
- *Saving Throws and Checks.* Its ability modifiers plus your Proficiency Bonus.
- *Immunities.* Poison; the Poisoned condition.
- *Senses and Languages.* Darkvision 60 ft. It understands the languages you know but can't speak.
- *In the Doorway.* Enemies can't move through the construct's space, whatever their size. A creature the construct hits with an Opportunity Attack has a Speed of 0 until the end of the current turn.
- *Strike.* Melee Attack Roll: Bonus equals your spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft. Hit: Force damage equal to 1d8 plus your Intelligence modifier.

*Hands for Hire.* Out of a fight, your construct can work a simple, repetitive task (hauling, digging, pumping, turning a mill, carrying one end of a litter) for up to 8 hours without supervision or rest, doing the work of two strong laborers.

features.name: Field Repairs
features.text:
When you finish a Short Rest, your construct regains Hit Points equal to half its Hit Point maximum if it's still working.

*Restart.* As a Magic action with Tinker's Tools, you can restart your stopped construct within 5 feet of you, under fire or after the fight; it starts working again with Hit Points equal to your Mhizha level. Once you restart it, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

*Loaded.* You can throw a Preparation, or use Flare, as if you were standing in your construct's space.

*Sentry.* Your construct doesn't sleep. While you rest, it can keep watch; if it sees or hears a creature it doesn't know within 60 feet of itself, it wakes you with a chime only you can hear.

features.name: Improved Construct
features.text:
Your construct's Strike deals 2d8 Force damage plus your Intelligence modifier.

*Errand.* You can send your construct on an errand to a place or person within 1 mile of you that you describe to it: to carry an object or a sealed message there, wait for an answer if you tell it to, and come back. It takes the route you'd take. It can't speak, and anyone who's met a Constructor knows to put the answer in writing.

features.name: Fail-Safe
features.text: Once per Long Rest, when your construct drops to 0 Hit Points, it drops to half its Hit Point maximum instead.

features.name: Gunner Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Mhizha level specified in the Gunner Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Mhizha Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Burning Hands*, *Thunderwave* |
| 5 | *Scorching Ray*, *Shatter* |
| 9 | *Fireball*, *Wind Wall* |
| 13 | *Ice Storm*, *Wall of Fire* |
| 17 | *Cone of Cold*, *Wall of Force* |

features.name: Turret
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, you set down a turret in an unoccupied space you can see within 10 feet of yourself. It is a Small object with AC 15, Hit Points equal to twice your Mhizha level, and Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. It lasts for 1 hour, until it drops to 0 Hit Points, or until you set down another. Like the Arc Gun, it is magic and doesn't fire in an Antimagic Field. You can set down a turret twice, and you regain both uses when you finish a Long Rest.

While your turret is deployed, it fires whenever you take the Attack action, once per turn (no action required): make a ranged spell attack against a creature the turret can see within 60 feet of it. The turret doesn't fire while you're more than 120 feet away from it. On a hit, the target takes Force damage equal to 1d6 plus your Intelligence modifier (2d6 from Mhizha level 10).

*Mobile Turret.* As a Bonus Action while you're within 5 feet of your turret, you can pick it up and set it down again in an unoccupied space within 10 feet of yourself. This doesn't use one of your turrets.

*Rangefinder.* You know the distance to anything you can see, out to a mile, and the height of anything you can see the top and bottom of, to within a few feet. With 10 minutes and Tinker's Tools you can also tell whether ground is level, which way water will run on it, and whether a wall, bridge, or roof is sound.

features.name: Forward Observer
features.text:
While you're within 120 feet of your turret, you can see and hear through it as well as through your own eyes and ears (no action required), and you can fire the Arc Gun or throw a Preparation as if you were standing in the turret's space.

*Watch.* When you set down your turret out of a fight, you can set it to watch instead of fire. While it watches, it doesn't attack and lasts for 8 hours instead of 1, but if a creature you didn't designate when you set it down comes within 60 feet of it, it sounds a chime that you hear if you're within 1 mile of it.

features.name: Shells
features.text:
When you would fire the Arc Gun, you can fire a shell instead. Each creature in a 10-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point you can see within 120 feet of yourself makes a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes Force damage equal to the Arc Gun's dice plus your Intelligence modifier; on a successful save, it takes half as much damage. Firing a shell is your Attack action, so your turret fires too. You can fire two shells, and you regain both when you finish a Long Rest.

*Signal Shell.* Out of a fight, you can fire a shell that does no damage and isn't expended: it bursts as a light and a sound seen and heard for miles, in a color and pattern you choose. Fired in a code you've agreed in advance, it carries a short message.

features.name: Bulwark
features.text:
While within 10 feet of your turret, you and your allies have a +2 bonus to Armor Class against ranged attack rolls.

*Siegecraft.* With 1 hour to study a fortification, you learn its weakest point, roughly how long it would hold against an assault or a siege, and what it would take to make it hold longer. You have Advantage on any ability check to plan, build, or break a fortification.

features.name: Lionskin Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Mhizha level specified in the Lionskin Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Mhizha Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Magic Missile*, *Thunderwave* |
| 5 | *Mirror Image*, *Shatter* |
| 9 | *Fly*, *Lightning Bolt* |
| 13 | *Fire Shield*, *Freedom of Movement* |
| 17 | *Passwall*, *Wall of Force* |

features.name: Powered Suit
features.text:
You gain Heavy armor training. With Tinker's Tools and 1 hour of work, you can make any armor you wear into your suit. Whatever it was made from, the suit is Heavy armor with a base Armor Class of 18 (your Dexterity doesn't add to it), it has no Strength requirement for you, and you have Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks while you wear it. You can have only one suit at a time; if you make another, the old one is ordinary armor again. The suit's systems run down both arms, so it gives you its Armor Class and the following benefits only while you aren't holding a Shield. While you hold a Shield, the suit works as the armor it was made from: you use that armor's Armor Class, category, and properties, plus the Shield's bonus, and you get none of the benefits below.

- *Built In.* The Arc Gun is built into the suit; you fire it without holding it, and the suit is your Spellcasting Focus, so you don't need to hold a tool to cast a Mhizha spell.
- *Gauntlets.* You can deliver the Arc Gun's shot as a blow: firing it at a creature within 5 feet of you doesn't give you Disadvantage, and you can have that shot deal Force damage instead of Lightning damage. Your Unarmed Strikes deal Force damage equal to 1 plus your Intelligence modifier, and you use Intelligence for their attack rolls.
- *Tailored.* A suit is cut to pass. Out of a fight, it can look like ordinary clothes of your station: court dress, a merchant's coat, a laborer's wrap. A creature that looks closely can tell it's armor with a successful Wisdom (Perception) check against your spell save DC.
- *Model.* When you finish a Long Rest, choose the suit's model, Infiltrator or Guardian.
  - *Infiltrator model.* The suit doesn't give you Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks, and your Speed increases by 10 feet.
  - *Guardian model.* The suit is built to hold a gate. When a creature you can see hits an ally within 5 feet of you with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to reduce the damage by 1d10 plus your Intelligence modifier; you can do this a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Kinetic Charge
features.text: The suit drinks the force that strikes it. When you take damage while you wear it (damage to Temporary Hit Points counts), or you reduce damage with the Guardian's Reaction, the suit becomes charged; it holds one charge at a time. An Infiltrator suit also becomes charged when you roll Initiative. The charge is the suit's whole store, and it goes out in one blow: when you hit a creature with the Arc Gun while the suit is charged, you can release the charge. The creature takes an extra 1d6 Force damage (2d6 if the suit is an Infiltrator). This extra damage increases by 1d6 when you reach Mhizha level 5, and it doesn't grow after that. The charge fades if you take off the suit or finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Suit Systems
features.text:
You gain the following benefits:

- *Built-In Curiosity.* When you build devices, you can also build one Mutapan curiosity into the suit, and change it whenever you build devices again: a curiosity from the Mutapan Curiosities table (*The Setting*, Characters, Wonders and Curiosities; a few are sampled under Mutapan Curiosities at the end of this chapter), or another small convenience the DM allows, such as a lamp in the faceplate that lights on a word; a gauntlet stove that boils water in a minute; a pump in the boots that clears a flooded room or a holed boat; or a speaking-horn that carries your voice to anyone within 300 feet. It works only for you while you wear the suit, and it's lost or destroyed only if the suit is.
- *Model Systems.* *Infiltrator:* you have a Climb Speed equal to your Speed, and when you fall, you take no damage and can move horizontally up to twice the distance you fall. *Guardian:* when you use the Guardian's Reaction to protect an ally within 5 feet of you, you can swap places with it, as long as you're both willing.

features.name: Improved Models
features.text:
*Infiltrator:* as a Bonus Action, you can release the suit's charge to have the Invisible condition until the start of your next turn. *Guardian:* you can't be moved against your will or given the Prone condition while you wear the suit, and your Reaction can protect an ally within 10 feet of you.

*Sealed Seams.* While you wear the suit, you're comfortable in extreme heat and extreme cold, and you automatically succeed on saving throws against Exhaustion from them.

features.name: Flight
features.text: While you wear the suit, you have a Fly Speed equal to your Speed.

features.name: Mapmaker Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Mhizha level specified in the Mapmaker Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Mhizha Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Expeditious Retreat*, *Feather Fall* |
| 5 | *Levitate*, *Misty Step* |
| 9 | *Blink*, *Slow* |
| 13 | *Arcane Eye*, *Dimension Door* |
| 17 | *Passwall*, *Teleportation Circle* |

features.name: The Map
features.text:
You gain proficiency with Cartographer's Tools; if you already have it, choose another type of Artisan's Tools. You carry a map that draws itself: it shows any place you have spent 10 minutes in, you can't become lost except by magic, and it is your Spellcasting Focus while you hold it.

*Fair Copy.* With Cartographer's Tools and 10 minutes of work, you can copy any map, chart, or plan you've seen, from memory, and you can tell at a glance whether a map is accurate, out of date, or a deliberate lie.

*Folds.* You can fold the map a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus plus 2, and you regain all expended folds when you finish a Long Rest. Fold Space costs one fold; Contour Lines costs two.

*Fold Space.* As a Bonus Action, you expend a fold: a willing creature (it can be you) you can see within 30 feet of yourself teleports up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

features.name: Contour Lines
features.text: As a Bonus Action, you expend two folds and draw the ground steeper than it is. Each creature of your choice in a 10-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point you can see within 60 feet of yourself makes a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes Force damage equal to the Arc Gun's dice, has the Prone condition, and has a Speed of 0 until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only.

features.name: Survey
features.text:
You can spend 10 minutes mapping your surroundings. The map shows every secret door, hidden passage, and trap within 60 feet of you that isn't hidden by magic, and you learn the general nature of each trap.

*Route.* When you plan a journey between two places on your map, you know how long it will take at each travel pace, the safest route and the fastest (rarely the same), and every danger the map has recorded on the way: a ford that floods, a pass that closes, a valley where cattle die.

features.name: Wide Fold
features.text:
When you use Fold Space, you can teleport two willing creatures instead of one, and each can teleport up to 30 feet.

*Longitude.* You always know exactly where you are on the face of the world, latitude and longitude both, and the true time where you stand. A ship you navigate can't become lost except by magic.

features.name: Shortcut
features.text: Once per Long Rest, as a Magic action, you fold the map along a line you've drawn: you and up to two willing creatures within 10 feet of you teleport to a place within 500 feet of you that is on your map. Each arrives in an unoccupied space of your choice there.

multiclass.gains: Hit Point Die, proficiency with Tinker's Tools, and training with Light armor
multiclass.text: You must have an Intelligence score of 13 or higher. Gain the following traits from the Core Mhizha Traits table: Hit Point Die, proficiency with Tinker's Tools, and training with Light armor. Gain the Mhizha's level 1 features, which are listed in the Mhizha Features table. For multiclass spell slots, add half your Mhizha levels (round up).

data.name: Natural Philosopher
data.blurb: Int. No magic: the laws the world already obeys.

traits.value: *Choose 3:* Arcana, History, Insight, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, Perception, or Survival
Simple weapons, and Martial weapons that have the Ammunition and Loading properties
*Choose 2:* Alchemist's Supplies, Cartographer's Tools, Glassblower's Tools, Navigator's Tools, or Tinker's Tools
*Choose A or B:* (A) Leather Armor, Light Crossbow, 20 Bolts, Crossbow Bolt Case, Dagger, Scholar's Pack, the two tools you chose, and 10 GP; or (B) 150 GP

features.name: Natural Philosophy
features.text:
You know the world by measuring it.

**Study.** As a Bonus Action, or over 1 minute outside combat, you study a creature, an object, or a feature of the environment that you can see within 60 feet of yourself. You can be studying one creature and one object or feature at a time; studying another replaces the earlier one of the same kind. A creature stays studied for 1 minute, and an object or feature until you finish a Short or Long Rest. This isn't the Study action, and it needs no check. When you study something, you learn one of the following of your choice:

- *A creature:* its Armor Class, which of its saving throws has the lowest bonus, one damage Resistance, Immunity, or Vulnerability it has (the DM chooses if it has several, and tells you if it has none), or its Speeds and special senses.
- *An object or a feature:* what it's made of, roughly how old it is, how it was made, or where it's weakest.

Studying something you're already studying renews it and teaches you another fact from the list. You can also study the place around you; from level 3, that's how you find what Mechanism can set off.

You learn only what can be seen, heard, or measured. Study never tells you what a creature thinks or feels.

**Measure.** You can judge, by eye and with the instruments you carry, the distance to anything you can see, its height, its weight, and its temperature, to within a tenth, and the time of day to within a few minutes.

features.name: Ballistics
features.text:
When you make an attack roll with a crossbow or a firearm, you can use your Intelligence modifier instead of your Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. A firearm is a Pistol, a Musket, or a period firearm such as the pocket pistol (*The Setting*, Characters, Equipment and Firearms); the stonebow is a crossbow.

**Calculated Shot.** Once per turn, when you hit a creature you're studying with an attack roll using a crossbow or a firearm, the attack deals the extra damage shown in the Calculated Shot column of the Natural Philosopher Features table. The extra damage is the same type as the weapon's.

**Weapon Mastery.** You can use the mastery property of one kind of crossbow or firearm you're proficient with, such as Heavy Crossbows or Pistols. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kind you chose. Each one plays differently: a Musket or Light Crossbow slows what it hits, a Heavy Crossbow pushes it (farther, once you learn Leverage), and a Pistol or Hand Crossbow carries Advantage into your next turn.

features.name: Aim
features.text: When you study a creature on your turn, your next attack roll against it before the end of the turn has Advantage if it's a crossbow or firearm attack that uses your Intelligence (see Ballistics). The Advantage comes from the measuring, so you can move as you like before or after, and take the shot from wherever the angle is. Studying a creature you're already studying counts, so you can Aim at the same target every turn.

features.name: First Causes
features.text:
You can ask why. You spend 1 minute examining something in the physical world, and then ask the DM why it happened or is happening: why the bridge failed, why the well went bad, why the ward keeps flickering. The DM answers with the most likely cause that follows from what can be seen, measured, or tested, in a sentence or two. If what you can examine isn't enough, the DM tells you so, and the use isn't expended. The answer is never about what a creature thinks or feels.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Instruments
features.text: Choose two of your tool proficiencies, or one tool proficiency and the Investigation skill (gaining proficiency in Investigation first if you lack it). You have Expertise with your choices.

features.name: Mechanism
features.text:
You turn the place against the people in it, using a law of nature the place already obeys.

**Setting it off.** As a Utilize action, you set off a feature of the place that you're studying, with one precise act from where you stand: a cut rope, a kicked wedge, an opened sluice, a tipped brazier, an angled lens, or, at a distance, a shot, a thrown stone, or a tug on a line already rigged. Choose one of the laws the DM named for the feature, and place a 20-foot Cube with its point of origin within 60 feet of you. Each creature of your choice that is in the Cube and within the feature's reach makes a saving throw (DC 8 plus your Intelligence modifier and Proficiency Bonus).

On a failed save, a creature takes the damage shown in the Mechanism column of the Natural Philosopher Features table and suffers the law's effect. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only. The feature is then spent. What it leaves behind (rubble, a flooded floor) stays, and it isn't a new feature unless the DM says the place has changed enough to hold one.

**What counts as a feature.** A structure under load, a slope, a body of water held back, a fire or a store of powder, a pocket of gas or smoke, a strong light. It has to be part of the place: nothing you or your allies placed, lit, or created there.

**Finding the feature.** When you study the place around you (a Bonus Action, or 1 minute outside combat), the DM names one feature in it you could set off, which laws from the Mechanism table it allows, and what it can reach, and you're now studying that feature. Every place has at least one: a chandelier or a beam overhead, a staircase or a slope, a canal or a cistern, a hearth or a powder store, a window in the sun. Where the DM finds nothing better, the ground itself will do: loose stones, a cut bank, a rotten floor, a cart on a rut (Mechanics). A rich place (a foundry, a ship's deck, a mill) has two or three, and studying it again finds the next. Philosophers stand in doorways a minute longer than anyone else, looking up; it's how you can spot one.

**Reach.** A feature reaches 30 feet from itself unless the DM names more, and it affects only creatures within that distance of it. A big feature (a dam, a powder store, a millrace, a mine full of firedamp) can reach farther, and the DM says how far when you find it.

You can use this feature five times, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

| Law | The feature | Save | Damage | On a failed save |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mechanics | A load, a slope, a hanging weight | Dexterity | Bludgeoning | Restrained (pinned) until the end of its next turn. The area becomes Difficult Terrain (rubble). |
| Heat | A fire, a furnace, powder, a sealed vessel | Dexterity | Fire | Pushed 10 feet away from the feature, and has Disadvantage on attack rolls until the end of its next turn, scorched and dazzled. Flammable objects in the area catch fire. |
| Pneumatics | Gas, smoke, foul air | Constitution | Poison | Poisoned until the end of its next turn. The area is Heavily Obscured until the end of your next turn. |
| Hydrostatics | Water held back: a sluice, a cistern, a dam | Strength | Bludgeoning | Pushed 10 feet away from the feature and Prone. The area becomes Difficult Terrain for 1 minute. |
| Optics | Strong light, and a lens, mirror, or glass that's part of the place | Constitution | Radiant | Blinded until the end of its next turn. |

Outside a fight, the same knowledge springs a trap from a safe distance, opens a sluice gate to flood a cellar, or brings down a wall where you want it to fall.

> **Features by Place**
>
> For the DM: what a study of the place can turn up. Name the first one that fits; a second study names the next.
>
> | Place | Features (laws) |
> |---|---|
> | Tavern, hall, or palace room | A chandelier or a roof beam (Mechanics); the hearth, lamp oil, or spirits (Heat); a tall window at noon (Optics) |
> | Street, square, or market | Scaffolding, a hanging sign, barrels stacked on a slope (Mechanics); a forge or cookfires (Heat); a fountain, a well, or a canal lock (Hydrostatics) |
> | Ship's deck | A boom, a yard, cargo in the hoist (Mechanics); the powder room or the galley fire (Heat); the sea through a gunport (Hydrostatics) |
> | Temple, church, or mosque | A bell, a gallery, scaffolding (Mechanics); candles, lamps, or censers (Heat); colored glass or a mirror in the sun (Optics) |
> | Mine, cellar, or sewer | Pit props, ore buckets (Mechanics); firedamp or foul air (Pneumatics); sump water (Hydrostatics) |
> | Workshop, foundry, or mill | A crane, a millwheel (Mechanics); the furnace or crucible (Heat); fumes (Pneumatics); the millrace (Hydrostatics) |
> | Forest or hillside | A dead tree, a scree slope, a balanced boulder (Mechanics); a swollen stream or a dam (Hydrostatics); a charcoal burner's mound (Heat or Pneumatics) |
> | Marsh, paddy, or riverbank | A dike or a sluice (Hydrostatics); marsh gas (Pneumatics); a cut bank (Mechanics) |
> | Open road or field | The ground itself: a ditch, loose stones, a cart on a rut (Mechanics); sometimes a hayrick (Heat) or a steep bank (Mechanics). The Experimentalist brings its own. |

features.name: Natural Philosopher Subclass
features.text: You gain a Natural Philosopher subclass of your choice: the Ballistician, the Crowner, the Experimentalist, the Naturalist, or the Navigator. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Natural Philosopher levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Natural Philosopher level or lower.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Natural Philosopher levels 8, 12, and 16.

features.name: Out of the Line
features.text: You worked out the line of the blow before it was thrown. When a creature you can see hits you with an attack roll while you aren't wearing Medium or Heavy armor, you can take a Reaction to halve the attack's damage against you (round down).

features.name: Leverage
features.text: Give me a lever long enough. When you Shove a creature, you can use your Intelligence modifier instead of your Strength modifier for the saving throw's DC. Once per round, when you or an ally you can see pushes a creature, the creature moves 10 feet farther. With a lever, a rope, or a pulley, you can lift, drag, or brace as if you were two sizes larger: raise a portcullis, tip a loaded cart into the street, swing a boom across a deck, or hold a door that four guards are leaning on.

features.name: Correspondence
features.text: You belong to the Republic of Letters. You can write to the learned world with one question about history, nature, a place, a creature, or an object. An answer arrives by letter in 1d6 days if anyone in your correspondence within reach of a regular post knows it (a letter between Leiden and London takes three or four days); what they know is what the best book on the subject says, plus whatever they have seen for themselves. If only someone farther off knows it, the answer comes at the speed of the post: weeks from Istanbul, months from Goa or Beijing. If no one does, a letter says so. The answer is what the learned world knows, which can be wrong. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again for 7 days.

features.name: Conservation
features.text: Nothing a blow spends is lost. Once per turn, when your attack or a feature of this class reduces a creature to 0 Hit Points, roll your Calculated Shot dice: another creature of your choice within 5 feet of it takes that much damage, of the same type (no action required).

features.name: Experimentum Crucis
features.text: You design the experiment that settles it. You spend 1 hour testing a hypothesis about a creature, object, place, or phenomenon you have studied, and then ask the DM up to three questions that can be answered yes or no. The DM answers each truthfully. A question the DM can't answer from what the experiment could reveal gets "unclear," and still counts. You and your companions settle the questions together, and a companion who helped with the experiment can ask one of them. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Explosion
features.text: You bring the reaction with you. As a Utilize action, you set off an explosion centered on a point you can see within 60 feet of yourself; it needs no feature you're studying. Each creature of your choice in a 20-foot-radius Sphere centered on that point makes a Dexterity saving throw against your Mechanism's save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes Fire damage of twice the Mechanism column's dice in the Natural Philosopher Features table (12d8) and is pushed 10 feet straight away from the center. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only. Flammable objects in the area that aren't being worn or carried catch fire. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Eureka!
features.text: The answer arrives all at once. After 1 minute with a problem (a lock, a machine, a puzzle, a creature's weakness), you can ask the DM for the one thing you're missing, and the DM tells you. The answer is something that can be seen, measured, or tested; it's never what a creature thinks, feels, or intends. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Skeptic
features.text: You've learned to doubt your own eyes. You have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Charmed condition, and on checks and saving throws to discern or disbelieve an illusion.

features.name: Epic Boon
features.text: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Fate is recommended.

features.name: The System of the World
features.text:
You see the whole of it. You're studying every creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself, and each of your attack rolls with a crossbow or a firearm against them has Advantage, as if you had Aimed. Calculated Shot and your subclass's features work against any of them. You still learn a fact only from a creature you study with your Bonus Action. When you finish a Short Rest, you regain one expended use of Mechanism.

> **Running a Natural Philosopher**
>
> This class asks the DM for true answers more often than any other: Study, First Causes, Correspondence, Experimentum Crucis, Eureka!, and most of the subclasses' features. Three rules carry nearly all of it.
>
> - **Answer with facts, not conclusions.** "The ash is from oak, and the fire was laid this morning" is a fact; "the innkeeper did it" is a conclusion. The class learns the what and leaves the who and the why for play. None of its features tells what a creature thinks, feels, or intends.
> - **One or two sentences.** A lead, not the solution.
> - **When you don't know, say "not enough to examine."** The use isn't spent, and the player looks somewhere else.
>
> Settle the place when it's studied, not when it's used. When the Philosopher studies a room, name the feature, its laws, and its reach then (Features by Place has a list), so that setting it off later waits on nothing. When the class's work earns money (a Master Gunner's wage, a Cabinet's specimens), use the defaults in the text and adjust to the place. And the features that hand you a story are yours to pull on: a letter answered, a patron impressed by the fireworks, a name made in the learned world.

features.name: Trajectory
features.text: Your attacks with crossbows and firearms ignore Half Cover and Three-Quarters Cover, and attacking at long range doesn't impose Disadvantage on them. In addition, from a hole, a wound, or a spent ball or bolt, you can work out where a shot came from, roughly how far away, and what kind of weapon fired it.

features.name: Gunnery
features.text: You are proficient with siege equipment such as ballistae, cannons, and mangonels; use the siege equipment in the *Dungeon Master's Guide* (*The Setting*'s Arms and Armies covers what a siege is like in 1668). When you aim one, it uses your Intelligence modifier for its attack rolls, and its attacks ignore Half Cover and Three-Quarters Cover.

features.name: Master Gunner
features.text: You can judge a gun by looking it over: its caliber, the weight of shot and the charge of powder it takes, its range, and whether it has been overloaded, cracked, or badly cast and is likely to burst. Given 10 minutes to look at a wall, a gate, or an earthwork, you know roughly how long it would stand against the guns you can see or name, and where a battery would have to stand to breach it. Garrisons, armies, merchant ships, and foundries everywhere want master gunners: wherever there are guns, you can find paid work as one, at a wage the DM sets (a skilled hireling's 2 GP a day is a fair start, more in a siege), and people who work with guns treat you as one of them.

features.name: Disabling Shot
features.text: When you hit a creature you're studying with an attack using a crossbow or a firearm, you can place the shot instead of taking your Calculated Shot's extra damage. Choose one: the creature has Disadvantage on attack rolls until the start of your next turn; its Speed is 0 until the start of your next turn; or it drops one object it's holding. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Fireworks
features.text: Given a day, your tools, and black powder and salts worth 25 GP, you can make a fireworks display that lasts about 10 minutes and can be seen for miles on a clear night: rockets, wheels, fountains, colored fire. A display at a feast, a wedding, or a ruler's birthday gets you noticed by whoever paid for the feast. You can also make up to six signal rockets as part of the same work; each, fired as a Utilize action, bursts in a color and pattern you chose when you made it, so that anyone who knows your code can read it.

features.name: Through and Through
features.text: Once per turn, when you hit a creature you're studying with a crossbow or a firearm, the shot can pass through: one creature within 5 feet directly behind the target, in a line from you, takes damage equal to a roll of the weapon's damage dice (not doubled), of the weapon's type, without your Calculated Shot. Ballisticians have been seen sprinting the length of a gallery to line two of them up.

features.name: The Perfect Parabola
features.text: Your attacks with crossbows and firearms against a creature you're studying score a Critical Hit on a roll of 19 or 20 on the d20.

features.name: Reconstruction
features.text: You gain Expertise in the Investigation skill, gaining proficiency in it first if you lack it; if you already have Expertise in it, you gain Expertise in another skill you're proficient in. In addition, you can spend 10 minutes studying a place where something happened in the last 24 hours. The DM tells you what happened there in broad strokes: how many creatures took part, what they did, roughly when, and which way they left.

features.name: The View
features.text: Given 10 minutes with a body, you learn how long it has been dead (to within an hour if it died in the last day, and to within a few days after that), what killed it, whether it was moved after death, whether it was alive when it went into the water or the fire, and what made the wounds: the kind of blade, shot, or blow, and from which side. You learn nothing about who did it, beyond what the wounds alone can say.

features.name: Find the Flaw
features.text: When you study a creature, you can also find its flaw. Choose one of the following, which lasts as long as you're studying it: its Armor Class decreases by 1, or it loses one Resistance of your choice (you learn which Resistances it has). Studying it again lets you choose again; the flaws don't stack.

features.name: What It Is
features.text: You can spend 1 minute studying an object to learn what it is: whether it is cursed and what the curse does, a magic item's properties and how to use them, or what poison or potion it holds. In addition, when you study a creature or object that is an illusion, you learn that it is one. When you study a creature for 1 minute outside combat, you also learn whether it is disguised or shapechanged; you don't learn who or what it really is. A Bonus Action's study in a fight tells you only that something about the creature's appearance is false. Study doesn't reveal that a creature is under another's control. The DM describes any outward signs (a fixed stare, a pause before each answer), and the conclusion is yours to draw.

features.name: Standing
features.text: When you lay your findings about a death or a crime before anyone with the power to act on them (a county bench, a magistrate, a kadi's court, a village's elders, a ship's captain), they take you seriously: they hear you out, and they don't dismiss what you show them without a reason, though they may still decide against you. If you hold the office of coroner in England, or its like elsewhere, you also have the office's rights: to view any body in your jurisdiction before it is buried, to summon a jury and witnesses, and to commit the accused for trial.

features.name: Nothing Is Immune
features.text: The extra damage from your Calculated Shot ignores Resistance, and a creature with Immunity to that damage type has Resistance to it instead (the extra damage doesn't ignore that Resistance).

features.name: Inquest
features.text: When a creature tells you about an event you have used Reconstruction on, you know whether its account contradicts the evidence, and which part. You learn nothing about why; an honest witness can be wrong, and a liar can tell the truth.

features.name: Case Closed
features.text:
**Naming a suspect.** After you use Reconstruction on a scene, you can name one creature as someone who took part in it. After you use What It Is on an object, you can name one creature as someone who made or carried it. Tell the DM the name, or a description that picks out one creature ("the man with the burned hand"). You can name one suspect for each scene or object, and your namings last until you finish a Long Rest.

**Meeting them.** When you roll Initiative and can see a creature you named, the DM tells you whether you were right about it. If you were, you have Advantage on the Initiative roll, and you begin the fight studying that creature.

**Exposing the flaw.** When a creature you're studying uses Legendary Resistance, you can take a Reaction to expose the flaw. The creature must expend one additional use of Legendary Resistance; if it can't, it fails the saving throw instead. Once you use this Reaction, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Apparatus
features.text: You gain proficiency with Alchemist's Supplies and Glassblower's Tools; if you already have either, choose another tool from the Natural Philosopher's tool list.

features.name: Experiments
features.text:
When you finish a Long Rest, you can spend 1 hour of it with your Alchemist's Supplies and Glassblower's Tools to prepare two experiments (two at every level; what grows is their damage, which follows the Mechanism column): charged globes, sealed vessels, primed jars, each one a set of reagents kept apart until the moment you mix them. An experiment lasts until you finish your next Long Rest, and it works only in your hands. You can't prepare experiments without your tools.

As a Utilize action, you release an experiment at a point you can see within 60 feet of yourself, choosing as you mix it one of the five energies in the table below: Fire, Lightning, Thunder, Cold, or Acid. It needs no feature you're studying. Each creature of your choice in a 20-foot Cube whose point of origin is that point (for Lightning, a Line 60 feet long and 5 feet wide from you) makes a saving throw against your Mechanism's save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes damage of one die fewer than the Mechanism column of the Natural Philosopher Features table (minimum 2d8, so 2d8 at level 3 and 5d8 from level 13) and suffers the energy's effect. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only.

| Energy | Save | Damage | On a failed save |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fire | Dexterity | Fire | Flammable objects in the area that aren't being worn or carried catch fire. |
| Lightning | Dexterity | Lightning | It can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn. A creature wearing metal armor has Disadvantage on the save. |
| Thunder | Constitution | Thunder | Pushed 10 feet away from the Cube's point of origin, and Deafened until the end of its next turn. The blast can be heard 300 feet away. |
| Cold | Constitution | Cold | Its Speed is halved until the end of its next turn. |
| Acid | Dexterity | Acid | Its Armor Class decreases by 1 until it finishes a Long Rest: armor, shell, or hide eaten away. This doesn't stack. |

features.name: Volatile
features.text: When you release an experiment, roll a d6. On a 1, it goes off badly: it still works, and you also take half the damage rolled (no saving throw).

features.name: Demonstration
features.text: Given 1 hour to set up and an audience, you can stage a demonstration: sparks drawn from a rubbed globe, a bell falling silent in a jar emptied of air, frost drawn onto a glass on a summer afternoon, a color that blooms when two clear liquids meet. It's harmless and it isn't magic, and anyone who watches it knows both. For the next 24 hours, you have Advantage on Charisma checks to impress, persuade, or raise money from anyone who watched it to the end.

features.name: Overproof
features.text: When you release an experiment, you can release it overproof: it deals two more dice of damage, and Volatile goes off badly on a 1 or 2.

features.name: Touchstone
features.text: With your Alchemist's Supplies and 10 minutes, you can tell what a metal, an alloy, a salt, or an acid is, and how pure it is: whether a coin is clipped or debased, whether gold has been adulterated and with what, and whether a powder is what its seller says it is. You can tell platina from silver, which almost no one outside Mutapa can yet do reliably, and you know what that knowledge is worth to the people who'd pay for it.

features.name: Insulation
features.text: You have Resistance to the damage of your own experiments.

features.name: Freezing Mixture
features.text: With your Alchemist's Supplies, a supply of saltpeter, and 10 minutes, you can chill water, wine, or a room well below a cellar's cool, and given snow or ice to start from, you can freeze water solid. Kept cold this way, food or remains don't spoil for 1 week, as long as you renew the mixture each day.

features.name: Chain Reaction
features.text: When you release an experiment, you can release a second one as part of the same action, at a point you can see within 60 feet of you. Roll Volatile for each. With two experiments a day, that's the whole day's work in one breath, and the room remembers it.

features.name: Natural History
