features.text: You gain Expertise in the Nature or Medicine skill, gaining proficiency in it first if you lack it, and you gain proficiency with the Herbalism Kit (if you already have it, choose another tool). When you study a creature, you also learn its habitat and what it eats, and the DM tells you one thing from its stat block: your choice of its hardest-hitting attack, an ability with limited uses or a Recharge, or a trait. Instead, you can ask what its kind fears or is drawn to (fire, a scent, its young), and the DM tells you that. From a track, a nest, spoor, or a carcass, you can tell what made it and roughly when.

features.name: Bread or Poison
features.text: You can spend 1 minute examining a plant, a fungus, a fruit, meat, or water to learn whether it's safe to eat or drink and, if it isn't, what it would do to whoever did. You also know how to find food and clean water in a land whose plants and animals you have studied for at least a day, and you know which of its people's foods you've never seen are worth asking about. This catches food of the Hidden Realm too: measurement doesn't care what made a thing.

features.name: Know Its Nature
features.text: A creature you're studying has Disadvantage on its saving throw against your Mechanism (Explosion isn't your Mechanism).

features.name: Specimen
features.text: When you finish a Short or Long Rest after a creature you have studied has died, you can spend 1 hour with its remains and your Herbalism Kit or Alchemist's Supplies to prepare a remedy. As a Bonus Action, a creature can drink the remedy or administer it to another creature within 5 feet. A creature that drinks it ends one poison or disease that kind of creature caused, or for 8 hours has Resistance to that kind of creature's Poison damage and Advantage on saving throws against its poisons and diseases. You can have one remedy at a time; it spoils when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Cabinet
features.text: You can preserve the remains of a creature you have studied (a skin, a skeleton, a pressed plant, something in a jar of spirits) with 1 hour of work and your Herbalism Kit or Alchemist's Supplies, and it keeps indefinitely. You can tell a real specimen from a fake one at a glance, and you know roughly what a collector would pay for one; a well-made specimen sells for about 50 GP times the creature's Challenge Rating (minimum 10 GP), and one of a creature no one has described can be worth many times that (ten times, unless the DM sets another price), and earns you a name in the learned world.

features.name: Field Survey
features.text: You can spend 1 hour watching and walking an area to learn what lives within 1 mile of you: each kind of creature, roughly how many, where they den, and which of them are hunting.

features.name: Know What It Does
features.text: When a creature you're studying forces you or an ally within 30 feet of you to make a saving throw, you can take a Reaction to give the saving throw Advantage. You can use this Reaction a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Plotted Course
features.text: You gain proficiency with Navigator's Tools; if you already have it, choose another tool. You and your companions can't become lost except by magic, you always know which way is north, and your group can travel at a fast pace without the usual Disadvantage on Wisdom (Perception or Survival) checks. This works on every plane.

features.name: Taking the Fix
features.text: With your Navigator's Tools and a clear sky, you can spend 10 minutes to fix your latitude to within a few miles, and the local time to within a minute; on land, with a telescope and a clear night, you can fix your longitude too. Given an hour and a day's travel, you can draw a chart of the way you came that someone else can follow, and you can read anyone's chart, whatever its language or its conventions, and tell how far to trust it.

features.name: Course Correction
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, you can call out a path. A number of allies up to your Proficiency Bonus who are within 30 feet of yourself and can see or hear you can each take a Reaction to move up to half their Speed. This movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.

Course Correction and Reading the Currents draw on one supply: you can use them a combined number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Reading the Currents
features.text: When a creature you can see hits an ally within 30 feet of you with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to halve the attack's damage against that ally (round down).

features.name: Safe Passage
features.text: When a creature within 30 feet of you makes a Dexterity saving throw against an effect you can see, you can take a Reaction, after it rolls but before you know whether it succeeds, to add your Intelligence modifier (minimum of +1) to the save.

features.name: Drift
features.text: Your Speed increases by 10 feet, and Difficult Terrain costs you no extra movement.

features.name: Weather Eye
features.text: You can predict the weather where you are for the next 24 hours, and when a storm, a fog, or a change of wind is coming within that time. Near the sea, you also know the times of the tides, and on a monsoon coast, whether the season is about to turn.

features.name: Through the Gap
features.text: When you use Course Correction, you can also move up to your Speed, and you and each ally who moves can move through the spaces of hostile creatures. Your own move provokes Opportunity Attacks as usual; your allies' movement still doesn't, even through hostile creatures' spaces. A creature can't end its move in another creature's space.

features.name: Pilot
features.text: You can bring a ship safely into any harbor or through any strait you can see, even one you've never entered, given an hour to watch the water first. Ships' masters everywhere need pilots: on any ship bound your way, you can work your passage as navigator or pilot, and the master gives you and up to five companions passage and food for the voyage in return.

features.name: The Path of Least Action
features.text: Overland travel with you takes half as long. In addition, once per Long Rest, when you use Reading the Currents, the ally can also move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks; if it ends this move out of the attacker's reach (for a melee attack) or out of its line of sight (for a ranged attack), the attack misses instead of being halved.

multiclass.gains: Hit Point Die, proficiency with one tool of your choice from the Natural Philosopher's tool list, and training with Light armor
multiclass.text: You must have an Intelligence score of 13 or higher. Gain the following traits from the Core Natural Philosopher Traits table: Hit Point Die, proficiency with one tool of your choice from the Natural Philosopher's tool list, and training with Light armor. Gain the Natural Philosopher's level 1 features, which are listed in the Natural Philosopher Features table.

data.name: Physician
data.blurb: Int full caster. The arcane healer.

traits.value: Medicine, plus *choose 2:* Arcana, History, Insight, Investigation, Nature, Perception, Persuasion, or Sleight of Hand
*Choose A or B:* (A) Leather Armor, Light Crossbow and 20 Bolts, Dagger, Healer's Kit, Spellbook, Arcane Focus (crystal), Scholar's Pack, and 7 GP; or (B) 100 GP

rows.Class Features: Spellcasting, Physician's Eye, Healing Prowess, Diagnosis

features.name: Spellcasting
features.text:
See the rules on spellcasting for how spells work. The information below details how you use those rules with Physician spells, which appear in the Physician spell list later in the class's description.

**Cantrips.** You know three Physician cantrips of your choice. Whenever you gain a Physician level, you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Physician cantrip of your choice. When you reach Physician levels 4 and 10, you learn another Physician cantrip of your choice, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Physician Features table.

**Spellbook.** Your spellbook is a casebook as much as a grimoire: the spells you have learned, and the notes on what they did. It contains six level 1 Physician spells of your choice to start. If you also have Wizard levels, your Physician and Wizard spells can share one spellbook; each class prepares only its own spells.

**Spell Slots.** The Physician Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

**Prepared Spells of Level 1+.** You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To do so, choose a number of spells from your spellbook equal to the number in the Prepared Spells column of the Physician Features table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

If another Physician feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Physician spells for you.

**Changing Your Prepared Spells.** Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of the spells there with spells from your spellbook.

**Spellcasting Ability.** Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Physician spells.

**Spellcasting Focus.** You can use an Arcane Focus or your spellbook as a Spellcasting Focus for your Physician spells.

**Ritual Adept.** You can cast any Physician spell as a Ritual if that spell has the Ritual tag and the spell is in your spellbook. You needn't have the spell prepared, but you must read from the book to cast a spell in this way.

**Undead.** If one of your Physician spells would make a creature it kills rise as Undead (as *Finger of Death* does), it doesn't rise; its body is destroyed instead.

**Expanding Your Spellbook.** Each time you gain a Physician level after 1, you can add two Physician spells of your choice to your spellbook for free. Each of these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. On your adventures, you might find other spells that you can add to your spellbook (see the "Your Spellbook" sidebar).

> **Your Spellbook**
>
> The spells you add as you gain levels represent your own research. You can also find spells on your adventures: on a scroll, in another caster's spellbook, or in a temple's records. **You can copy any spell that appears on the Physician spell list into your spellbook, whichever class the scroll or book was written for.** For each level of the spell, copying it into your book takes 2 hours and costs 50 GP. Copying a spell out of your book into another takes 1 hour and costs 10 GP per spell level.

features.name: Physician's Eye
features.text: You use Intelligence instead of Wisdom when you make a Wisdom (Medicine) check, and you have Expertise in the Medicine skill.

features.name: Healing Prowess
features.text:
You have one **Prowess Die**, two from Physician level 2, and four from level 5, as shown in the Prowess Dice column of the Physician Features table. A Prowess Die is a d6. It becomes a d8 at Physician level 5, a d10 at level 11, and a d12 at level 17.

As a Bonus Action, you can touch yourself or another creature and expend one Prowess Die. That creature regains a number of Hit Points equal to the number rolled plus your Intelligence modifier.

However you use it, you can use Healing Prowess only once on each of your turns. Several subclasses give Healing Prowess new ways to travel (on an arrow, a cloud, a blade); each of those is still your one use for the turn. A feature that only expends a Prowess Die, without saying it uses Healing Prowess, isn't a use of it.

You regain all expended Prowess Dice when you finish a Long Rest, and half your maximum, rounded down (one from level 2, two from level 5), when you finish a Short Rest.

features.name: Diagnosis
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself (you can choose yourself: you count as willing).

If the creature is willing, or is an ally that can't refuse (it has the Incapacitated condition or 0 Hit Points), you diagnose it automatically. You learn its current Hit Points and Hit Point maximum, every condition affecting it, whether it is diseased, has the Poisoned condition, or is under a curse, and the ability in which it has the lowest saving throw bonus.

Otherwise, make an Intelligence (Medicine) check. The DC equals 10 plus half the creature's Challenge Rating (round down), or 10 plus half its level if it has no Challenge Rating. On a success, you learn the following:

- Whether the creature is **unharmed**, **injured** (below its Hit Point maximum), **Bloodied** (at or below half its Hit Point maximum), or **near death** (at or below a quarter); you learn the most severe that applies.
- Every condition affecting it, and whether it is diseased, has the Poisoned condition, or is under a curse.
- Whether it has Resistance, Immunity, or Vulnerability to Necrotic or Poison damage, and whether it has Immunity to disease.
- The ability in which it has the lowest saving throw bonus.

A creature's saving throw bonus for an ability is the one its stat block lists, or its ability modifier if the stat block lists none. If two or more abilities tie for the lowest, the DM names either.

On a failure, you learn nothing, and you can't attempt to diagnose that creature again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

A creature you diagnose, automatically or with a successful check, is your **patient** until you finish a Long Rest. You can have any number of patients. When you restore Hit Points to a patient with a Physician feature or a Physician spell, you can reroll any 1s on the healing dice. You must use the new rolls.

> **Doing Rounds**
>
> Most Physicians diagnose the party over breakfast: it's free on the willing, and it makes everyone a patient for the day. In a fight, that leaves Diagnosis for the enemy, and the answer is for the whole table. Say it out loud: "It's Bloodied, and its worst save is Wisdom."
>
> **For the DM.** Diagnosis is a reveal. When you prepare a fight, note each creature's lowest save beside its stat block, so you can answer at once, and answer in terms of the body: a shaking hand, a shallow breath, eyes that won't settle.

features.name: Treatment
features.text:
As a Utilize action, you can expend one use of a Healer's Kit and make an Intelligence (Medicine) check to treat your patient, who must be within your reach. The DC depends on what you are treating:

| Treatment | DC |
|---|---|
| End the Poisoned condition | No check, unless an effect with a save DC imposed it |
| End the Blinded or Deafened condition (if not permanent) | 12 |
| Cure one disease | 13 |
| End the Paralyzed condition | 15 |
| Remove one level of Exhaustion (once per creature per Long Rest) | 15 |

If a spell or other effect with a save DC imposed the condition, the DC is that save DC instead whenever it's higher (for the Poisoned condition, it always is). A disease you cure with Treatment is beaten the slow way, and the creature can't catch that disease again. Natural diseases and their course are in *The Setting* (Running Euphonia, Disease).

On a success, the chosen effect ends; if a spell or other ongoing effect imposed the condition, that effect ends on the creature. Either way, the use of the Healer's Kit is spent, and you can't attempt the same treatment on that creature again until it finishes a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Physician Subclass
features.text:
You gain a Physician subclass of your choice, the specialty that shapes your practice: Chirurgeon, Combat Medic, Doctor, Hedge Witch, Immortalist, Neurologist, Plague Doctor, Surgeon, or Vitalist, each detailed after this class's description. *Chirurgeon* is the older form of *surgeon*: Lanternhall gives the old word to the saw and the new one to the hovering scalpel, and the two schools don't get along. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Physician level or lower.

Every specialty uses the same Prowess Die. What changes is how it reaches its target (the last column says how much each specialty asks of a new player):

| Specialty | How your Prowess Die travels | To learn |
|---|---|---|
| Chirurgeon | Into you, on a hit with your Saw | Light |
| Combat Medic | On an arrow, or in place of one | Moderate |
| Doctor | Down a chain of linked allies | Moderate |
| Hedge Witch | Ripped out of an enemy, into a friend | Moderate |
| Immortalist | Riding a spell of your own energy | Heavy |
| Neurologist | Along the nerves, 30 feet | Moderate |
| Plague Doctor | On a cloud | Moderate |
| Surgeon | Through your instrument, hovering where you send it | Light |
| Vitalist | By touch, then through the pulse of everything alive | Light |

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Physician levels 8, 12, and 16.

features.name: To the Wounded
features.text: On your turn, while you are moving toward a creature that isn't Hostile to you and is Bloodied or has 0 Hit Points (each foot of the move bringing you closer to it), your Speed increases by 10 feet, and your movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.

features.name: Bedside Manner
features.text: If you are conscious and within 30 feet of a creature when it spends Hit Point Dice during a Short Rest, that creature adds your Intelligence modifier to each Hit Point Die it spends during that rest. A creature can't benefit from more than one Physician's Bedside Manner during the same rest.

features.name: Vitals
features.text:
When you use Healing Prowess, you can use Diagnosis on a different creature as part of the same Bonus Action, or as part of the same attack if a feature lets you use Healing Prowess without spending a Bonus Action.

You also have Advantage on saving throws against disease and against the Poisoned condition.

features.name: Last Words
features.text: When you see a creature that has 0 Hit Points, or one dying of a wound, a poison, or a disease, you know how long it has left, to within a minute or a day. As a Utilize action, you can touch a dying creature and hold it at the edge: for 1 minute, it's conscious and can speak, though it can't move or take actions, and it makes no Death Saving Throws (damage still causes failures). The hold ends early if the creature regains Hit Points. When the minute ends, it is as it was. Once you hold a creature this way, you can't hold it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Constitution of Iron
features.text: You have Immunity to disease and to the Poisoned condition, and you have Advantage on saving throws against the Frightened condition.

features.name: Resuscitation
features.text: When you restore Hit Points to a creature that has 0 Hit Points, it regains additional Hit Points equal to your Physician level, and the next time it stands up from Prone before the end of its next turn, it spends none of its movement.

features.name: The Whole Ward
features.text: You always have the *Mass Heal* spell prepared, and it counts as a Physician spell for you. When you cast it, each creature it heals also loses one level of Exhaustion.

features.name: Standing Orders
features.text: Once on each of your turns, when you take the Magic action to cast a Physician spell of level 1 or higher, you can expend one Prowess Die. One creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself regains Hit Points equal to the number rolled plus your Intelligence modifier. This isn't a use of Healing Prowess, and it leaves your Bonus Action free.

features.name: Epic Boon
features.text: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Spell Recall is recommended.

features.name: Attending Physician
features.text:
When you roll Initiative, you regain one expended Prowess Die.

In addition, when a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself would die (by failing its third Death Saving Throw, by taking damage that reduces it to 0 Hit Points with remaining damage equal to or exceeding its Hit Point maximum, or by an effect that kills it outright), you can take a Reaction to prevent its death. The creature instead drops to 0 Hit Points and is Stable, and it then regains Hit Points equal to one roll of your Prowess Die plus your Intelligence modifier (no die is expended). Once you use this Reaction, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

> **Running a Physician**
>
> **Timing.** Every affliction a Physician's class features lay on a creature ends at the end of a turn (usually the creature's next one) or on a saving throw it makes at the end of each of its turns, or when its duration or your Concentration ends. None ends at the start of a turn.
>
> **The drop.** A party with a Physician gets back up. Every specialty has a way to put a fallen ally straight back on their feet, several can stop the drop outright once per Long Rest from 14th level, from 17th the Physician can bring a whole fallen party back at once with *Mass Heal*, and at 20th it can stop a death. Hit as hard as the fight deserves, and let the rescue be the moment the table remembers.

subclasses.name: Chirurgeon
subclasses.lead: A Chirurgeon heals with a saw in hand. You fight in the front rank, mend yourself on every cut you land, take the limb that would kill its owner, and fit the peg or the hook afterward. Every army, every navy, and every port has someone who does this work.

features.name: Theatre Training
features.text:
Your instrument is a Saw. You gain training with Medium armor and Shields, and proficiency with the following Martial weapons: the Battleaxe, Glaive, Greataxe, Greatsword, Halberd, Longsword, and Scimitar. The Saw is any of those weapons, or a Handaxe or Sickle, and you can use it as a Spellcasting Focus for your Physician spells. You can use your Intelligence modifier instead of your Strength modifier for the attack and damage rolls you make with your Saw. The Saw comes with Weapon Mastery: you can use the mastery properties of two kinds of Slashing weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, and whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kinds you chose.

**The Barber's Chair.** You can shave, cut hair, draw a tooth, let blood, and set a simple break. In any town, camp, or ship, you can set up a chair for an afternoon and earn a modest living, and a soldier, sailor, or laborer who has sat in your chair will point you to a bed, a meal, or the person you're looking for. By evening you've heard what the men and women in the chair were saying: the DM tells you one thing the place is talking about that it isn't telling strangers.

features.name: Under the Knife
features.text: When you hit a creature with your Saw in melee, you can use Healing Prowess on yourself as part of the same attack, without spending a Bonus Action: expend one Prowess Die and regain Hit Points equal to the number rolled (you don't add your Intelligence modifier). The work is on you as much as on them. When you do, if the creature you hit is Large or smaller, you can push it up to 10 feet away from you, and you can move with it, up to the same distance, to stay beside it. Moving with it costs none of your movement and doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.

features.name: Amputation
features.text:
You can cripple a limb in a fight, or take one on a table for a patient.

*In a fight.* When you hit a creature with your Saw in melee, you can expend one Prowess Die to cripple a limb instead of using Under the Knife; you can't do both on the same turn. The creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or have the limb you chose crippled. On a Critical Hit, it fails automatically. If you cripple an arm, the creature drops whatever it was holding in that hand and has Disadvantage on the first attack roll it makes on each of its turns; if you cripple a leg, it has the Prone condition, and its Speed is halved. The arm's effects and the halved Speed last for 1 minute; the creature repeats the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending them on a success. (It can stand up from Prone as normal.) Only a limb taken on a table is gone for good. A creature that has Immunity to Slashing damage, or that has no such limb, is unaffected. Once a creature fails this saving throw, you can't cripple a limb in a fight again, on any creature, until you finish a Short or Long Rest; on a successful save the Prowess Die is still expended.

*On a table.* Outside combat, you can spend 1 minute removing a limb from a creature within your reach that is willing, or that has the Incapacitated condition and isn't Hostile to you. No check is required. One disease, poison, curse, or other ongoing effect confined to that limb ends; whether an effect is so confined is the DM's judgment (usually, one that entered through that limb, such as a bite or a wound). The creature takes 2d10 Slashing damage that can't be reduced or prevented, gains one level of Exhaustion, and loses the limb until it is restored by *Regenerate* or comparable magic. A creature that has lost an arm can hold only one object at a time and can't wield a two-handed weapon, or a Shield and a weapon at once. A creature that has lost a leg has its Speed halved and needs a cane or crutch to move unless it has a prosthetic leg; it falls Prone after it takes the Dash action, and it has Disadvantage on Dexterity checks made to keep its balance.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.text: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Pegs and Hooks
features.text:
You make what you take. You gain proficiency with your choice of Tinker's Tools or Woodcarver's Tools. During a Long Rest, using those tools, you can fit a prosthetic limb to a creature that has lost one.

- **A prosthetic arm** grips and holds. The creature can hold two objects again, including a Shield and a weapon at once, though it still can't wield a two-handed weapon.
- **A prosthetic leg** carries weight. The creature's Speed is no longer halved for the lost leg, it no longer needs a cane or crutch, and it no longer falls Prone after it takes the Dash action.

You keep a watch on your patients. While you're within 1 mile of a creature whose limb you've taken on a table or that you've fitted with a prosthetic, you know if it has a disease or the Poisoned condition, and you know when its wound has turned.

features.name: Field Hospital
features.text:
You learn to pitch a field hospital: a ward of cots and kettles that heals whoever is laid in it. As a Magic action, you expend a spell slot of level 3 or higher and pitch it. It is a 30-foot Emanation centered on you that lasts for 1 minute, and you must maintain Concentration on it as if on a spell. Until it ends, you can take a Bonus Action on each of your turns to restore 2d6 Hit Points to one creature in it, plus 1d6 for each slot level above 3.

Once per Long Rest, you can pitch the full field hospital without expending a spell slot, as if with a level 3 slot. The full hospital's radius increases by 10 feet, a creature that regains Hit Points from it regains additional Hit Points equal to your Intelligence modifier (once per turn), and while you concentrate on it you can use Healing Prowess on any creature in it, rather than only a creature you touch. A chirurgeon pitches one full tent a day.

Your other Physician spells with a range of Self that create an Emanation or other area centered on you (such as *Aura of Life* or *Antilife Shell*) get the same treatment: the area's radius increases by 10 feet, and a creature that regains Hit Points from one you are concentrating on regains additional Hit Points equal to your Intelligence modifier (once per turn).

features.name: The Bellows
features.text: As a Bonus Action, you can expend one Prowess Die to work the bellows in a 15-foot Cone originating from you. Each willing creature of your choice in the Cone spends one of its Hit Point Dice and regains Hit Points as if it had spent that die at the end of a Short Rest, adding your Intelligence modifier to the roll. A creature that has no Hit Point Dice remaining gains no benefit. A creature that has no Hit Point Dice of its own, as most monsters don't, instead regains Hit Points equal to one roll of your Prowess Die plus your Intelligence modifier (no die is expended). A creature can't be affected by your Bellows again until it finishes a Long Rest.

features.name: Theatre Closed
features.text:
When a creature within 10 feet of you would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, you can take a Reaction to declare the theater closed. Until the start of your next turn, each creature within 10 feet of you that you choose when you take the Reaction, including the triggering creature, can't be reduced below 1 Hit Point. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

> **Playing a Chirurgeon**
>
> You stand in the front rank, and every cut your Saw lands can mend you and drive the enemy back. Out of a fight, you take the limb that's killing its owner, fit the peg or hook afterward, and know when the wound turns.

subclasses.name: Combat Medic
subclasses.lead: The Combat Medic goes where the wounded are: the breach, the boarding party, the ambush on the caravan road. You keep the Physician's full spellcasting and every Prowess Die, and you add armor, Martial weapons, and the habit of sending your medicine by bow or blade. Your arrows and knives can heal your allies or cripple your enemies, and when a friend goes down, your next shot is already in the air.

features.name: Field Training
features.text:
You gain training with Medium armor and Shields, and proficiency with Martial weapons. You can also use any weapon you are proficient with as a Spellcasting Focus for your Physician spells.

**Camp Physic.** When your company makes camp, you can site it: the water drawn upstream, the latrines dug down, the sick kept apart, and the food kept dry. In a camp you've sited, members of your company have Advantage on saving throws against natural diseases they would catch there. You also know how armies live: after watching a camp, a garrison, or a column on the march for a few minutes, you can ask the DM one of the following questions about it, and the DM answers truthfully. How well fed is it, and how long will its food last? How sick is it, and with what? How close to mutiny is it, and over what?

**Weapon Mastery.** Your training includes Weapon Mastery. You can use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as Longbows and Daggers. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose.

features.name: Arrows of Healing and Plague
features.text:
You can carry your medicine on a projectile. When you take the Attack action and make a ranged attack with a Ranged weapon or a weapon that has the Thrown property, you can expend one Prowess Die to make one of the attacks a **medicated shot**. Only one attack per Attack action can be a medicated shot. When you do so, choose one of the following:

- **Arrow of Healing.** Instead of making an attack roll, the shot automatically hits a creature of your choice that you can see within the weapon's normal range. The creature takes no damage from the shot and regains Hit Points equal to the number rolled on the Prowess Die plus your Intelligence modifier. The shot triggers no effect that happens on a hit, such as a weapon's mastery property.
- **Arrow of Plague.** Make the attack roll as normal. On a hit, the target takes extra Necrotic damage equal to the number rolled on the Prowess Die, and it can't regain Hit Points until the end of its next turn.

The ammunition or thrown weapon is expended as normal. A medicated shot is a use of Healing Prowess, though it doesn't use your Bonus Action.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.text: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Covering Shot
features.text:
When a creature you can see within the normal range of a Ranged or Thrown weapon you are wielding is reduced to 0 Hit Points, you can take a Reaction to make an Arrow of Healing at that creature, expending a Prowess Die and ammunition as normal.

Whenever you restore Hit Points to a creature that has 0 Hit Points, you and that creature each gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus plus your Intelligence modifier.

features.name: Field Pharmacology
features.text:
You can lace your projectiles. When you make an Arrow of Plague, you can expend a second Prowess Die to add one of the following agents. On a hit, the target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or suffer the agent's effect until the end of its next turn. If the target is your patient, it instead makes the saving throw using the ability in which you learned it has the lowest saving throw bonus.

- **Sedative.** The target has the Incapacitated condition. The effect ends early if the target takes damage after the shot that applied it.
- **Blinding Agent.** The target has the Blinded condition.
- **Paralytic.** The target's Speed becomes 0, and it can't take Reactions.

Field Pharmacology brings two more benefits:

- **Multi-Shot.** When you make an Arrow of Healing, you can expend two Prowess Dice instead of one. If you do, the shot heals two creatures of your choice within the weapon's normal range, each regaining Hit Points equal to one of the expended dice, rolled for it, plus your Intelligence modifier.
- **Spreading Draught.** When an Arrow of Plague hits a creature, or an Arrow of Healing restores Hit Points to one, each other creature of your choice within 5 feet of that creature regains Hit Points equal to your Intelligence modifier. (With Multi-Shot, choose one of the two creatures.)

features.name: Stimulant
features.text: As a Bonus Action, you can expend two Prowess Dice to stimulate one creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself. For 1 minute (you must maintain Concentration on it, as if on a spell), the creature has Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage, and once on each of its turns when it hits a creature with an attack roll or damages one with a spell, it can add one roll of your Prowess Die to the damage (no die is expended). Only one creature can be stimulated by you at a time; stimulating a second creature ends the effect on the first.

features.name: Line of Fire
features.text:
Your medicated shots ignore Half Cover and Three-Quarters Cover. In addition, you can make a medicated shot against a creature you can't see if a creature that you can see and that is Friendly to you is within 5 feet of it.

> **Playing a Combat Medic**
>
> You fight from range in armor, and once on each Attack action one shot is medicine: it heals a friend or sickens an enemy. Out of a fight, you site the camp so the company stays well, and you can read any army's food, sickness and temper by watching it.

subclasses.name: Doctor
subclasses.lead: If a stranger pictures a Physician, they picture a Doctor: the degree, the house call, and the title people use at the door. You link your patients in chains of vital current, heal and bolster them in the middle of a fight, and step through the air to whichever of them needs you when someone decides you make a good target. Your patients needn't stay at your elbow: a friend running the rooftops is still on your chain, and you can heal them from the street, or be up there beside them in a step the moment someone comes for you.

features.name: Vital Stream
features.text:
You channel a stream of vitalizing energy through your focus. As a Bonus Action, you can link yourself to willing creatures you can see within 30 feet of yourself. You and the creatures you have linked are your **chain**. Your chain can include up to two creatures other than you; this number increases to three at Physician level 6, four at level 10, and five at level 14.

A creature stays in your chain while it is within 60 feet of you or of another creature in your chain, so a chain can stretch as far as its members do. Its link ends if it dies, or if it is ever more than 60 feet from you and from every other creature in your chain. All your links end if you have the Incapacitated condition for any reason other than dropping to 0 Hit Points, and you can end any link at any time (no action required). Dropping to 0 Hit Points, yours or a linked creature's, doesn't end a link. Links otherwise last until you finish a Long Rest.

While you have a chain, you gain the following benefits:

- **Range.** You can use Healing Prowess on any creature in your chain, rather than only a creature you touch. Only Healing Prowess travels the chain this way; a spell you cast doesn't, unless a feature says it does.
- **Heal or Bolster.** When you use Healing Prowess on a creature in your chain, you can choose to have it gain Temporary Hit Points equal to the number rolled plus your Intelligence modifier instead of regaining Hit Points.
- **Triage.** When you use Healing Prowess on a creature in your chain, one other creature of your choice in your chain gains Temporary Hit Points equal to your Intelligence modifier.
- **Stand Back.** When a creature in your chain is reduced to 0 Hit Points, you can take a Reaction to use Healing Prowess on it. Once you use Stand Back, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

**The Title.** When you introduce yourself as a doctor at a door, a gate, or a checkpoint where someone inside is sick or hurt, you're let in to see the patient, and nobody asks for your papers until the patient has been seen. A certificate in your hand that a person is too ill to travel, to stand trial, or to be married this month is believed by any official who doesn't have a doctor of their own to send.

> **The Chain at the Table**
>
> Nobody has to track an order or measure between pairs. Before the day, link the party with one Bonus Action. In a fight, one question matters: is this creature within 60 feet of anyone in the chain? If it is, your Healing Prowess can reach it. Describe the link: a thread of light, a pulse you can see in both throats at once, a warmth that travels.

features.name: Practice
features.text: In any settlement, you can set up a practice with a day's work and a room. While you practice, you earn a comfortable living, and patients talk. After a day of practice in a place, ask the DM two of the following questions about it, and the DM answers truthfully. Who here is sick, who is pregnant, and who is drinking? Who has been beaten, and who is paying for it? Who is hiding a condition, and from whom? Who here is dying, and who would be glad of it? You can ask again after each further week of practice there. A household that has called you to a bedside will let you in again.

features.name: House Call
features.text: When you would take damage, or when a Hostile creature ends its turn within 5 feet of you, you can take a Reaction and expend one Prowess Die to teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 5 feet of a creature in your chain that is within 30 feet of you. You still take the damage that triggered the Reaction.

features.name: On Your Feet
features.text:
You can cast *Revivify* on a creature in your chain, even if you don't have it prepared, without expending a spell slot or providing Material components. For this purpose, a creature that was in your chain when it died is treated as still linked for 1 minute after its death. A creature you return to life this way regains Hit Points equal to one roll of your Prowess Die plus your Intelligence modifier (no die is expended), instead of 1 Hit Point. Once you cast *Revivify* in this way, you can't cast it this way again until you finish a Long Rest.

In addition, you are no longer limited in how often you can use Stand Back; you can use it whenever you have a Reaction and a Prowess Die to spend.

features.name: The Living Chain
features.text:
Once on each of your turns, when you cast a Physician spell of level 1 or higher that restores Hit Points, each creature in your chain, including you, regains Hit Points equal to your Intelligence modifier.

In addition, when a creature in your chain is reduced to 0 Hit Points, you can use House Call and Stand Back as one Reaction, expending one Prowess Die for both: you teleport to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of that creature, wherever it is in your chain, and use Healing Prowess on it.

> **Playing a Doctor**
>
> Link the party over breakfast, and your healing reaches anyone on the chain, wherever the chain stretches. Out of a fight, you set up a practice in town and learn who is sick and who is hiding it.

subclasses.name: Hedge Witch
subclasses.lead: The Hedge Witch learned healing outside the schools, from a relative, a village healer, or a neighbor who knew that life costs life. You take the vitality you give: out of an enemy, out of the pain you and your friends receive, and when you must, out of your own blood. You curse as readily as you cure, and the village comes to your door at night for both.

features.name: Rip Life
features.text: When you use Healing Prowess, you can rip it from a creature instead of touching an ally: choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself that isn't a Construct or an Undead. The creature must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC, taking Necrotic damage equal to the number rolled on the Prowess Die plus your Intelligence modifier on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. Either way, you, or one creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself, then regain Hit Points equal to the number rolled plus your Intelligence modifier.

features.name: Cunning Folk
features.text: You know the remedies, charms, and taboos of any countryside you've lived in for a season. The people there who would never go to a Lanternhall doctor come to you, and they tell you what they'd never tell a priest. Once a week in such a place, someone knocks after dark with a true story, and you choose which kind of visitor it is: someone sick or hurt and hiding it; someone cursed, or who believes it, who names who did it; or someone who tells you what the place is afraid of. The DM plays the visitor. You can also look at a charm, a witch bottle, a poppet, or a hex sign and tell what it was made to do, whether it worked, and whether the hand that made it knew what it was doing.

features.name: Ill Wish
features.text: As a Bonus Action, you can curse one creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself; this costs no Prowess Die. The creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or be cursed until the end of your next turn. Choose one ability score when you curse the creature: while cursed, it has Disadvantage on ability checks and saving throws made with that ability. If the creature is your patient, it makes the saving throw against Ill Wish using the ability in which you learned it has the lowest saving throw bonus. The curse ends early if you use this feature on another creature, or if the target is affected by *Remove Curse* or a similar effect.

features.name: Communal Pain
features.text:
As a Magic action, you can expend one Prowess Die to raise an aura of shared suffering in a 10-foot Emanation originating from you for 1 minute. While the aura lasts, once on each turn when another willing creature in the aura takes damage, you can take half of that damage (round down) in its place (no action required). Damage you take this way can't be reduced in any way. You can end the aura early at any time (no action required).

Every point of damage you take from hostile creatures while the aura is active, including damage you take in another creature's place, is stored as **Pain**. You can store Pain up to three times your Physician level; any excess is lost. Stored Pain is lost when the aura ends.

As a Magic action, you can release your stored Pain in one of two ways:

- **Retribution.** One creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself takes Necrotic damage equal to the Pain released, or half as much on a successful Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC.
- **Restitution.** One creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself regains Hit Points equal to the Pain released.

Releasing Pain reduces your stored Pain to 0.

**Back Doors.** The healers outside the licenses know of one another. In any countryside, within a day you can find the local cunning man, wise woman, or their equivalent, and they'll give you a bed, a meal, and a warning about who in the district is looking for people like you.

features.name: Blood Price
features.text: You can pay for healing with your own blood. While your Communal Pain aura is active, you can take a Bonus Action to expend one Prowess Die and roll it. You take Necrotic damage equal to the number rolled, which can't be reduced or prevented, and each other willing creature in the aura regains Hit Points equal to the number rolled. Damage you take this way is stored as Pain.

features.name: The Long Grudge
features.text: Your curses settle in. Your Ill Wish now lasts for 1 minute (you must maintain Concentration on it, as if on a spell), you can have up to two creatures cursed by it at once (cursing a third ends the oldest curse), and a creature cursed by your Ill Wish takes extra Necrotic damage equal to your Intelligence modifier the first time each turn it takes damage from your Rip Life or a Physician spell you cast.

features.name: Threefold
features.text:
When you release Pain, you can divide it among up to three creatures you can see within 30 feet of yourself, choosing Retribution or Restitution for each. A creature cursed by your Ill Wish that takes Retribution damage takes an additional amount equal to your Intelligence modifier. You can store Pain up to five times your Physician level, and you can release Pain as a Bonus Action.

In addition, your Communal Pain aura becomes a 20-foot Emanation.

> **Playing a Hedge Witch**
>
> Your healing comes out of an enemy, or out of the pain you and your friends take, and a curse costs you a Bonus Action. Out of a fight, the village tells you what it hides from the priest, and you can read any charm or hex and the hand that made it.

subclasses.name: Immortalist
subclasses.lead:
The Immortalist turned the Physician's magic inward, to see how far a body could go. You found the Font inside yourself, and you pay for spells with your own life as well as with spell slots: your Hit Point Dice become a second supply of magic. Your harm takes the form of your own energy (fire, cold, lightning, radiance, or the will), and as you rise, your body stops aging, stops needing food or air, and refuses to die easily.

*For a campaign about a healer and the monster inside, see the optional rule The Monster Within, later in this class description.*

features.name: The Font Within
features.text:
You find the Font: the same source of life that clerics receive from their gods and druids from nature. There is only one, but you have found it inside your own body rather than outside it, and you draw on it from there. It gives you a second way to pay for your magic.

**Draw on the Font.** You keep your spell slots and cast with them as normal. You can also pay for a Physician spell with your own Hit Point Dice, which is called drawing on the Font:

- **Cost.** When you cast a Physician spell of level 1 through 5, you can spend a number of Hit Point Dice equal to the spell's level instead of expending a spell slot. If you cast the spell with a higher-level slot's effect, you spend Hit Point Dice equal to the level at which you cast it, which can be no higher than the highest level of spell slot you have.
- **Limit.** You can't draw on the Font to cast a spell of level 6 or higher. Drawing on the Font counts as expending a spell slot for the rule that you can expend only one spell slot to cast a spell on a turn.
- **Which dice.** Only Hit Point Dice you gained from Physician levels can be spent this way, and between Long Rests you can spend a number of them this way no greater than your Proficiency Bonus.
- **No healing from them.** Hit Point Dice spent this way are expended without being rolled and don't restore Hit Points.
- **Recovery.** When you finish a Short Rest, you regain one expended Hit Point Die.

> **The Cost Shows**
>
> Every die spent on a spell is a die that won't heal the Immortalist at the next rest, and the character won't feel it until they try to rest. As the DM, show the cost before then: fatigue, unsteady hands, a drawn face. A Physician who has spent their Font by noon should look like it.

**Symbiosis.** Drawing on the Font changes what your body needs and what it can survive. You gain the following as you reach the listed Physician levels:

- **Level 5.** You add *Fly* to your spellbook. It counts as a Physician spell for you and doesn't count against the spells you add to your spellbook when you gain a level.
- **Level 9.** You stop aging, and you can't be aged magically.
- **Level 13.** You no longer need to eat, drink, or breathe.
- **Level 17.** When you drop to 0 Hit Points, you are automatically Stable, and you don't make Death Saving Throws. Damage still causes Death Saving Throw failures; you become Stable again after each one.

**The Font in Others.** You know the Font when you touch it. By touching a creature for a moment, you learn whether it is living, dying, dead, or Undead, and whether the Font has opened in it as it has in you.

**Fellow Seekers.** Ascetics, alchemists, and adepts of the inner elixir recognize what you are after a few minutes' talk. In any city, monastery, or pilgrim road where such people live, you can find one within a day, and they'll share a meal, a place by the fire, and what they know of the Font in that place.

features.name: Attuned Energy
features.text:
Choose a damage type: Cold, Fire, Lightning, Psychic, or Radiant. This is your **attuned energy**: the form your own vitality takes when you push it outward. Fire is your metabolism let loose, the vital heat every living body burns to stay alive. Lightning is the signal that runs your nerves. Cold is the slowed heart and the held breath, and the rime that follows. Radiant is your own life burning as bright as the sun, and everything near you feels the heat of it. Psychic is the will that moves your flesh, sent to move something else: a watcher sees nothing leave you, only the target buckling as though struck from inside.

A Physician's harm is Necrotic. Yours no longer has to be. When you cast a Physician spell that deals Necrotic damage, you can have it deal your attuned damage type instead; the spell is otherwise unchanged, and what anyone watching sees is your energy, not the spell's.

You also work in your energy directly. You gain your energy's set from the Attunements list below:

- **A cantrip,** which counts as a Physician cantrip for you and doesn't count against the number of cantrips you know.
- **One spell of each level from 1 through 5,** each added to your spellbook when you reach a Physician level at which you can cast it. These spells count as Physician spells for you and don't count against the spells you add to your spellbook when you gain a level.
- **Swaps.** You can swap any of them, when you gain it or whenever you gain a Physician level, for another spell of the same level that deals your attuned damage type, from the Bard, Cleric, Druid, Physician, Sorcerer, Warlock, or Wizard spell list. If no spell of a given level deals your attuned damage type, you can choose one of a lower level that does.

> **Attunements**
>
> Each set is a cantrip, then one spell per level from 1 to 5. Pick a word and play; swap later if you like.
>
> **Fire.** *Fire Bolt*, then *Burning Hands · Scorching Ray · Fireball · Wall of Fire · Flame Strike.*
>
> **Cold.** *Ray of Frost*, which also drops the target's Speed, then *Ice Knife · Dragon's Breath · Cold Storage · Ice Storm · Cone of Cold.*
>
> **Lightning.** *Shocking Grasp*, which keeps the target from making Opportunity Attacks, then *Chromatic Orb · Convulsion · Lightning Bolt · Call Lightning · Defibrillation.* (Cast *Chromatic Orb* as Lightning. No level 4 spell in SRD 5.2.1 is built on Lightning, so *Call Lightning*, a level 3 spell, is the set's level 4 pick; *Conjure Minor Elementals*, which adds Lightning to your own attacks, is the level 4 swap. *Arc*, a new Sorcerer and Wizard spell in the Spells appendix at the back of this book, is another level 3 choice: a Bonus Action teleport instead of the line.)
>
> **Radiant.** *Sacred Flame*, which ignores cover, then *Guiding Bolt · Moonbeam · Spirit Guardians · Guardian of Faith · Flame Strike.*
>
> **Psychic.** *Vicious Mockery*, which gives the target Disadvantage on its next attack roll, then *Dissonant Whispers · Mind Spike · Fugue · Phantasmal Killer · Dream.* (*Dream* is the one level 5 spell in SRD 5.2.1 that deals Psychic damage to another creature, and it works on a sleeper, not in a fight; in a fight, cast *Phantasmal Killer* with a level 5 slot.)

features.name: Life-Fused Casting
features.text:
When you cast a level 1+ spell that deals your attuned damage type, or use a Bonus Action to deal damage with such a spell you are concentrating on, you can expend one Prowess Die as part of that action and choose one of the following:

- One target of the spell takes extra damage of your attuned type equal to the number rolled.
- One creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself regains Hit Points equal to the number rolled plus your Intelligence modifier.

You can't use Life-Fused Casting on a spell cast from an item's charges.

features.name: Font-Touched
features.text: Choose two spells from the Cleric spell list, each of a level for which the Physician Features table gives you spell slots at your Physician level. A spell can't be one that produces a creature or anything else that takes its own actions: the Font is your own life, and it won't run anything that acts on its own. Each spell counts as a Physician spell for you, is added to your spellbook, and is always prepared; it doesn't count against the number of spells you can prepare. You choose an additional spell this way at Physician levels 10 and 14.

features.name: Transfusion
features.text:
You learn to move vital energy between forms, and from your own body into another's.

**Exchange.** As a Bonus Action, you can expend one of your Hit Point Dice to regain one expended Prowess Die. You can do this a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

**Perfusion.** Once per Long Rest, as a Magic action, you can touch another willing creature and route the Font into its spellcasting. Choose one:

- *Draw on its behalf.* Spend from 1 to 5 Physician Hit Point Dice. The creature regains one expended spell slot whose level equals the number of Hit Point Dice you spent. This counts as drawing on the Font.
- *Give what you carry.* Expend one of your own spell slots. The creature regains one expended spell slot of the same level.

The creature can't regain a spell slot of a level higher than the highest it can normally cast, and it must have expended a slot of that level to regain it. The creature regains a spell slot, not any other resource.

features.name: Conduit
features.text: You have Resistance to your attuned damage type. In addition, when you cast a level 1+ spell that restores Hit Points to one or more creatures, expending a spell slot or Hit Point Dice to do so, you can cause one creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself to take damage of your attuned type equal to your Intelligence modifier plus the level of the spell slot expended or the number of Hit Point Dice spent to cast it. This doesn't work with a spell cast from an item's charges.

features.name: Rebirth
features.text:
When you are reduced to 0 Hit Points but not killed outright, you instead drop to 1 Hit Point. Each other creature within 10 feet of you either takes 2d10 damage of your attuned type or regains 2d10 Hit Points; you choose for each creature. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

> **Playing an Immortalist**
>
> You pay for spells with spell slots and with your own Hit Point Dice, and your harm comes out as the energy you chose. Out of a fight, you can tell by touch whether the Font has opened in someone, and seekers in every city know you as one of their own.

subclasses.name: Neurologist
subclasses.lead: Your medicine works on the nerves, and through them on the mind. Thomas Willis gave the discipline its name in Oxford four years ago, and it's still the least understood of the specialties. Neurologists work on the current that runs through every living body, offering solace to allies and torment to enemies. You heal at a distance along the nerves, steady a friend against fear and charm, and cast the spells that frighten, stun, and break a mind.

features.name: Reading the Nerves
features.text:
When you use Diagnosis on a creature, automatically or with a successful check, you also learn whether any effect on its mind, such as a charm, a fear, a compulsion, or a voice, is the creature's own, the work of a spell or similar magical effect, or the influence of another creature; if the source is a creature you can see, you learn which one.

Add the following to your Treatment table:

| Treatment | DC |
|---|---|
| End the Charmed or Frightened condition | 12 |
| End the Stunned condition | 15 |

In addition, you gain proficiency in the Insight skill if you don't already have it, and you learn the *Vicious Mockery* cantrip, which counts as a Physician cantrip for you and doesn't count against the number of cantrips you know.

**Tells.** You can read the body's signals in anyone you talk with for a minute: you know whether they're afraid, in pain, exhausted, drunk or drugged, or hiding an injury. The feature tells you the state; it doesn't tell you the reason.

**Nerve Spells.** A **nerve spell** is a Physician spell that deals Psychic damage or can give a creature the Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, Stunned, or Incapacitated condition. Several Neurologist features work on them.

**Neurologist Spells.** When you reach a Physician level specified in the Neurologist Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared. Each counts as a Physician spell for you and is added to your spellbook.

| Physician Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Dissonant Whispers*, *Mind Spike* |
| 5 | *Speak with Dead*, *Tiny Hut* |
| 7 | *Compulsion*, *Phantasmal Killer* |
| 9 | *Dominate Person*, *Modify Memory* |

features.name: Reflex
features.text:
You can send your medicine along the nerves instead of through your hands. When you use Healing Prowess, you can choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself instead of a creature you touch. The creature regains Hit Points equal to the number rolled plus your Intelligence modifier.

**Nerve Sheathing.** A nerve carries better when it is wrapped. When you use Reflex, the creature can choose one of the following: it regains its Reaction if it has used it since the start of its last turn, or it can immediately move up to half its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

features.name: The Quiet Room
features.text: With an hour of treatment (a dark quiet room, running water, music, or talk), you can ease a creature's mind: one fear, panic, or mania that isn't magical leaves it for a day, and it sleeps that night. You can also tell, by watching a fit, whether it's a seizure, a possession, a curse, or a performance, and you can explain the difference to a cathedral in terms it can't easily dismiss.

features.name: Steady the Signal
features.text:
When a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself fails a saving throw against the Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, or Stunned condition, or against a spell or other effect that deals Psychic damage, you can take a Reaction and expend one Prowess Die to let it reroll the saving throw. It must use the new roll.

In addition, you can perform Treatment for the Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, or Stunned condition on your patient while you can see it within 30 feet of yourself, rather than only within your reach, and doing so doesn't expend a use of a Healer's Kit.

features.name: Press the Wire
features.text:
When you cast a nerve spell, you can expend one Prowess Die as part of casting the spell. One target of the spell has Disadvantage on its saving throw against it.

You can also quicken or drag the signal itself: you can cast *Haste* or *Slow* once without expending a spell slot, even if you don't have it prepared. You regain the ability to do so when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Frayed Nerves
features.text:
The first time a creature fails a saving throw against a given casting of a nerve spell, it takes extra Psychic damage equal to your Intelligence modifier, and it can't take Reactions until the end of its next turn.

In addition, once on each of your turns when you cast a nerve spell of level 1 or higher, you and each creature of your choice within 10 feet of you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Intelligence modifier.

features.name: The Body Electric
features.text:
The whole wire answers you. You have Immunity to the Paralyzed and Stunned conditions, and magic can't reduce your Speed. One patient of your choice that isn't Hostile to you (you choose when you finish a Long Rest) has Advantage on saving throws against the Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, and Stunned conditions while it is within 30 feet of you.

In addition, when you use Reflex, the creature can instead immediately take one of these actions: the Attack action (one weapon attack only), the Dash action, the Disengage action, the Hide action, or the Utilize action. A creature can benefit from this once, and can't do so again until it finishes a Long Rest.

> **Playing a Neurologist**
>
> Your healing travels 30 feet along the nerves, and your spells frighten, charm and stun. Out of a fight, you calm a troubled mind, tell a fit from a possession, and read the tells in anyone you talk with.

subclasses.name: Plague Doctor
subclasses.lead: Everyone knows the beaked, masked figure in robes walking through a stricken town, and everyone gives it a wide berth. A Plague Doctor works in clouds of miasma that cure or infect, and can save a whole town or doom it.

features.name: Miasma
features.text:
You learn to carry your medicine on the air. When you use Healing Prowess, you can release it as a cloud instead of a touch: choose a point you can see within 30 feet of yourself. A 10-foot-radius Sphere of restorative vapor appears centered on that point and lasts until the end of the turn. One creature of your choice in the area regains Hit Points equal to the number rolled on the Prowess Die plus your Intelligence modifier. Each other creature of your choice in the area that has at least 1 Hit Point regains Hit Points equal to your Intelligence modifier. Each creature of your choice in the area has Advantage on the next saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn.

Miasma comes with three more benefits: you gain proficiency in the Nature skill if you don't already have it, you have Resistance to Poison damage, and you can't transmit a disease you carry.

features.name: Bill of Health
features.text: You know the quarantine law and practice of any port, city, or border you're in: how long it holds arrivals, what passes it accepts, and how its cordon is kept. Health boards, harbor masters, and quarantine officers recognize you as one of theirs. You can issue a bill of health for a person or a ship you've examined and found clean, and those officers will honor it. (Forging one is outside this feature.)

features.name: Pathology
features.text: When you cast a Physician spell that deals Necrotic or Poison damage, you can expend one Prowess Die as part of casting the spell to deal extra damage of that type to one target of the spell equal to the number rolled.

features.name: Purge
features.text:
Your treatment reaches everyone in the cloud. When you use Miasma, you can take a Utilize action on the same turn to perform Treatment on every willing creature in that Miasma's area at once, whether or not it is your patient, making a single Intelligence (Medicine) check and expending a single use of a Healer's Kit. Each creature is treated for the same effect; a creature that has been treated for that effect since its last rest can't benefit, whether the earlier attempt succeeded or failed.

In addition, you can make your Miasma noxious. When you do, no creature regains Hit Points or gains Advantage from it; instead, each hostile creature in the area when it appears takes Poison damage equal to the number rolled on the Prowess Die plus your Intelligence modifier, or half as much on a successful Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. Once you make your Miasma noxious, you can't do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest. From Physician level 10, you can do so twice between rests.

features.name: The Slow Way
features.text: You can tell, by Diagnosis or an hour's examination, which members of a household have had a disease and come through it the slow way, and so can't catch it again, and which were cured by magic and can. You can also nurse the slow way. When you tend a creature through a natural disease over a Long Rest, without ending it with a spell or a feature, it has Advantage on its saving throws against the disease until your next Long Rest; if it recovers, it can't catch that disease again.

features.name: Outbreak
features.text:
Your afflictions spread. When a creature fails a saving throw against a level 1+ Physician spell you cast that deals Necrotic or Poison damage, or fails its saving throw against your noxious Miasma, it becomes **infected**. The infection is a disease. An infected creature can't regain Hit Points. At the start of each of its turns, it takes Necrotic damage equal to your Intelligence modifier (you can choose for it to take none). At the end of each of its turns, it makes a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a success, the infection ends. On a failure, one other creature of your choice within 5 feet of it becomes infected. An infection ends after 1 minute if it hasn't ended sooner. No more creatures can be infected at once than your Intelligence modifier (minimum of one); while that many are infected, no other creature becomes infected. Creatures that have Immunity to disease can't be infected, and your allies are never infected by this feature.

In addition, each creature that regains Hit Points from your Miasma has Resistance to Poison damage and can't be diseased until the end of its next turn.

**Tracing.** When you examine a creature that has a natural disease, you learn the route the disease took to it: the water, the air, a touch, the cloth, the food, or the vermin. You can also ask the DM one of the following questions, and the DM answers truthfully. Whom or what did it catch the disease from (if that source is within a day's travel)? Who else here has it? Who or what carried it here? (For the DM: in our history no one showed that fleas carry plague until Paul-Louis Simond did in 1898.)

features.name: The Cordon
features.text:
The radius of your Miasma becomes 20 feet. In addition, each friendly creature within 10 feet of you has Advantage on Constitution saving throws and has Immunity to disease and to the Poisoned condition.

**Wide Berth.** You can walk into and out of a quarantined city, a cordon, or a pest house, and no guard stops you. A health officer anywhere will take your word on whether a house can be opened, a ship unloaded, or a body buried.

> **Playing a Plague Doctor**
>
> You release your healing as a cloud that mends your friends and, from level 6, can turn noxious on your enemies. Out of a fight, you know every port's quarantine law, issue bills of health the officers honor, trace an outbreak to its source, and walk through any cordon.

subclasses.name: Surgeon
subclasses.lead: A Surgeon works from across the room. Your instrument cuts from sixty feet away, and it carries your healing to whoever stands near it.

features.name: The Fine Instrument
features.text:
Your instrument is a Scalpel. It is a Spellcasting Focus for your Physician spells rather than a weapon. You also learn the *Mage Hand* cantrip if you don't already know it. It counts as a Physician cantrip for you and doesn't count against the number of cantrips you know, and the spectral hand takes the shape of your instrument.

**Public Operation.** In any town with a university, a hospital, or a market square, you can give a public demonstration of your art for an afternoon. You earn a modest fee from the crowd, and by evening every physician, barber, and apothecary in town knows your name and where you're staying. One of them comes to you with a case nobody else will touch; the DM supplies the case.

features.name: The Incision
features.text: As a Magic action, you can make an **incision**: a ranged spell attack using Intelligence against a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself. On a hit, the target takes 1d10 Force damage. This damage increases to 2d10 at Physician level 5, 3d10 at level 11, and 4d10 at level 17. The incision is magic but not a spell: *Counterspell* can't stop it, features that work on spells don't apply to it, and it doesn't work in an Antimagic Field.

features.name: Cut and Close
features.text: When you hit a creature with an incision, you can use Healing Prowess as part of the same attack, without spending a Bonus Action. You expend a Prowess Die as normal. The creature you heal can be any creature within 10 feet of you or within 10 feet of the target. If the target is your patient, it can't take Reactions until the end of its next turn.

features.name: The Sharpest Cut
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, you can send your instrument to hover at a point you can see within 60 feet of yourself, where it stays until you send it again, recall it as a Bonus Action, or have the Unconscious condition. It returns to you if it is ever more than 60 feet from you, and it can't be targeted by attacks, spells, or other effects.

Your incisions now add your Intelligence modifier to their damage. While your instrument hovers, your incisions originate from it rather than from you, and you can use Healing Prowess on any creature within 10 feet of it rather than only a creature you touch.

The hovering instrument can also do anything your *Mage Hand* could do (manipulate an object, open a door or a container, carry up to 10 pounds) using a Bonus Action, without your having to cast the spell. It can use a Healer's Kit, and you can make Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) checks through it, and Intelligence (Medicine) checks to stabilize or examine a creature within 5 feet of it.

**Quiet Work.** The Field Service keeps a short list of Surgeons for work that has to be done quietly, and you're on it. Once between adventures, you can ask any Field Service rider or Lanternhall house for one thing the Service gives its own: passage with a caravan it guards, a bed and a stable in any town on its routes, or a sealed letter carried to anyone along them. The Service asks the same of you in return, the next time you pass through a town where it needs a Surgeon who isn't seen.

features.name: The Sealed Table
features.text:
You add *Telekinesis* and *Resilient Sphere* to your spellbook. They count as Physician spells for you and are always prepared; they don't count against the number of spells you can prepare.

You also learn to seal the table. When you cast *Resilient Sphere*, you can choose to have it enclose you and one willing creature within 5 feet of you together, as though the two of you were a single Large creature. While you are enclosed together, you can perform Treatment on that creature and use Healing Prowess on it as normal; nothing else passes through the sphere in either direction, as the spell describes.

In addition, you can perform Treatment on your patient while it is within 10 feet of your hovering instrument, rather than only within your reach.

features.name: Not on My Table
features.text:
When a creature within 10 feet of you, or within 10 feet of your hovering instrument, would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, you can take a Reaction to refuse it. Choose the point the triggering creature was within 10 feet of, you or the instrument. Until the start of your next turn, each creature within 10 feet of that point that you choose when you take the Reaction, including the triggering creature, can't be reduced below 1 Hit Point. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

> **Playing a Surgeon**
>
> You cut from across the room: the incision is a ranged spell attack, and each one that hits can carry healing to someone near you or near the target. Out of a fight, a public operation fills the room and brings you the cases nobody else will take, and the Field Service owes you favors on the road.

subclasses.name: Vitalist
subclasses.lead: You couldn't find where your body stopped. The life in your chest and the life in the air, the ground, the river and the people beside you is one current, and you're a place where it runs strong. When you heal someone, you aren't giving away something of yours, and you feel it come back. In the villages you arrive with a basket of simples, open every window, and ask for nothing but a bed, and you can diagnose a field, a well or a herd as readily as a patient.

features.name: Continuity
features.text:
You feel the Font everywhere: in the air you breathe, the ground under you, the sky over you, and every living thing around you, and you feel yourself as part of it. You can't be cut off from it; a cellar, a city, and a dungeon are all alive. The life you pass on runs through you on the way, and you gain the following benefits.

- **Within and Without.** When you restore Hit Points to another creature with a Physician spell or Healing Prowess, you regain Hit Points equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1). You can benefit from this once on each turn.
- **Nothing Is Wasted.** When Hit Points you restore with a Physician spell or Healing Prowess would raise a creature above its Hit Point maximum, the excess goes instead to another creature of your choice within 30 feet of you that is missing Hit Points (the most injured, unless you choose otherwise); that creature can be you. The excess passes on only once: whatever the second creature can't use is lost. You can't heal a creature that is already at its Hit Point maximum just to send the healing on.
- **The Day Shows.** When you restore Hit Points to a creature, the world around you answers, and does it no harm. The light warms and goes golden, the air thickens and moves, insects hum, birds start up, and the nearest green things lean toward you, bud, or flower; a crack in a wall fills with moss. Anyone watching knows something just happened.

features.name: The Book of the World
features.text:
When you reach a Physician level specified in the Vitalist Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared, and they are in your spellbook. They count as Physician spells for you and don't count against the number of spells you can prepare.

| Physician Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Goodberry*, *Speak with Animals* |
| 5 | *Locate Animals or Plants*, *Speak with Plants* |
| 7 | *Locate Creature*, *Plant Growth* |
| 9 | *Commune with Nature*, *Reincarnate* |

features.name: Signatures
features.text:
You gain proficiency in the Nature skill and with the Herbalism Kit; if you already have either, choose another skill from the Physician's skill list or another tool. By handling a plant, a stone, a fungus, or a part of an animal for 1 minute, you learn its virtues: whether it's poisonous and what it would do, what it heals or harms, and whether it could serve as a component for a spell you know. Given an hour in any place where things grow, you can find the simples for an ordinary remedy, a dye, or a poison.

**Diagnose a Place.** You can use Diagnosis on a place you stand in (a field, a well, a wood, a house): you learn whether it is blighted, poisoned, diseased, or cursed, and whether it is thin ground (the rule is in *Euphonia: Life on the Border*, Introduction, under "The Hidden, in the rules").

**Treat a Place.** You can use Treatment on a place you have diagnosed. It takes 1 hour and a use of a Healer's Kit, and the DC is the same as for the affliction in a creature (cure a disease for a blighted field or a sickly herd, end the Poisoned condition for a poisoned well, which needs no check). On a success, the place mends over the next few days. A curse needs magic, as it would in a patient.

**Respectable.** Your magic is natural magic, the kind every crown licenses because nobody can tell where it ends and medicine, gardening and alchemy begin. Your heals still turn the light gold and the grass toward you (The Day Shows), and someone always reports it; this is how you answer them. You have Advantage on any ability check to convince an official, a licensing examiner, or an inquisitor that your magic is lawful.

features.name: The Ground Takes It
features.text: When you or a creature you can see within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can take a Reaction and expend one Prowess Die to let the world take part of it: the damage is reduced by the number rolled plus your Intelligence modifier. Where the hurt goes shows: the grass under the creature browns, a puddle steams, a beam groans.

features.name: The World's Pulse
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, or over a minute outside a fight, you can feel for the pulse of the living world around you. Until the end of your next turn, you know the location of every living creature within 30 feet of yourself, and whether each is unharmed, injured, Bloodied, or near death. A creature that is hidden from you or has the Invisible condition can't hide its location from this sense, and you have Advantage on Initiative rolls when a living creature you sensed this way is among your foes. Undead and Constructs have no pulse: you sense them only as a gap where the life around them stops, which is often how you find them. The range becomes 60 feet at Physician level 10.

This sense needs no sight, and it works through doors and thin walls, but 1 foot of stone, dirt, or wood, 1 inch of metal, or a thin sheet of lead blocks it.

You also heal through the current. You can use Healing Prowess on any creature within 30 feet of yourself (60 feet from Physician level 10), rather than only a creature you touch, whether or not you are feeling for the pulse.

**The Long Cure.** If you have a weapon, bandage, or other object that carries a creature's blood or wound, you can cast a spell on it that restores Hit Points or ends a condition or disease, and the spell reaches that creature at any distance if it's on the same plane of existence. The spell's casting time becomes 1 hour.

features.name: Spillover
features.text:
