When Nothing Is Wasted has no creature to send the excess to, the excess stays with the creature you healed as Temporary Hit Points, up to a total equal to your Physician level.

**The Herbal.** When you finish a Long Rest, you can prepare one simple with your Herbalism Kit and give it to anyone. Any creature can take a Utilize action to apply the simple to itself or to a creature within its reach; that creature regains Hit Points equal to one roll of your Prowess Die. The simple loses its virtue at your next Long Rest.

**Almanac.** With a day's observation of a place, you can write its almanac for the season. The DM tells you the two things about the coming months that matter most to the people there, from these: whether the harvest will be good or poor; whether a sickness season is coming, and roughly when; when its birds, fish, or herds will move; and what has gone wrong with its water, soil, or air. A village that reads your almanac and finds it right sends for you the next year.

features.name: The Wheel Turns
features.text:
When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you, to which you have restored Hit Points since your last Long Rest, drops to 0 Hit Points but isn't killed outright, you can take a Reaction: the creature drops to 1 Hit Point instead and regains Hit Points equal to your Physician level. Every green thing within 60 feet of you goes through a year in a moment: it buds, flowers, fruits, and drops its leaves. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

**The Great Chain of Being.** When you diagnose a creature, automatically or with a successful check, you also learn its creature type and whether it is a Hidden creature (*Life on the Border*, Introduction, under "The Hidden, in the rules").

> **Playing a Vitalist**
>
> Heal, and feel it come back: every time you mend someone else, you mend a little yourself, and whatever a creature can't hold goes on to the next one who needs it. Out of a fight, you can diagnose a field, a well or a herd, and treat it. Open the windows.

multiclass.gains: Hit Point Die, proficiency in the Medicine skill, and training with Light armor
multiclass.text: You must have an Intelligence score of 13 or higher. Gain the following traits from the Core Physician Traits table: Hit Point Die, proficiency in the Medicine skill, and training with Light armor. Gain the Physician's level 1 features, which are listed in the Physician Features table. For multiclass spell slots, add all your Physician levels, as you would Wizard levels. If you have levels in another class, you regain expended Prowess Dice only when you finish a Long Rest.

optional_rules.name: The Monster Within
optional_rules.lead:
You heard the warnings against pushing the limits of Immortalism, and you did it anyway.

*This optional rule is off unless the DM turns it on for a campaign about a healer and the monster inside, and even then only an Immortalist can take it. Every feature in this rule is a Physician feature.*

On this path you draw more deeply on the Font than is safe. You are tested at four points in your career and once more at the end. Each test you pass gives you power. The first test you fail puts the Monster in you, and each failure after that makes it stronger.

The Rites belong to the hospitals that found the Font by study, Lanternhall first among them, and the hospitals warn their students off them. They are no part of Nath or Daoist practice, which reaches the perfected body by discipline, under a teacher, over years (see Immortalist).

sections.name: The Path in Order
sections.text:
1. **Level 4: you choose the path.** You choose it when you reach Physician level 4, after a level of living with the Font. The choice is permanent, and choosing it means undertaking the first Rite at that level. A way back, if a table wants one, is a story for the DM to write: a cure found, a bargain struck.
2. **Levels 4, 8, 12, and 16: the four Rites.** Each Rite is one Font saving throw, made unaided. A success gives you the next Ascendance boon. A failure transforms you into the Monster for 1 hour. Your first failure also means you carry the Monster from then on, and each later failure gives you the next Overgrowth benefit. From level 8 on you can decline a Rite, which also closes the Final Rite.
3. **From your first Rite, pass or fail: Deeper Draw and Surge.** You can spend more Hit Point Dice on the Font, and you can Surge to halve a spell's cost in dice at the risk of a Font saving throw.
4. **If you carry the Monster: Monster Form and the Shifting Balance.** A failed Font saving throw from Surge transforms you for 1 minute. At levels 7, 11, and 15 you gain more control over the change.
5. **Level 19: the Final Rite.** It is open only if you attempted all four Rites. If you failed all four, you make no roll, and your ending is **Acceptance**: you and the Monster share one life. Otherwise you can **resign** and keep what you have, or you can roll. The roll ends in **Mastery** (you learn *Wish*), **the Arrival** (you become the Avatar for good), or **the Eruption** (you die).

> **Terms in This Rule**
>
> - **Font saving throw.** A Constitution saving throw against DC 5 plus your Physician level. Made **unaided**, it is a d20 plus your Constitution modifier and Proficiency Bonus and nothing else. (Font Saving Throws)
> - **Rite.** One of four tests, at levels 4, 8, 12, and 16. (The Rites)
> - **Ascendance.** The four boons you gain, in order, for Rites you pass. (The Rites)
> - **The Monster.** What a failed Rite brings out: a body of muscle and frenzy with your mind pushed aside. To **carry the Monster** is to have failed at least one Rite, so that it can come out again. (The Rites)
> - **Overgrowth.** The three benefits the Monster gains, in order, for Rites you fail after the first. (The Rites)
> - **Monster Form.** The rules you use while transformed. (Monster Form)
> - **The Struggle.** The Font saving throw at the start of each of your turns in Monster Form, which decides whether you or the Monster has the turn. (Monster Form)
> - **The frenzy.** In Monster Form, you must attack a Hostile creature within your reach. (Monster Form)
> - **The Shifting Balance.** Three features, at levels 7, 11, and 15, for a character who carries the Monster. (The Shifting Balance)
> - **The Final Rite.** The test at level 19, with four endings: Mastery, the Arrival, the Eruption, and Acceptance. (The Final Rite)
> - **The Avatar.** What you become at the Arrival: one permanent form with the Monster's body and your spellcasting. (The Final Rite, The Arrival)
> - **Unbound.** The Avatar's one-minute surge of free casting. (The Arrival)
> - **Overtaken.** What happens when the Avatar fails a Font saving throw: the DM controls the character until it is called back, drops to 0 Hit Points, or dawn comes. (The Arrival)
> - **The Due.** The price the Font takes when it answers a request, rolled on a d6 by the DM. It is rolled when the Final Rite's d20 shows 16 or higher, when the Avatar uses The Ask, and when someone raises a character lost to the Eruption. (The Due)

sections.name: Font Saving Throws
sections.text: Several features on this path call for a **Font saving throw**: a Constitution saving throw with a DC equal to 5 plus your Physician level. When a feature says the save is made **unaided**, you roll a d20 and add only your Constitution modifier and your Proficiency Bonus (even without proficiency in Constitution saving throws): no other bonus or penalty, and no Advantage, Disadvantage, reroll, or replacement of the d20 (such as Portent), applies to it, whatever its source. You can't choose to fail a Font saving throw.

sections.name: The Rites
sections.text:
Someone who knows the Rites must teach you before your first one. A Rite works only for a creature that understands what it is choosing and chooses it freely. A Rite that is forced, tricked, or magically compelled doesn't happen.

What a Rite involves (where it is done, what it requires, how long it takes) is the DM's to shape. By default, a Rite is a night alone in a shut room in a teaching hospital, after a day's fast, with the teacher outside the door until dawn. The rules cover only who may teach one, that you undertake it alone, and what you roll.

When you reach Physician level 4, and again when you reach levels 8, 12, and 16, you can undertake a Rite: you make a Font saving throw, unaided.

- **The first Rite** is part of choosing this path. Declining the path at level 4 is final.
- **From level 8 on,** you choose each time. A Rite you decline is not attempted and gives you nothing. Declining it closes that Rite and the Final Rite; you can still attempt the next Rite at its level.
- **If no one can teach you at level 4,** you undertake the first Rite at the first opportunity at level 4 or higher, and any later Rite whose level you have already reached follows it at that time.

**Success — Ascendance.** You make it through, and the power is yours. You gain the next boon from the Ascendance list, in order:

1. **Another spell.** You choose one additional spell with your Font-Touched feature (at Physician level 6, if you don't have it yet). This is on top of the one Deeper Draw gives, so a passed first Rite brings two.
2. **A level 6 spell from the Font.** Once per Long Rest, once your Physician level gives you level 6 spell slots, you can draw on the Font to cast a level 6 Physician spell (6 Hit Point Dice).
3. **Free Life-Fused Casting.** A number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, no more than once on each of your turns, you can use Life-Fused Casting without expending a Prowess Die. You regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
4. **A level 7 spell from the Font.** Once per Long Rest, once your Physician level gives you level 7 spell slots, you can draw on the Font to cast a level 7 Physician spell (7 Hit Point Dice).

**Failure — the Monster.** You immediately transform into the Monster for 1 hour (it can still end early, as described in Monster Form).

- **Your first failed Rite:** the Monster is born. From now on you **carry the Monster**, and a failed Font saving throw from Surge transforms you.
- **Each failed Rite after that:** the Monster grows. You gain the next benefit from the Overgrowth list, in order.

The Overgrowth list (its benefits are cumulative):

1. **Thicker.** The Temporary Hit Points you gain on transformation are doubled.
2. **Larger.** The radius of Monstrous Aura becomes 15 feet, and your Unarmed Strike die in Monster Form becomes a d12.
3. **Hardened.** You have Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage while in Monster Form.

A character who passes every Rite never carries the Monster, though The Due (at the end of this rule) can still transform them for a minute.

> **The Rites' Odds**
>
> Each Rite is harder than the one before it: the DC rises by 4 from one Rite to the next, and your Proficiency Bonus rises by 1. Only your Constitution modifier changes these odds.
>
> | Constitution modifier | Level 4 | Level 8 | Level 12 | Level 16 | Pass all four | Fail all four |
> |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
> | +1 | 75% | 60% | 45% | 30% | 6% | 4% |
> | +2 | 80% | 65% | 50% | 35% | 9% | 2% |
> | +3 | 85% | 70% | 55% | 40% | 13% | 1% |
> | +4 | 90% | 75% | 60% | 45% | 18% | under 1% |
> | +5 | 95% | 80% | 65% | 50% | 25% | under 1% |
>
> A character who attempts all four Rites usually passes two or three. At a Constitution modifier of +2, about nine in ten carry the Monster by level 16. Say this at the table when the path is chosen at level 4.

sections.name: Deeper Draw
sections.text: Once you have attempted your first Rite (see "The Rites"), whether you succeeded or failed, you can draw deeper: the number of Hit Point Dice you can spend drawing on the Font between Long Rests increases by your Proficiency Bonus. You also choose one additional spell with your Font-Touched feature (if you don't have that feature yet, you make the choice when you gain it at Physician level 6).

sections.name: Surge
sections.text:
Once you have attempted your first Rite, whether you succeeded or failed, you can Surge when you draw on the Font to cast a spell. If you do, the number of Hit Point Dice you must spend is halved (round up). At the end of that turn, make a Font saving throw. On a failure, the Font takes its toll: you expend additional Physician Hit Point Dice equal to the number you saved (if you have fewer, you expend all you have and gain one level of Exhaustion), and you can't Surge again until you finish a Long Rest. If you carry the Monster (see "The Rites"), it also comes through: you transform into the Monster (see "Monster Form").

You can Surge a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

sections.name: Monster Form
sections.text:
When you first carry the Monster, write its card: your swapped ability scores, Armor Class, Unarmed Strike attack and damage, and saving throws. That way, the swap is never worked out in the middle of a fight.

When you transform, the following rules apply for the duration. Unless another feature says otherwise, the transformation lasts for 1 minute. It ends early if you drop to 0 Hit Points.

**The Struggle.** At the start of each of your turns in Monster Form, make a Font saving throw. On a success, you hold on: you choose what you do, within the frenzy, and you can end the transformation at the end of the turn (no action required). On a failure, the Monster has the turn: you must take the Attack action against the creature nearest you, friend or foe (if several are equally near, the DM chooses), and you can't use Healing Prowess or end the transformation on that turn. Outside combat, you make this save once a minute, and a success lets you end the transformation.

- **Ability Swap.** Your Strength and Intelligence scores swap, and your Dexterity and Wisdom scores swap; swap them before applying any item or effect that sets a score. Your Constitution and Charisma scores don't change, so your Hit Point maximum is unchanged. Any spell you are permitted to cast, and any Physician feature you are permitted to use, while transformed uses your Intelligence score as it was before the swap.
- **Temporary Hit Points.** You gain Temporary Hit Points equal to twice your Physician level.
- **No Spellcasting.** You can't cast spells, and your Concentration on any spell ends. You can't take actions, Bonus Actions, or Reactions granted by Physician features outside this rule, unless a feature says it works in Monster Form; their passive benefits still apply.
- **Proficiencies.** You lose your skill proficiencies and gain proficiency in Athletics and Intimidation. When you use an Unarmed Strike to Grapple or Shove a creature, the target has Disadvantage on its saving throw. You keep your armor training and weapon proficiencies, and armor you are wearing changes with you.
- **Unarmed Strikes.** Your Unarmed Strikes deal 1d10 plus your Strength modifier Bludgeoning damage. You can attack twice, instead of once, when you take the Attack action; this doesn't stack with Extra Attack.
- **Slam.** When you Shove a creature you are grappling toward another creature or a solid object within 5 feet of it, the Grappled creature stops short of it, and both the Grappled creature and the creature or object take Bludgeoning damage equal to one roll of your Unarmed Strike die plus your Strength modifier.
- **Monstrous Aura.** At the start of each of your turns, you regain Hit Points equal to one roll of your Prowess Die (no die is expended). Each creature of your choice that starts its turn within 10 feet of you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 plus your Proficiency Bonus plus your Strength modifier) or have the Frightened condition until the end of that turn. A creature that has been Frightened by your Monstrous Aura can't be Frightened by it again until you next transform (for the Avatar, until you finish a Long Rest).

You keep control of your character, but the frenzy drives you: on each of your turns, if a Hostile creature is within your reach, you must take the Attack action against one (an attack, a Grapple, or a Shove).

When the transformation ends, you return to your normal form with the same number of Hit Points, and you lose any remaining Temporary Hit Points. Then the body pays: you expend Physician Hit Point Dice equal to your Proficiency Bonus (if you have fewer, you expend all you have and gain one level of Exhaustion).

> **What About Their Clothes?**
>
> Armor changes with you, because Armor Class matters. Everything else is up to your group. Decide before the first Rite whether the Monster's clothing survives the change, so that it isn't being settled in the middle of a scene.

> **The Monster at the Table**
>
> The Monster is the healer's own life with the healer's judgment taken out. It doesn't speak, but it wants things, and the player and the DM can let a want show in how it moves. It knows the healer's patients by smell: people who have seen it stand over a sleeping patient and leave them be tell a different story from the ones it threw through a wall. A town that knows it has a carrier treats the healer like a household with the plague: grateful for the medicine, and a chain on the door at night.
>
> | 1d6 | What the Monster Wants |
> |---|---|
> | 1 | |
> | 2 | |
> | 3 | |
> | 4 | |
> | 5 | |
> | 6 | |

sections.name: The Shifting Balance
sections.text:
If you carry the Monster, the balance between your two forms shifts as you gain levels. You gain each of the following at the listed Physician level, or immediately upon first carrying the Monster if you are already of that level or higher.

- **Level 7 — Hold It Together.** You can end Monster Form early as a Bonus Action. While in Monster Form, you can use Healing Prowess.
- **Level 11 — Call It.** You can transform into the Monster as a Bonus Action. Once you use Call It, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest. While in Monster Form, you retain your Diagnosis feature, your proficiency in Medicine, and your patient, and you can cast Physician cantrips and level 1 Physician spells. You can't draw on the Font or use Life-Fused Casting while transformed.
- **Level 15 — Turned.** Monster Form no longer ends on a Font saving throw. You still make the Struggle at the start of each of your turns, and a failure still gives the Monster that turn, but a success no longer lets you end the transformation; once transformed, you remain the Monster for its full duration unless you use Hold It Together or drop to 0 Hit Points. You can use Call It a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus per Long Rest. Transforming no longer breaks your Concentration, and you can cast Physician spells of level 3 or lower while in Monster Form, using spell slots only.

sections.name: The Final Rite
sections.text:
When you reach Physician level 19, if you attempted all four Rites, you come to the Final Rite. If you failed all four, you make no roll: your outcome is the last one below, Acceptance. Otherwise you choose: undertake the Final Rite, or resign. A Physician who declined any earlier Rite does not undertake the Final Rite and gains nothing at level 19 from this feature.

**Resignation.** You don't undertake the Final Rite. You keep everything you have, and you gain the next Ascendance boon you don't yet have.

**The Roll.** If you undertake the Final Rite, roll a d20, unaided: add 4 for each of the four Rites you succeeded on, and nothing else. No modifier, bonus, Advantage, reroll, or replacement of the d20 (such as Portent) applies, whatever its source. A total of 25 or higher, or a natural 20, is Mastery; a total of 20 to 24 is the Arrival; a total of 19 or lower is the Eruption. Whatever the outcome, if the d20 itself shows 16 or higher, the Font heard you: once the outcome is settled, the DM rolls on The Due.

> **The Odds**
>
> | Rites passed | Mastery | The Arrival | The Eruption | Heard (The Due) |
> |---|---|---|---|---|
> | 4 | 60% | 25% | 15% | 25% |
> | 3 | 40% | 25% | 35% | 25% |
> | 2 | 20% | 25% | 55% | 25% |
> | 1 | 5% | 20% | 75% | 25% |
>
> With a full record the Final Rite is a fair gamble. With one or two Rites passed it is a long shot that usually ends in the Eruption, and anyone who comes out of it with one Rite passed has been heard. Most who resign have passed fewer than three. A character who failed all four makes no roll; the ending is Acceptance.
>
> Say this at the table when the path is chosen at level 4: the Final Rite can end a character on one roll that nothing modifies. The player always has the choice to resign.

**Mastery.** You learn the *Wish* spell. It is a Physician spell for you, it is always prepared, and it doesn't count against the number of spells you can prepare. Any Ascendance boons you don't yet have are yours as well, and if you carry the Monster, so are any Overgrowth benefits you don't yet have.

**Higher Symbiosis.** When you achieve Mastery, you gain the first benefit below. If your DM awards Epic Boons for play beyond level 20, you gain the next benefit each time you gain an Epic Boon, in order.

- **(1) Regrowth.** While you are Bloodied and have at least 1 Hit Point, you regain Hit Points equal to one roll of your Prowess Die at the start of each of your turns (no die is expended).
- **(2) The Deep Draw.** You can draw on the Font to cast a spell of any level.
- **(3) The Body Keeps.** You have Resistance to Necrotic and Poison damage. You don't sleep; you can finish a Long Rest with 6 hours of light activity.
- **(4) Unfinished.** If you die and your body isn't destroyed, you return to life at the next dawn with 1 Hit Point and 3 levels of Exhaustion. Once this happens, it can't happen again until a year has passed.

A Master who carries the Monster can wish it away. This is a wish beyond duplicating a spell, with that wish's risks. If it is granted, the Monster is gone: you no longer carry it, and you lose Overgrowth and the Shifting Balance.

> **After Mastery**
>
> Mastery is not an ending. Two directions a Master might go, for the DM and player to consider:
>
> - **The source.** The Font is the life the Revelator's Cosmography calls Positive Energy, the plane of life unalloyed, found inside a body. A Master can go looking for where it came from.
> - **The refusal.** The one wish no one else can make: to be rid of the Font. A Master who wishes this loses *Wish*, Higher Symbiosis, and the Font, and keeps everything else. By default the Font allows it, and the DM rolls on The Due.

**The Arrival.** *You become a warped avatar of the Font, ever churning, always on the verge of losing what remains of yourself to the endless pulse of life.* You do not learn *Wish*. Your original form is gone; you now appear as the **Avatar** at all times, and Monster Form, if you carried it, no longer exists apart from you. The following rules apply for the rest of your life:

- **The Avatar's body.** The Monster Form rules for Proficiencies, Unarmed Strikes, Slam, and Monstrous Aura apply to you at all times, with the second Overgrowth benefit (whether or not you earned it) and without the third; the aura's regeneration is replaced by the one below. Your ability scores don't swap, you keep your proficiency in Medicine, your spellcasting, and your other Physician features, and you gain no Temporary Hit Points.
- **The frenzy.** The Monster's frenzy (see "Monster Form") drives you at all times. A failed Font saving throw from Surge makes you Overtaken instead of transforming you; the Font doesn't also take its toll.
- **Unbound.** As a Bonus Action, you can open yourself to the Font for 1 minute, and you can't end it early. While you are Unbound, you have Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage; when you take the Attack action, you can replace one of its attacks with casting a Physician spell of level 5 or lower that has a casting time of an action, drawing on the Font without spending Hit Point Dice (once per Unbound, the spell can be of level 6 or higher instead, and it calls for High Casting's Font saving throw below, unaided); and you can use Life-Fused Casting without expending a Prowess Die. At the end of each of your turns while you are Unbound, make a Font saving throw, unaided, against DC 12 rather than the usual DC; the DC increases by 1 for each later save in the same minute. You can become Unbound three times, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
- **Overtaken.** Whenever you fail a Font saving throw, the Font takes you. While you are Overtaken, the DM controls you: on each of your turns you attack, Grapple, or Shove the creatures nearest you, friend or foe, and if you are Unbound, your spells land among them as the DM chooses. Being Overtaken doesn't end when the fight does. It ends when you drop to 0 Hit Points, when another creature within 30 feet of you takes the Utilize or Influence action to call you back and succeeds on a DC 15 Wisdom (Medicine) or Charisma (Persuasion) check, or, if no one calls you back, at the next dawn. When it ends, Unbound ends too, and you gain one level of Exhaustion.
- **The Absorbed.** A creature that dies within 30 feet of you while you are Overtaken is absorbed into the Font: its body is gone, and only *Wish* or *True Resurrection* can return it to life.
- **The Ask.** Once per Long Rest, you can take a Magic action to ask the Font for anything *Wish* could do, except create objects or wealth. It answers: the effect happens, using no spell slot and carrying none of *Wish*'s stress. Asking costs you one level of Exhaustion, and then the DM rolls on The Due.
- **High Casting.** Whenever you cast a spell of level 6 or higher, including the one Unbound allows, you must make a Font saving throw, unaided, at the end of the turn, whether or not you drew on the Font to cast it.
- **The Dawn Wish.** At dawns of the DM's choosing (by default, one dawn a month), the Font casts *Wish* through you; this uses no spell slot and carries none of *Wish*'s stress. The DM chooses the wish, and it always concerns life: something restored, healed, grown, or spread. You experience it as a dream.
- **The Pulse.** While you have at least 1 Hit Point, you regain Hit Points equal to half your Physician level (round down) at the start of each of your turns.

**The Eruption.** The Font takes all of you. You die, and your body is gone into the Font. Only *Wish* or *True Resurrection* cast by another creature can return you to life, and the Font hears that request too: the DM rolls on The Due for the caster.

**The Due.** When the Font answers, it chooses the price, and it chooses one that fits. The DM rolls a d6:

- **1–3 — You.** The price lands on the one who asked. The Avatar is Overtaken. Any other Physician transforms into the Monster for 1 minute, whether or not they carry it, with its frenzy, and can't end the transformation early. A creature that isn't a Physician gains 2 levels of Exhaustion instead.
- **4–5 — The one it was for.** The creature that gained the most from the request drops to 0 Hit Points; if it already had 0 Hit Points, it fails one Death Saving Throw. If no other creature gained from it, the price lands on the one who asked, as for 1–3.
- **6 — Something that fits, for good.** The DM names one lasting price that fits the request (a memory, a name, a sense, a year, a bond) and the Font takes it. It doesn't come back.

**Acceptance (All Four Failed).** You stop fighting the Monster. You do not learn *Wish*. The following rules apply for the rest of your life:

- **The Monster for good.** Monster Form has no duration. You can transform, or return to your original form, as a Bonus Action as often as you like; Call It and Hold It Together no longer have limits. A failed Font saving throw from Surge no longer transforms you; the Font only takes its toll, as described in Surge.
- **At peace.** You no longer make the Struggle's saving throws, and the body doesn't pay when the transformation ends.
- **No frenzy.** In Monster Form you choose your own actions; you no longer have to attack, Grapple, or Shove a Hostile creature within your reach.
- **Fully grown.** You have the first two Overgrowth benefits and every benefit of the Shifting Balance.
- **Ready.** You gain Temporary Hit Points equal to twice your Physician level when you roll Initiative while in Monster Form, instead of when you transform.
- **Settled aura.** A creature Frightened by your Monstrous Aura can't be Frightened by it again until you finish a Long Rest.
- **Two bodies.** In Monster Form you can cast Physician spells of level 5 or lower using spell slots, except spells that restore Hit Points, and you can't use Healing Prowess (whatever Hold It Together says). You still can't draw on the Font or use Life-Fused Casting while transformed. The healer and the Monster take turns.
- **Apex.** When you would drop to 0 Hit Points while in Monster Form, you can make a Font saving throw. On a success, you drop to 1 Hit Point instead. Each time you succeed, the DC increases by 5 until you finish a Long Rest.

**Beyond.** When you accept the Monster, you gain the first benefit below. If your DM awards Epic Boons for play beyond level 20, you gain the next benefit each time you gain an Epic Boon, in order.

- **(1) One Body.** Monstrous Aura's regeneration also works in your original form, while you are Bloodied and have at least 1 Hit Point. In Monster Form, you keep your skill proficiencies in addition to Athletics and Intimidation.
- **(2) Deep Hunger.** In Monster Form, you can draw on the Font and use Life-Fused Casting, and you can cast Physician spells of any level using spell slots.
- **(3) Unbending.** In Monster Form, you have Immunity to the Charmed, Frightened, and Paralyzed conditions, and you have Advantage on Strength and Constitution saving throws.
- **(4) From Nothing.** If you die and your body isn't destroyed, you return to life in Monster Form at the next nightfall with 1 Hit Point and 3 levels of Exhaustion. Once this happens, it can't happen again until a year has passed.

new_spells.name: Ambulance
new_spells.higher: You can move one additional creature for each spell slot level above 2.
new_spells.text:
You take hold of a body that can't move itself and bring it out.

Choose one creature you can see within range that is willing or has the Incapacitated condition. An unwilling creature can make a Strength saving throw; on a success, the spell has no effect on it. Otherwise, the creature glides through the air to an unoccupied space you can see within range, up to 60 feet from where it started, on a surface that can bear its weight. This movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks, and the creature takes no damage from falling during it. If the creature has 0 Hit Points when the movement ends, it becomes Stable.

**Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot.** You can move one additional creature for each spell slot level above 2.

new_spells.name: Anaesthesia
new_spells.text:
You touch a willing creature and put it under.

The creature has the Unconscious condition for the duration. While the spell lasts it can't be woken by damage or by any other means, except by your touch (no action required) or by *Dispel Magic* or comparable magic. You have Advantage on Intelligence (Medicine) checks made to treat it while it is under, and it is unaware of its surroundings and remembers nothing of what is done to it.

new_spells.name: Convulsion
new_spells.higher: The damage increases by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 2.
new_spells.text:
You send a current through a creature's nerves and turn its own muscles against it.

Choose a creature you can see within range. It must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 3d8 Lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. On a failed save, the creature also drops one object it is holding, and it can't take Reactions until the end of its next turn.

A Construct or an Ooze automatically succeeds on this saving throw.

**Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot.** The damage increases by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 2.

new_spells.name: Cold Storage
new_spells.higher: The damage increases by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 3.
new_spells.components: V, S, M (a pinch of frost)
new_spells.text:
You take a body down to the cold that stops it, whether or not it agreed to go.

Choose a creature within your reach.

- **Willing, or Incapacitated and not hostile to you.** The creature has the Unconscious condition and enters stasis. For the duration it doesn't need air, food, or water; it can't be woken; it doesn't age; and its condition doesn't change. Every disease, poison, curse, and other ongoing effect on it is suspended, and time spent in stasis doesn't count against their durations. If the creature has 0 Hit Points, it is Stable and makes no Death Saving Throws while the spell lasts. The stasis ends if you touch the creature and end it (no action required), or if the creature takes damage.
- **Unwilling.** The creature must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 5d8 Cold damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. A creature reduced to 0 Hit Points by this damage doesn't die or make Death Saving Throws; it enters stasis as above until the spell ends.

**Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot.** The damage increases by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 3.

new_spells.name: Fugue
new_spells.higher: The damage increases by 5 for each spell slot level above 3.
new_spells.text:
You make a body feel everything that has already been done to it, all at once, and then leave it there.

Choose a creature you can see within range. It must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, it takes 10 Psychic damage, or 15 if it is Bloodied, and it is **vacant** for the duration. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and is not vacant.

A vacant creature is elsewhere. While it is vacant:

- It can't see or hear anything more than 10 feet away from it.
- It can't take Bonus Actions or Reactions, and on its turn it can move or take an action, but not both.
- It has Disadvantage on saving throws against the Charmed and Frightened conditions.

At the end of each of its turns, a vacant creature can repeat the saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success.

A creature that can't feel pain (a Construct, an Ooze, or an Undead) is unaffected by this spell; there is no record in it to read.

**Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot.** The damage increases by 5 for each spell slot level above 3.

new_spells.name: Defibrillation
new_spells.higher: Both the damage and the healing increase by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 5.
new_spells.components: V, S, M (two rods of copper, and diamonds worth 300+ GP, which the spell consumes if it returns a creature to life)
new_spells.text:
You send a single charge through several creatures at once, choosing what it does to each of them.

Choose up to five creatures you can see within range, no two of which are more than 30 feet apart. For each of them, choose one of the following effects:

- **Stop.** The creature must make a Constitution saving throw, taking 5d8 Lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
- **Start.** If the creature has 0 Hit Points, or has died within the last minute and its body is not missing any vital parts, it regains 3d8 Hit Points. A creature that had died returns to life; no more than one creature can return to life from a single casting.

**Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot.** Both the damage and the healing increase by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 5.

new_spells.name: Second Breath
new_spells.higher: When you cast this spell using a level 9 spell slot, the healing increases to 3d8 plus your spellcasting ability modifier.
new_spells.components: V, S, M (diamonds worth 300+ GP for each creature the spell returns to life, which the spell consumes)
new_spells.text:
You breathe for everyone around you, and they breathe again.

When you cast this spell, each creature of your choice in the Emanation regains Hit Points equal to 2d8 plus your spellcasting ability modifier. At the start of each of your turns for the duration, each creature of your choice in the Emanation that is Bloodied or has 0 Hit Points regains Hit Points equal to 2d8 plus your spellcasting ability modifier.

When you cast it, each creature of your choice in the Emanation that died since the start of your last turn returns to life, provided its body isn't missing any vital parts, and regains the Hit Points above. Each creature of your choice in the Emanation that has the Prone condition can stand up without spending any movement, and the Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Frightened, Paralyzed, Poisoned, and Stunned conditions end on each creature of your choice in the Emanation.

For the duration, each creature of your choice in the Emanation has Advantage on saving throws against the Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, and Stunned conditions.

**Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot.** When you cast this spell using a level 9 spell slot, the healing increases to 3d8 plus your spellcasting ability modifier.

new_spells.name: Arc
new_spells.higher: The damage increases by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 3.
new_spells.text:
You become the signal for an instant, and arrive.

Choose an unoccupied space you can see within 60 feet of yourself. You teleport to that space, traveling as a line of current between the two points. Each creature in a Line 5 feet wide between the space you left and the space you arrive in must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking 2d8 Lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

**Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot.** The damage increases by 1d8 for each spell slot level above 3.

data.name: Revelator
data.blurb: Half caster. The planes of the Plenum.

traits.value: *Choose 2:* Arcana, History, Insight, Medicine, Nature, Perception, Religion, or Survival
Light and Medium armor and Shields
*Choose A or B:* (A) Scale Mail, Shield, Spear, Light Crossbow and 20 Bolts, Cartographer's Tools, Priest's Pack, and 8 GP; or (B) 120 GP

rows.Class Features: Spellcasting, Vistas, Planar Strike, Planar Adept

features.name: Spellcasting
features.text:
You draw the power of the cosmos through yourself. See the rules on spellcasting for how spells work. The information below details how you use those rules with Revelator spells, which appear in the Revelator spell list later in the class's description.

**Spell Slots.** The Revelator Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

**Prepared Spells of Level 1+.** You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Revelator spells. *Cure Wounds* and *Protection from Evil and Good* are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Revelator levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Revelator Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Revelator spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

**Changing Your Prepared Spells.** Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one spell on your list with another Revelator spell for which you have spell slots.

**Spellcasting Ability.** Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Revelator spells.

**Spellcasting Focus.** You can use Cartographer's Tools, a token carried back from a spirit voyage, or a weapon with which you have proficiency as a Spellcasting Focus for your Revelator spells.

features.name: Vistas
features.text:
*Your glimpse of the greater cosmology awakened something within you, something you can now share with others.*

**Revelations.** Revelations are the planes you know. Each gives one Spirit Aspect (what a spirit of that plane can do, from level 3, when you can call one) and one Influence (what washes over a creature when you open a vista there). You start knowing two, the echoes of the world closest to home: the Hidden and the Ghostlands. Most Revelations are granted by your features by name; two features let you choose one (The Near Planes at level 5 and The Circuit at level 13). The full set is in the Cosmography later in the class's description. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one Revelation you chose with another you're eligible for. Revelations granted by features can't be replaced.

**Favor.** The planes answer you a number of times between rests: you have the number of Favors shown in the Favors column of the Revelator Features table, plus one for each plane you have walked (Soul's Journey). Opening a vista spends one, and so do the other features that tell you to spend a Favor. Healing costs more: an Influence that restores Hit Points or grants Temporary Hit Points costs two Favors. A Short or Long Rest brings every Favor back.

**Opening a Vista.** As a Bonus Action, you spend a Favor and open a vista to a Revelation you know, beside a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself (it can be you), and **let in an Influence**: that Revelation's Influence takes effect on the creature. From Revelator level 3, a vista can call a spirit instead (Visiting Spirit), and the spirit steps through beside the creature you chose. A plane needs a breath between answers: you can't open a vista to the same plane on two of your turns in a row.

**Influences.** Unless an Influence says otherwise, it lasts until the start of your next turn.

**Your Open Vista.** A vista stays open for 1 minute, until you open another one, until you dismiss it (no action required), or until you have the Incapacitated condition. While it's open, it sets the damage type of your Planar Strike; its Influence keeps its own, shorter clock (above).

When a vista or its Influence calls for a saving throw, the DC equals your spell save DC. Whenever a Revelator feature uses your spell save DC or spell attack modifier, it means the ones you use for Revelator spells.

**One Bonus to AC.** Bonuses to AC from Revelator Influences and Aspects don't stack with each other; a creature uses the highest.

**Your First Two Revelations.** Every Revelator starts with these. The rest are in the Cosmography, after the pathways, and the Cosmography Summary table compares them all.

**The Hidden.**
- ***Spirit Aspect: Fae Trickster.*** *Fey.* It has Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks, and in place of its other action it can take the Magic action to cast *Minor Illusion* without components. **Command:** *Misdirect.* One creature within 5 feet of the spirit must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.
- ***Influence: Merriment.*** The creature can end one Charmed or Frightened condition on itself, and has Advantage on its next saving throw.
- ***Planar Strike.*** Psychic damage.

**The Ghostlands.**
- ***Spirit Aspect: Shade.*** *Undead.* It has Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks, it can take the Hide action in addition to its other action, and it can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch. **Command:** *Go Ahead.* It moves up to twice its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks and takes the Hide action, and you see through its eyes until the start of your next turn.
- ***Influence: Gloom.*** Choose an ally or an enemy; shadow falls on either. On an ally, the next attack roll against it has Disadvantage. On an enemy, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have Disadvantage on its next attack roll.
- ***Planar Strike.*** Necrotic damage.

features.name: Planar Strike
features.text:
When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can replace one of the attacks with a Planar Strike: a melee spell attack against a creature within 5 feet of yourself, or a ranged spell attack against a creature within 60 feet of yourself. You can make only one Planar Strike on each of your turns. Planar Strike is magical but isn't a spell.

**Damage.** On a hit, the target takes the dice shown in the Planar Strike column of the Revelator Features table, plus your Wisdom modifier once for each of those dice (so 2d12 adds twice your Wisdom modifier).

**The Plane's Power.** The damage is the type the Cosmography gives your open vista's Revelation. If you have no vista open, it's Force damage.

**One Hand for the Plane.** You need a free hand, or a hand holding your Spellcasting Focus, to make a Planar Strike. On a turn when you make one, you can't also make the extra attack of the Light property or the Nick mastery.

**Your Weapons.** A weapon you have proficiency with is a Spellcasting Focus for you, so you can make a Planar Strike with a Spear in one hand and a Shield on the other arm. A Planar Strike is made only with the Attack action on your own turn, so you make Opportunity Attacks with the weapon. A Light Crossbow reaches targets more than 60 feet away, and it works where magic is suppressed.

features.name: Planar Adept
features.text: You learn two cantrips of your choice from the Revelator spell list. *Guidance* and *Message* are recommended. The chosen cantrips count as Revelator spells for you, and Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for them. Whenever you gain a Revelator level, you can replace one of these cantrips with another cantrip from the Revelator spell list.

features.name: The Border Ethereal
features.text:
*You branch out into the tangible spirit of all things, the Ethereal Plane.*

You know the Revelation of the Border Ethereal, the Ethereal Plane's near reach: the curtain a ghost steps through, a step aside from the room you stand in. It's the plane you cross most often. Revelators call it the Veil when they speak of it as a barrier: the thin wall between the world and every other plane.

**Veilsight.** You can see into the Border Ethereal within 60 feet of yourself, and you can speak with ghosts and spirits as if you shared a language. This covers any Undead, Fey, or Elemental, and any creature that is in the Border Ethereal.

features.name: Ethereal Stride
features.text:
*You learn to step through the Veil in the body, a stride at a time.*

As a Bonus Action, you can spend a Favor to step into the Border Ethereal until the end of your turn. While there, you can move through creatures and objects as if they were Difficult Terrain, and creatures on the Material Plane can't see you unless they can see into the Ethereal. You can affect and be affected only by things in the Ethereal Plane. Ethereal Stride doesn't open a vista.

**Guiding.** You can bring one willing creature you touch. It enters the Border Ethereal with you, moves with you, staying within 5 feet of you, and returns when you do.

You return to the Material Plane when the stride ends. If you would arrive inside an object or creature, you are shunted to the nearest unoccupied space and take 1d10 Force damage. The same applies to any creature you guide.

features.name: Visiting Spirit
features.text:
When you open a vista, you can **call a spirit** instead of letting in an Influence. A spirit of that plane steps through into an unoccupied space next to the creature you chose. It uses the Visiting Spirit stat block, with that Revelation's Spirit Aspect.

You can have one spirit at a time, and it doesn't require Concentration. It stays for 1 hour, until it drops to 0 Hit Points, until you call another spirit, until you dismiss it (no action required), or until you have the Incapacitated condition. If a spirit you called drops to 0 Hit Points, you can't call any spirit again until you finish a Short or Long Rest; you can still let in Influences.

**A Guest, Not a Soldier.** The spirit is an ally to you and your companions, but it doesn't fight: it can't make attack rolls, and it doesn't deal damage. It has no turn of its own; it acts on yours. At any point on each of your turns, you can move it up to its Speed (no action required), and it takes the Help action or, if you choose, the Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Hide, Search, or Utilize action. If its Aspect gives it a Reaction, you decide when it takes it.

**Commanding the Spirit.** While the spirit is within 100 feet of you, you can command it with a Bonus Action, and the vista that calls it also commands it; letting in an Influence doesn't. When commanded, the spirit uses its Aspect's power at once. The command comes on top of its action: a commanded spirit still moves and Helps that turn.

**Speaking Across.** While the spirit is within 100 feet of you, you can communicate with it telepathically. As a Bonus Action, you can see through its eyes and hear what it hears until the start of your next turn, gaining any special senses it has.

> **Visiting Spirit**
>
> *Small or Medium creature (your choice) of the type its Spirit Aspect names, Neutral*
>
> **AC** 12 + your Wisdom modifier
>
> **HP** 5 + your Revelator level
>
> **Speed** 30 ft.
>
> | STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
> |---|---|---|---|---|---|
> | 10 | 14 | 10 | 10 | 12 | 10 |
>
> **Saving Throws** use your saving throw bonuses
>
> **Senses** Darkvision 60 ft.; Passive Perception 11
>
> **Languages** understands the languages you know
>
> ***Aspect.*** It gains the Spirit Aspect of the Revelation that called it, including its creature type. Effects that depend on creature type, such as *Protection from Evil and Good* or *Banishment*, treat the spirit as that type. When an Aspect calls for a saving throw, the DC equals your spell save DC.

> **For the DM: The Spirit Is a Guide**
>
> A Visiting Spirit helps, scouts, and carries, and it isn't there to take hits for the party. Play it like a familiar: enemies swat it when it's in their way or when it's obviously helping, and otherwise ignore it.

features.name: Revelator Pathway
features.text: You gain a Revelator subclass of your choice: the pathway that called you on your spirit voyage. The Bridge, the River of Life, the Mountain, the River of Death, and the Tree are detailed after this class's description. Each pathway is a road that begins beside the world and ends in the Outer Planes. At level 3 you learn its earth end, the place in the Deep Ethereal where the road begins. At level 7 you learn its Inner Circuit plane, and at level 15 its Far Circuit plane (The Planes by Tier). Your earth end is the plane you know best. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your pathway's features that are of your Revelator level or lower; the Tree also has one at level 5.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Revelator levels 8, 12, and 16.

features.name: The Near Planes
features.text:
*You reach past the Border to the planes that feed the world: life, its emptying, the far Ethereal, and the four elements.*

You learn one Revelation of your choice from the Cosmography's Near Planes: Positive Energy, Negative Energy, the Deep Ethereal, or the Elemental Planes.

features.name: The Crossings
features.text:
*The spirit and soul meet the mind.*

You know the Revelation of the Astral, the sky the spirit crosses on its way out of the world.

**Wayfinder.** You can't become lost by magical means, and you always know the direction to the nearest portal, curtain, or color pool on the plane you're on. You have Advantage on Intelligence checks to recall lore about the planes and their inhabitants.

features.name: Guide's Hand
features.text:
*Your experience allows you to help others traveling with you.*

**Many Travelers.** When you use Ethereal Stride, you can guide a number of willing creatures equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one), each of whom you touch or who is within 5 feet of a creature you guide.

**Hold the Threshold.** When a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself fails a Death Saving Throw, or suffers a failure by taking damage while it has 0 Hit Points, you can take a Reaction and spend a Favor, calling on the Ghostlands, to turn one of those failures into a success. This doesn't open a vista.

features.name: Reach Beyond
features.text:
*You can push through to the deepest, most well-guarded parts of reality, if you're brave enough.*

Once per Long Rest, as a Bonus Action, you can open a vista without spending a Favor, reaching instead for any Revelation in the Cosmography that you don't know. You can do this even when you have no Favors left. A reach within the Cosmography draws no Attention (defined below).

**Past the Map.** Instead, you can reach past the Cosmography, toward what it leaves out: a single layer or realm, such as the efreet's city in the Plane of Fire or a god's hall in Valhalla; a ruler and their court, such as an archfey, Yama with his scribe, the Jade Emperor in his palace, the lord of the deepest circle of the Nine, or a demon lord in their layer; or what lies between and beyond, such as the dead gods adrift in the Astral, the crossroads of the Middle World, or the Far Realm. The vista both calls a spirit and lets in an Influence, and the Influence affects every creature of your choice within 30 feet of the vista. The DM decides what comes through from that place's nature, taking the Cosmography's Aspects and Influences as the yardstick: the nearest plane's, bent toward the place you reached. By default, use the nearest plane's Aspect and Influence as written, dressed in the look and voice of the place you reached. A reach past the map always draws Attention.

**The Strain.** The further you reach, the more passes through you, and your body has to bear it. Reaching past the Cosmography forces you to make a Constitution saving throw: DC 15 for a particular layer or realm, or DC 20 for a god, a ruler, or the Far Realm. On a failed save, you take 6d6 Psychic damage (10d6 against DC 20); on a successful save, you take half as much damage. If you fail the DC 20 save, your spirit also takes the long way home: you can't spend Favors until you finish a Short or Long Rest. You can still Strike, cast spells, and command whatever came through. Either way, the vista opens, and you get what you reached for.

**Attention.** A power of that place notices you, and you have its Attention. The DM decides what the power guards and what it wants from you; it might call in a favor, pay you a visit, set you a test, or name a debt. By default, it asks one service of you before you gain your next level, in proportion to what you reached for: a message carried, a guest sheltered, a thing returned to its place. Powers act from their own nature, which isn't always kind. The debt is the cost, and it is paid in story, not in Favors. While you have a power's Attention, using Reach Beyond on its place again deepens the relationship rather than drawing new Attention.

features.name: Soul's Journey
features.text:
*Your soul never forgets your travels, for better and for worse.*

A Revelation you know is **walked** once you have been to that plane in the body, spent at least a Long Rest there, and come back. How you got there doesn't matter: by portal, by another's spell, by being taken, or by waking up there. The plane cares only that you stayed, and what it does to those who stay is the lesson (see "What the Walk Costs," in "Walking the Planes" after the Cosmography). A plane you walked before you knew its Revelation is walked the moment you learn it.

**Walking the Middle World.** Being born in the world and living in it doesn't count as walking the Middle World. Its Revelation is the world seen whole, from the axis at its center, and you walk it the way you walk any plane: you climb to the axis in the body (up the slopes above a sacred mountain, or to the crossroads where every road meets), spend a Long Rest there, and come back down. The DM decides where the way up begins and what the climb asks of you. By default, it begins at the nearest sacred mountain or great crossroads, a few days' travel away, and the climb is one hard journey with one real danger on the way up.

A walked plane knows you: each plane you have walked adds one Favor to your pool, up to a number of extra Favors equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

**The First Voyage.** When you gain this feature, one Revelation you know counts as walked: the place your first voyage took you, back when you walked the Wheel in spirit.

**The Hard Roads.** Seven places on the Wheel are walked by almost no one, and walking one leaves a mark for life. They're described in "Walking the Planes," after the Cosmography.

features.name: Wider Vistas
features.text: When you let in an Influence, you can choose a second creature (it can be you) you can see within 30 feet of the vista. The Influence affects both creatures, and it costs no more Favors than it would for one. If the Influence offers a choice, as Gloom does between an ally and an enemy, you choose separately for each creature.

features.name: The Circuit
features.text:
*You understand the shape of the world.*

You learn one Revelation of your choice from the Near Planes, the Inner Circuit, the Borderlands, or the Dominions (The Planes by Tier). It can be the Inner Circuit plane of another pathway. The Far Circuit is beyond you until The Circuit Made Whole. Before The Circuit Made Whole, The Circuit is the only way to learn:

- **The Borderlands:** the planes in the shadow of the Dominions: Arcadia and the House of Song on either side of the Seven Heavens, Gehenna beside the Nine Circles, Pandemonium beside the Abyss. The roads pass through them (the River of Death rises in Pandemonium and runs past Gehenna, and the Bridge crosses Arcadia on its way down from the House of Song), but no pathway stops there. By now you know the roads through them anyway.
- **The Dominions:** one quiet corner of each great realm. They are the Sphere of the Moon in the Seven Heavens, Cocytus in the Nine Circles, and the Seven Gates of the Abyss.

features.name: Ethereal Wayfarer
features.text:
*Your body learns to stay on the far side of the Veil as long as your spirit does.*

**Long Stride.** Ethereal Stride can last up to 1 minute (Concentration, as if it were a spell) instead of until the end of your turn, and you can end it as a Bonus Action. Creatures you guide stay in the Border Ethereal with you for the duration, and any of them can return to the Material Plane as a Bonus Action.

**Etherealness.** You can cast *Etherealness* without expending a spell slot. When you do, you can bring a number of willing creatures within 10 feet of you equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: The Body Follows
features.text:
*Your body can now go wherever your spirit has been.*

You can cast *Plane Shift* without expending a spell slot or Material components. It can take you only to the Material Plane or to a plane whose Revelation you know, and you arrive exactly where you intend. You can't use this casting to send an unwilling creature to another plane. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Ethereal Sight
features.text:
*Nothing on either side of the Veil hides from you for long.*

Your Veilsight extends to 120 feet, and you and your spirits can see Invisible creatures and objects within that range.

features.name: Epic Boon
features.text: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Spell Recall is recommended.

features.name: The Circuit Made Whole
features.text:
*You understand why the world is the shape that it is.*

You gain the following benefits.

**Every Revelation.** You know every Revelation in the Cosmography.

**Old Acquaintance.** You can use Reach Beyond twice per Long Rest.

**Favor in the Moment.** When you roll Initiative, you regain up to two Favors.

**Spirit of Totality.** When you call a spirit, you can call the Spirit of Totality instead: a spirit of no one plane, sent by all of them together. It is still your one spirit, and it uses the Visiting Spirit stat block. It counts as every creature type, and it understands and speaks every language, but it has no Aspect's traits. When you command it, it uses the commands of two different Spirit Aspects of your choice; it can't choose a command that depends on an Aspect's trait: Element's Way, which needs a chosen element, or Moonlight, which needs the light of the Sphere of the Moon's Lantern. While it's with you, each time you hit with your Planar Strike you can choose its damage type from any plane's.

**Walked Whole.** The hard roads add up. For every two hard roads you have walked, Favor in the Moment regains one more Favor. If you have walked all seven, you also have Advantage on the Constitution saving throw for the Strain of Reach Beyond.

> **Playing a Revelator**
>
> You see the world's other rooms, and you've been to some of them. The planes answer a few times between rests, and a Short Rest brings every Favor back, so a party that stops to breathe gets a generous Revelator. Your spirit doesn't fight: it's a guide, a scout and a voice in the right ear, so give it a job every turn. Ethereal Stride is your exit and your shortcut: step through the wall, and bring a friend. Out of a fight, you talk with ghosts, see into the Border Ethereal, and know the planes better than anyone at the table; when the party wonders what lives behind a door, you have often seen the other side of it. Every Revelation you learn is another door, and another story about what came through it.

subclasses.name: The Bridge
subclasses.lead:
*Endure What You Are Commanded to Endure*

A long stretch of paved road, better kept in some places than others. It comes down from the House of Song's workshops, through Arcadia's orchards and the gears of the Celestial Bureaucracy, and ends at a bridge over the River of Death in Acheron, where the road runs out onto Acheron's endless battlefield. The Wheel draws the whole bridge in Acheron. In the Plenum the bridge is longer than the picture: its near end, the Bridgehead, stands in the Deep Ethereal beside the world. A Revelator of the Bridge starts there and walks the road both ways: back up it to the Celestial Bureaucracy (level 7), and at last across the bridge into Acheron (level 15). A Revelator of the Bridge stands in the way: they Weigh one foe, take the blows meant for their friends, and are mended by the blows they take.

features.name: Bridge Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Revelator level specified in the Bridge Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared. They count as Revelator spells for you. Called to Account, at level 3, isn't a spell; it is described below the table.

| Revelator Level | Spell |
|---|---|
| 3 | Called to Account |
| 5 | *Zone of Truth* |
| 9 | *Slow* |
| 13 | *Stoneskin* |
| 17 | *Geas* |

**Called to Account.** As a Bonus Action, you can expend a spell slot of level 1 or higher to call one creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself to account. It makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, for 1 minute, it has Disadvantage on attack rolls against creatures other than you, and it can't willingly move to a space more than 30 feet away from you. You must maintain Concentration on it as if on a spell. It ends early if you make an attack roll against a creature other than the target, if you cast a spell that targets an enemy other than the target, if an ally of yours damages the target, or if you end your turn more than 30 feet away from the target.

features.name: The Bridgehead
features.text: You know the Revelation of the Bridgehead, the near end of the last bridge.

features.name: The Scale
features.text:
Whenever you open a vista, of any plane and for any purpose, you can also Weigh one creature you can see within 30 feet of the vista that isn't your ally. It stays Weighed for 1 minute, and only one creature can be Weighed at a time. Weighing the same creature again just starts the minute over.

While a creature is Weighed:

- **The Scale Tips.** *When it deals damage to you or one of your allies:* the scale tips, and it takes 1d6 Force damage. An attack or effect that damages several of you at once tips the scale only once.
- **Slowed.** *The first time the scale tips:* its Speed decreases by 10 feet until the Weighing ends.
- **Fed by the Blow.** *When damage it deals to you tips the scale, and you still have at least 1 Hit Point:* you regain Hit Points equal to your Wisdom modifier. You must be the one who takes the damage; damage you take for an ally through Bear the Verdict counts. Once this happens, it can't happen again until the start of your next turn.
- **No Hiding.** *Always:* you know the direction to it while it's on the same plane as you, and it gains no benefit from the Invisible condition against you or your spirits.

features.name: Bear the Verdict
features.text:
You gain training with Heavy armor, and you have Advantage on saving throws you make to avoid being moved or knocked Prone. When an ally within 5 feet of you takes damage, you can take a Reaction, after the damage is rolled, to take that damage instead, as if it had been dealt to you: your Resistances, Vulnerabilities, and Immunities apply to it, and the ally's don't. Any other effect of the attack still applies to the ally. If the damage came from a Weighed creature, the scale still tips.

On this pathway the plane comes through your guard more than your hands: your Planar Strike adds your Wisdom modifier no more than twice, however many dice it rolls.

features.name: The Celestial Bureaucracy
features.text: You know the Revelation of the Celestial Bureaucracy.

features.name: The Paperwork
features.text: You can read the seals, stamps, and forms of any office, court, or bureaucracy, in any language: you know whether a document is genuine, what office issued it, and what it lets its bearer do. After an hour in a government office, a customs house, or a court's antechamber, you know whom to see, in what order, and what each of them will want.

features.name: Lockstep
features.text: Your spirit stands where you can't. While your spirit is within 100 feet of you, you can use Bear the Verdict when an ally within 5 feet of your spirit takes damage, as if you were in the spirit's space. You take the damage, not the spirit.

features.name: A Heavier Scale
features.text: The scale's weight shifts onto the Weighed. Each time it tips, the creature also has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the end of its next turn (tips don't stack: one Disadvantage at a time).

features.name: Keeper of the Crossing
features.text: You know the toll owed at any bridge, ford, ferry, gate, or customs post you come to, and whether you're being cheated. Toll-keepers, ferrymen, and bridge-wardens take you for one of their own: they'll tell you who has crossed ahead of you in the last week, and how they paid.

features.name: Acheron
features.text: You know the Revelation of Acheron. You've crossed.

features.name: Endure the Sentence
features.text: When you take damage from the Weighed creature through Bear the Verdict, you have Resistance to it.

features.name: Found Wanting
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, you pronounce judgment on a Weighed creature whose scale has tipped during this Weighing (its slowed Speed shows it), wherever it is on the same plane as you. It makes a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, it takes 6d10 Force damage, loses Concentration, and is banished to an empty stretch of the road until the end of its next turn. It then returns to the space it left (or the nearest unoccupied one). When it returns, it doesn't know the location of any creature it can't see. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

> **Playing a Revelator of the Bridge**
>
> You stand in the narrow place: Weigh the foe that worries you, stand beside the friend it wants, and take the blow for them. Out of a fight you read every seal and form, and you know which clerk to see. When the party needs papers, you go to the customs house.

subclasses.name: The River of Life
subclasses.lead:
*Heal Through the River That Never Ends*

The River of Life rises in Eden, runs through Elysium, and pours out into the sea at the edge of the world. There, in the Deep Ethereal, the Maelstrom turns it back toward its source, and that whirlpool is where a River Revelator's road begins. River Revelators are healers: water rises among the wounded, the spirits of wells and rivers talk to them, and the dying are shown the way across.

features.name: River of Life Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Revelator level specified in the River of Life Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared. They count as Revelator spells for you.

| Revelator Level | Spell |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Bless* |
| 5 | *Aid* |
| 9 | *Mass Healing Word* |
| 13 | *Control Water* |
| 17 | *Mass Cure Wounds* |

features.name: The Maelstrom
features.text: You know the Revelation of the Maelstrom.

features.name: Wellspring
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, you can spend two Favors to set down a Wellspring: the Maelstrom fills a spring in one 5-foot square of a surface a creature could stand on (the ground, a floor, stairs, a deck, or the surface of water; not a wall or ceiling) that you can see within 60 feet of yourself, and the square can be in a creature's space. A creature is in the Wellspring if its space includes that square and it's on the surface or in the water within 5 feet below it; a creature flying above it isn't. Its water doesn't hinder movement or block sight. You can have one Wellspring at a time; setting down a new one closes the old. The Wellspring isn't a vista: setting it down doesn't count toward a plane's breath, and your vistas open and close as usual while it runs.

**The Water Heals.** When a Bloodied creature of your choice starts its turn in the Wellspring, or enters it during its turn by any means, it regains Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature regains Hit Points this way only once per turn, and the Wellspring arriving under a creature isn't the creature entering it. While you have the Incapacitated condition, the water heals you and your allies, and no one else. A creature at 0 Hit Points that isn't dead is Bloodied, so the water lifts anyone fallen in it, you included, at the start of their turn, before they roll a Death Saving Throw: they regain the Hit Points and are no longer Unconscious (they're still Prone).

**The Water Follows.** At the start of each of your turns, you can move the Wellspring up to 30 feet along a continuous path you can see over surfaces it can be set down on, into a creature's space if you like (no action required). It moves before the water heals anyone, so if it flows under you, it can heal you as your turn starts.

**Striking or Casting Feeds the River.** The Wellspring runs through the end of the turn you set it down, and through the end of each later turn of yours on which, while an enemy is still in the fight, you make a Planar Strike against an enemy (hit or miss) or cast a Revelator spell (a cantrip counts). An enemy is in the fight while it's Hostile and still able and willing to fight; a captive, or a creature that has surrendered or fled, isn't. The DM says when no enemy is left. At the end of any other turn of yours, the Wellspring runs dry and closes. While you have the Incapacitated condition, the Wellspring doesn't run dry and you can't move it. If you're still Incapacitated after the water has healed at the start of your turn, it closes then. It also closes when no enemy is left in the fight, after 1 minute, if you end your turn more than 60 feet from it, or when you dismiss it (no action required).

**Between Fights.** When you set the Wellspring down while no enemy is in the fight, each Bloodied creature of your choice within 10 feet of it regains Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and then the Wellspring closes. You can set one down this way once, and you can't do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Water-Taken
features.text: You can breathe water, and you have a Swim Speed equal to your Speed. You always know which way the nearest open water lies, and whether water you can see is safe to drink; if it's fouled (poison, disease, a corpse upstream), you know which way the fouling came from. The spirits of springs, pools, wells, and rivers know you as one of the water's own: they start Friendly toward you, and with your Veilsight they'll tell you who has drunk, bathed, or drowned there, and what else they've seen.

features.name: Elysium
features.text: You know the Revelation of Elysium.

features.name: The River Rises
features.text: Once per Short or Long Rest, when you make a Planar Strike against an enemy while your Wellspring is open, you can let the Wellspring break after the attack roll, hit or miss (no action required). Each creature of your choice within 10 feet of the Wellspring regains 2d6 Hit Points (3d6 at Revelator level 11, 4d6 at Revelator level 17); roll once for all of them. They don't need to be Bloodied, and this doesn't count as anyone's healing from the water this turn. You can do this on the turn you set the Wellspring down. Then the Wellspring closes.

features.name: Clean Water
features.text: Once per Long Rest, you can spend 10 minutes at a well, spring, cistern, or stream and open the River of Life into it. The source is cleansed of poison and disease and stays clean for 24 hours: the whole well, spring, or cistern, or 30 feet of a stream below where you stand. Water that runs on past that can be fouled again. Cleansing the water doesn't cure anyone who already drank it.

features.name: Water Finds Its Level
features.text: Once per Long Rest, when you set down a Wellspring or as a Bonus Action while one is open, you can let the water find its level. Each Bloodied creature of your choice within 10 feet of the Wellspring regains Hit Points until it's no longer Bloodied: it has half its Hit Point maximum (round down) plus 1. A creature at 0 Hit Points is no longer Unconscious (it's still Prone). No creature loses Hit Points, and Temporary Hit Points don't count toward the level and aren't changed. This works between fights too: the water heals first, then finds its level. A creature it lifts is no longer Bloodied, so the water doesn't heal it on its turns until it's Bloodied again.

features.name: What the Water Took
features.text: Once per Long Rest, you can put your hand in a body of water and name a creature or object lost in it, or in the same river, lake, or stretch of coast, within the last year. You learn where it lies, or where it came ashore. If it was a person, you also learn whether they drowned, were taken, or walked out on their own feet, and if they were taken, by what.

features.name: Eden
features.text: You know the Revelation of Eden.

features.name: The Far Shore
features.text:
When a creature that you can see, or a creature in your Wellspring, dies, you can tell it the way across (no action required), unless you have the Incapacitated condition. Its spirit goes where its people's dead go, across or home to its family as an ancestor, but it doesn't linger as a ghost, and it can't be made into Undead unless it chose that in life, as a lich does or a guardian sworn to a tomb. This doesn't prevent a spell that returns it to life, and *Speak with Dead* still works on its body. This works on an Undead too: if you tell it the way across, it doesn't rise or re-form again, unless it chose undeath in life. The DM says whether an Undead chose undeath. An Undead that escapes at 0 Hit Points instead of being destroyed, such as a vampire turning to mist, hasn't died.

**Held on This Shore.** Once per Short or Long Rest, when damage would reduce a creature of your choice in your Wellspring from 1 or more Hit Points to 0 and wouldn't kill it outright, the water can catch it (no action required): it's left with Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus instead. This works while you have the Incapacitated condition; the water catches only you and your allies then.

> **Playing a River Revelator**
>
> You keep people standing. Your Wellspring is a spring you set down and move around the fight: every turn a Bloodied friend starts in it, the water heals them, and it lifts the fallen before they roll. It runs as long as the fight does and you keep striking or casting. From level 7, once a rest, you let it break over everyone near it; from level 11, once per Long Rest, you let the water find its level and lift every Bloodied friend near it back above half; and from level 15, once a rest, it catches a friend who would drop in it. Out of a fight you know whether a well is safe, clean a town's water, find what a river took, and show the dying the way across. In any village, they ask you about the well.

subclasses.name: The Mountain
subclasses.lead:
*Excellence in Everything*

The heart of the earth: the unmoving stone playground of the gods, rising from Asphodel to Svarga with the Middle World on its slopes. A Revelator of the Mountain is good at a little of everything, and keeps a spirit that turns aside the blows meant for friends.

features.name: Mountain Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Revelator level specified in the Mountain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared. They count as Revelator spells for you.

| Revelator Level | Spell |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Guiding Bolt* |
| 5 | *Enhance Ability* |
| 9 | *Haste* |
| 13 | *Fabricate* |
| 17 | *Legend Lore* |

features.name: The Foot of the Mountain
features.text: You know the Revelation of the Foot of the Mountain.

features.name: Arete
features.text: You have one extra Favor (two from Revelator level 11). From level 5, when The Near Planes gives you a Revelation to choose, you can replace a Revelation you chose when you finish a Short Rest, not only a Long Rest.

features.name: Everything Is Next Door
features.text: You gain proficiency with one tool of your choice and learn one language of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can exchange the tool, the language, or both for others: the Mountain lends; it doesn't give.

features.name: Hundred Hands
features.text: When a creature you can see attacks an ally within 5 feet of your spirit, and your spirit is within 100 feet of you, you can take a Reaction to give the attack roll Disadvantage. Your spirit catches the blow, but it takes nothing for it.

features.name: The Middle World
features.text: You know the Revelation of the Middle World.

features.name: High Places
features.text: When you spend 10 minutes at the top of a hill, tower, mast, or other high place with a wide view, you see the lay of the land for a day's travel around: the roads and rivers, the settlements and their smoke, and anything that's wrong in it (a burned farm, an army's dust, a place where the Veil has worn thin). The DM describes what's there to be seen. You can do this once per Long Rest.

features.name: Many-Turning
features.text: When you open a vista to let in an Influence, your spirit can take on that Revelation's Spirit Aspect, including its creature type, instead of its own, without spending another Favor. Its current Hit Points and Hit Point maximum don't change. It keeps the new Aspect until you change it again, and it can change only once for each vista you open.

features.name: Twofold Vista
