features.text: When you open a vista to let in an Influence, you can also let in the Influence of a second Revelation you know through the same vista, on the same creature or another within 30 feet of the vista. The second Influence costs what it would cost on its own: one more Favor, or two more if it restores Hit Points or grants Temporary Hit Points (Vistas). The first Revelation is your open vista, for your Planar Strike's damage; both count as opened this turn, so neither can be opened on your next turn.

features.name: Guest-Friendship
features.text: You always know the customs of hospitality where you are: what to bring, what to refuse, where to sit, and what not to say. You never give offense by accident. While you're someone's guest and have eaten under their roof, you have Advantage on Charisma checks to persuade them.

features.name: Excellence
features.text: Healing and Temporary Hit Points from your Influences increase by your Proficiency Bonus, and an Influence that lasts until the start of your next turn lasts until the end of your next turn instead.

features.name: Svarga
features.text: You know the Revelation of Svarga, the mountain's summit.

features.name: Seen from the Summit
features.text: Once per Long Rest, when you spend an hour studying a person, a place, or an institution (a court, a guild, a city's government, a family), the DM tells you three true things about how it works: who holds it up, what it fears, and what it wants.

features.name: Apotheosis
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, you regain a number of Favors equal to half the number in your Favors column (round up), and for 1 minute you have Advantage on attack rolls for your Planar Strikes. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

> **Playing a Revelator of the Mountain**
>
> You know a little about everything and change your mind more freely than other Revelators, and your spirit stands beside your friends to turn blows aside. Out of a fight you climb something high and read the country, and you know the customs of any house that takes you in. Whatever the question, you've been somewhere next door to the answer.

subclasses.name: The River of Death
subclasses.lead:
*Carry Whoever Pays the Fare*

In myth the Styx is the river under the world, circling the land of the dead; on the Wheel it rises in Pandemonium's howling caverns and runs down through the Lower Planes. A Revelator knows it as the River of Death, and knows it rises in the Source Mists, in the Deep Ethereal, and starts there. A Revelator of the River of Death keeps company with the dead: two spirits at a time, a crowd of unpaid shades let into a fight, and at last the Ferryman himself.

features.name: River of Death Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Revelator level specified in the River of Death Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared. They count as Revelator spells for you. The Ferryman's Sleep, at level 9, isn't a spell; it is described below the table.

| Revelator Level | Spell |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Bane* |
| 5 | *Blindness/Deafness* |
| 9 | The Ferryman's Sleep |
| 13 | *Confusion* |
| 17 | *Modify Memory* |

**The Ferryman's Sleep.** As a Magic action, you can expend a spell slot of level 3 or higher and touch a willing creature to lay it down as if dead. You can also do this without expending a spell slot if you take 10 minutes longer, as with a Ritual. For 1 hour, the creature appears dead to outward inspection and to spells used to determine its status. It has the Blinded and Incapacitated conditions, its Speed is 0, it has Resistance to all damage except Psychic damage, and it has Immunity to the Poisoned condition.

features.name: The Source Mists
features.text: You know the Revelation of the Source Mists.

features.name: The River Below
features.text: You have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet, or your Darkvision's range increases by 30 feet if you already have it. You can't become lost underground, and you always know the direction to the nearest water that flows beneath the ground.

features.name: The Fare
features.text: When you call a spirit, you can keep the spirit you already have instead of dismissing it, letting you have two Visiting Spirits at once. Both act on your turn. When you command your spirits, only one of them uses its Aspect. If you call a spirit while you have two, you choose which one leaves. The Spirit of Totality (level 20) counts as both of your spirits.

features.name: Blood in the Pit
features.text: *Your spirits remember the taste of blood.* Once per turn, when you hit a creature with Planar Strike, you can expend one of your Hit Point Dice. Roll it, and add the number rolled to the damage.

features.name: Asphodel
features.text: You know the Revelation of Asphodel.

features.name: Last Rites
features.text: When you see a corpse, you know how long ago it died, and whether its spirit has gone on, lingers nearby, or is being kept from going. You know the funeral customs of any people whose dead you have seen buried, and the dead of those peoples take you seriously: you have Advantage on Charisma checks with spirits of the dead.

features.name: The Unpaid
features.text: When you open a vista, you can let in the Unpaid instead of calling a spirit or letting in an Influence: the shades who couldn't afford the fare. The vista can open on any Revelation you know and spends a Favor as usual, and that plane is your open vista. They fill a 15-foot-radius area centered on the vista for 1 minute. The area is Difficult Terrain for your enemies, and an enemy that starts its turn there must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or take 1d6 Psychic damage (2d6 from Revelator level 11, 3d6 from level 15) and have Disadvantage on its next attack roll. The Unpaid stay for the full minute even if the vista closes. Letting them in doesn't dismiss your spirits, and they don't count against your limit of spirits, but only one crowd of the Unpaid can be in the world at a time.

features.name: Full Passage
features.text: When you command your spirits, both can use their Aspects. When you use Blood in the Pit, you can expend two Hit Point Dice instead of one.

features.name: Tartarus
features.text: You know the Revelation of Tartarus.

features.name: The Ferryman
features.text:
The Ferryman's skiff slides out of the mist. As a Bonus Action, you call the Ferryman for 1 minute. At the end of each of your turns while he's present, he can carry up to three willing creatures within 30 feet of you, teleporting each to an unoccupied space you can see within 60 feet of yourself. The Charmed and Frightened conditions end on any creature he carries; it forgets what charmed or frightened it. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

> **Playing a Revelator of the River of Death**
>
> You travel with company: two spirits at once, one to scout or carry while the other stands by a friend. Out of a fight you read a corpse at a glance, and the dead take you seriously. When someone hasn't gone on, the family sends for you.

subclasses.name: The Tree
subclasses.lead:
*Fight With the Dead at Your Back*

The Tree stands with its roots in the Wells, where the Deep Ethereal meets the Lower World (the Plenum's lower realms, where most peoples' dead go), its trunk through the Middle World, and its branches through Valhalla, Limbo, and Eden. A Revelator of the Tree climbs it with the dead at their back: a fighter in the front rank, armed and trained by the spirits who chose them, who changes places with their own spirit in the press and gets up again when they fall.

features.name: Tree Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Revelator level specified in the Tree Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared. They count as Revelator spells for you. Light of the Hall, at level 9, and the Reaching Root, at level 13, aren't spells; they are described below the table.

| Revelator Level | Spell |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Heroism* |
| 5 | *Magic Weapon* |
| 9 | Light of the Hall |
| 13 | The Reaching Root |
| 17 | *Tree Stride* |

**Light of the Hall.** As a Magic action, you can expend a spell slot of level 3 or higher to shine with the light of the hall of the slain. It is a 30-foot Emanation from you that lasts for 1 minute, and you must maintain Concentration on it as if on a spell. While in it, you and your allies each deal an extra 1d4 Radiant damage when you hit with a weapon or an Unarmed Strike.

**The Reaching Root.** As a Bonus Action, you can expend a spell slot of level 4 or higher to raise a root of the world tree from a surface in an unoccupied space you can see within 60 feet of yourself. It lasts for 1 minute, and you must maintain Concentration on it as if on a spell. When it rises, make a melee spell attack against a creature within 30 feet of the root. On a hit, the target takes 4d8 Bludgeoning damage and is pulled up to 30 feet toward the root; if the target is Huge or smaller, it has the Grappled condition (escape DC equal to your spell save DC). The root can grapple only one creature at a time, and you can make it release a Grappled creature (no action required). On each of your later turns, you can take a Bonus Action to repeat the attack against a creature within 30 feet of the root. For each slot level above 4, the root can grapple one more creature at a time.

features.name: The Wells
features.text: You know the Revelation of the Wells.

features.name: Tyr's Hand
features.text:
*The bravest of the Aesir has one hand, and he put the other where it went on purpose.* You gain proficiency with Martial weapons and a Fighting Style feat of your choice (see the *Player's Handbook*). Your training includes Weapon Mastery: you can use the mastery properties of two kinds of Simple or Martial weapons of your choice, and whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kinds you chose. When you attack with a weapon whose mastery property you can use, you can use your Wisdom modifier instead of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls.

On this pathway the plane comes through your weapon more than your hands: your Planar Strike adds your Wisdom modifier no more than twice, however many dice it rolls.

features.name: Into the Fray
features.text: When you command your spirit, you can swap places with it if it's within 30 feet of you. You and the spirit each teleport into the other's space.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.text: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Valhalla
features.text: You know the Revelation of Valhalla.

features.name: The Mead-Bench
features.text: Soldiers, mercenaries, sailors, and any other company that drinks together before a fight take you for one of their own after an evening in their company. They'll share their rumors, their billets, and their grievances with you, and in any town with a garrison or a harbor, someone among them can tell you where the fighting is and who is paying for it.

features.name: Rise Each Dawn
features.text: When you drop to 0 Hit Points and don't die outright, your spirit, if you have one, can fall in your place: it drops to 0 Hit Points (so you can't call another until you finish a Short or Long Rest), and you drop to 1 Hit Point instead. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Feather Cloak
features.text: *Freyja lent her feather cloak to Loki, and a Sakha shaman's coat is hung with iron feathers for the same flight.* When you command your spirit, you can teleport to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of it, wherever it is within 100 feet of you, instead of swapping places with it. While you're within 5 feet of your spirit, creatures can't make Opportunity Attacks against you.

features.name: Limbo
features.text: You know the Revelation of Limbo.

features.name: Rise Together
features.text:
Rise Each Dawn recharges when you finish a Short or Long Rest. When an ally you can see within 30 feet of yourself drops to 0 Hit Points and doesn't die outright, you can take a Reaction to spend Rise Each Dawn on that ally instead, if you have a spirit: your spirit falls in the ally's place, and the ally drops to 1 Hit Point.

> **Playing a Revelator of the Tree**
>
> You fight up close, with a weapon you trust and your spirit at your shoulder, and you can change places with it. Out of a fight, any company that drinks together before a battle takes you for one of their own. When the door has to be opened, you're usually first through it.

multiclass.gains: Hit Point Die, proficiency in one skill of your choice from the Revelator's skill list, and training with Light and Medium armor and Shields
multiclass.text: You must have a Wisdom score of 13 or higher. Gain the following traits from the Core Revelator Traits table: Hit Point Die, proficiency in one skill of your choice from the Revelator's skill list, and training with Light and Medium armor and Shields. Gain the Revelator's level 1 features, which are listed in the Revelator Features table. For multiclass spell slots, add half your Revelator levels (round up). If you have levels in another class and fewer than five Revelator levels, you can call a spirit with Visiting Spirit only once, and you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

cosmography.lead:
**The Wheel.** The Wheel is one diagram, printed in every *Cosmographia* from Lisbon to Lahore. Earth sits at the center with the elements around it. Above are the seven planetary spheres, the fixed stars, and the Empyrean. Hell's funnel is inside the earth. Euphonia's cosmographers read the same diagram for alignment: a plane's height runs from Good at the top to Evil at the bottom, and its bearing runs from Law on one side to Chaos on the other. Planes on opposite sides of the Wheel are opposite in height, in bearing, or in both. *The Setting* (The Plenum, The Wheel) has the table of what stands where.

**Whose names.** The planes below go by their names on the Wheel, because it is the map the learned share. Where an entry gives a direction after a plane's name, such as Asphodel (Evil), that is where the Wheel puts the plane. It is a position on the diagram and passes no judgment on the plane or on the dead who go there.

**The Plenum.**

**Core-book names.** *Plane Shift*, *Gate*, and the *Monster Manual* name the planes as the core books do. Some planes go by a different name here (the Middle World is the Material Plane, Asphodel is Hades, the earth ends are regions of the Ethereal Plane); every other plane in the Cosmography keeps its core-book name. The full table is The Planes, by Their Core Names, in this book's appendices.

This is the complete list of Revelations. Each gives a Spirit Aspect (what a spirit of that plane can do, and the power it uses when you command it), an Influence, and the damage your Planar Strike deals while a vista to that plane is open. Class and pathway features name the Revelations they grant; The Near Planes (level 5) and The Circuit (level 13) choose from here. The Cosmography Summary table, after the Revelator at a Glance, compares them all.

**Where they are.** Every Revelation is a place you can walk (Soul's Journey) or reach with *Plane Shift*. The Outer Planes are where the Wheel puts them. The planes below are the ones the Wheel doesn't place, in the order you learn them: the two Echoes, the five earth ends in pathway order, and the Middle World.

- **The Hidden.**
- **The Ghostlands.**
- **The Bridgehead.**
- **The Maelstrom.**
- **The Foot of the Mountain.**
- **The Source Mists.**
- **The Wells.**
- **The Middle World.**

rows.Command: *Unmake:* strip a Resistance
