groups.name: The Echoes
groups.lead: The Hidden and the Ghostlands, the two Revelations every Revelator starts with, are printed in full in the Vistas feature (level 1).

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: Fae Trickster
parts.text: *Fey.* It has Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks, and in place of its other action it can take the Magic action to cast *Minor Illusion* without components. **Command:** *Misdirect.* One creature within 5 feet of the spirit must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

parts.label: Influence: Merriment
parts.text: The creature can end one Charmed or Frightened condition on itself, and has Advantage on its next saving throw.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: Psychic damage.

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: Shade
parts.text: *Undead.* It has Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks, it can take the Hide action in addition to its other action, and it can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch. **Command:** *Go Ahead.* It moves up to twice its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks and takes the Hide action, and you see through its eyes until the start of your next turn.

parts.label: Influence: Gloom
parts.text: Choose an ally or an enemy; shadow falls on either. On an ally, the next attack roll against it has Disadvantage. On an enemy, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have Disadvantage on its next attack roll.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: Necrotic damage.

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: Ghost
parts.text: *Undead.* It can move through creatures and objects as if they were Difficult Terrain, taking 1d10 Force damage if it's inside an object at the end of your turn. **Command:** *Through the Wall.* It carries an object of up to 10 pounds, or a spoken message of up to twenty-five words, through walls and doors to a place or creature it can reach this turn.

parts.label: Influence: Step Aside
parts.text: The next time the creature takes damage, the damage is halved.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: Force damage.

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: Assessor
parts.text: *Construct.* Up to three times per calling, when a creature within 10 feet of it speaks a deliberate lie, it knows, and it can tell you. **Command:** *Entered in the Record.* Choose one creature within 30 feet of the spirit that has damaged you or one of your allies since the end of your last turn. The next attack roll one of your allies makes against it before the start of your next turn has Advantage.

parts.label: Influence: Verdict
parts.text: If the creature is Weighed, its scale tips twice. Each tip deals the scale's 1d6 Force damage and counts as a tip for Slowed and A Heavier Scale; a Verdict isn't damage the creature deals, so it doesn't trigger Fed by the Blow. If it isn't, it becomes Weighed (as The Scale, in the Bridge, describes, even if you don't have that feature) and its scale tips once. Either way, you take 1d6 Force damage: a verdict costs the judge something too. If Wider Vistas lets the Influence affect two creatures, choose one of them to be Weighed; the other takes 1d6 Force damage instead.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: Force damage.

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: River Spirit
parts.text: *Elemental.* It has a Swim Speed of 30 feet, and it can breathe water and air. **Command:** *Rising Water.* The water carries one creature within 5 feet of the spirit that is willing or has 0 Hit Points up to 15 feet along the ground or across water, ignoring Difficult Terrain and without provoking Opportunity Attacks. If your Wellspring is open and no one else is in it, it can instead carry the creature the same way up to 30 feet into the Wellspring, where the water can heal it when its turn starts.

parts.label: Influence: Renewal
parts.text: The creature ends one of these conditions on itself: Blinded, Deafened, Poisoned, or Prone. It can then move up to half its Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: Cold damage.

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: Hundred-Handed
parts.text: *Giant.* Its carrying capacity is that of a Huge creature with a Strength of 20, and it can carry a willing Medium or smaller creature at its full Speed. **Command:** *Heave.* It shoves one creature within 5 feet of it, which must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed 5 feet away or have the Prone condition (your choice).

parts.label: Influence: Aegis
parts.text: The creature gains a +2 bonus to AC. The first creature to hit it while the Influence lasts must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: Bludgeoning damage.

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: Passenger
parts.text: *Undead, or the passenger's own type with the DM's agreement.* It remembers the way back along any road it has traveled, and by touching a corpse it can tell you how that person died. **Command:** *Hush.* One creature within 5 feet of the spirit must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be unable to take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

parts.label: Influence: Forgetting
parts.text: The creature makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, it loses Concentration and can't take Reactions.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: Psychic damage.

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: Root-Warden
parts.text: *Fey.* It can speak with plants. **Command:** *Roots.* One Large or smaller creature within 5 feet of the spirit must succeed on a Strength saving throw or have a Speed of 0 until the start of your next turn.

parts.label: Influence: Urd's Thread
parts.text: Roll a d6. The creature adds the number rolled to, or subtracts it from, its next D20 Test; you choose which after seeing the d20 roll.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: Force damage.

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: Radiant Mote
parts.text: *Celestial.* It sheds Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 feet. **Command:** *Warm Light.* One creature within 5 feet of the spirit that has 0 Hit Points and isn't dead becomes Stable.

parts.label: Influence: Surge of Life
parts.text: The creature regains Hit Points equal to 1d8 plus your Wisdom modifier.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: Radiant damage.

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: Hollow
parts.text: *Undead.* Light dies near it: Bright Light within 10 feet of the spirit is Dim Light, and Dim Light there is Darkness. **Command:** *Wither.* One creature within 5 feet of the spirit must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be unable to regain Hit Points until the start of your next turn.

parts.label: Influence: Drain
parts.text: The creature makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it takes 2d6 Necrotic damage, and while the Influence lasts it can't regain Hit Points, its Regeneration doesn't function, and it has Disadvantage on the next Strength or Constitution check or saving throw it makes. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: Necrotic damage.

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: Mist-Walker
parts.text: *Elemental.* It has a Fly Speed of 30 feet (it can hover). **Command:** *Ferry.* It teleports up to 15 feet, and it can take one willing Medium or smaller creature within 5 feet of it along, to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of where it arrives.

parts.label: Influence: Through the Curtain
parts.text: A willing creature teleports up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. Or it steps behind the curtain instead: until the start of its next turn, it has the Invisible condition and Resistance to all damage. Both end after the first attack roll against it is resolved.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: Force damage.

parts.label: The Elements
parts.text: When you open this vista, choose an element: Air (Lightning), Earth (Acid), Fire (Fire), or Water (Cold). The vista's Influence, its spirit, and your Planar Strike all carry that element while the vista is open.

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: Elemental
parts.text: *Elemental.* It has Resistance to its element's damage and gains a trait. *Air:* it has a Fly Speed of 30 feet (it can hover) and can carry a Small creature. *Earth:* it has a Burrow Speed of 20 feet and can't be moved against its will. *Fire:* it sheds Bright Light in a 20-foot radius and sets unattended flammable objects alight at a touch. *Water:* it has a Swim Speed of 30 feet and puts out fires within 10 feet of itself. **Command:** *Element's Way.* *Air:* one creature within 5 feet of it must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed 10 feet away. *Earth:* the ground in a 10-foot square it can see becomes Difficult Terrain until the start of your next turn. *Fire:* one creature within 5 feet of it must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or have Disadvantage on its next attack roll. *Water:* it douses the flames on one ally within 5 feet of it, or that ally ends the Prone condition on itself.

parts.label: Influence: Elemental Edge
parts.text: The creature's weapon hits and Planar Strikes deal an extra 1d6 damage of the element's type.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: The element's damage type.

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: Astral Dreamer
parts.text: *Celestial.* It has a Fly Speed of 30 feet (it can hover). **Command:** *Dream Message.* It speaks a message of up to twenty-five words into the mind of a creature you have met that is on the same plane; the creature can answer the same way.

parts.label: Influence: Speed of Thought
parts.text: The creature's Speed doubles, and it gains a Fly Speed equal to its Speed. If it is aloft when the Influence ends, it floats down 60 feet a round until it lands and takes no damage from the fall.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: Psychic damage.

groups.name: The Inner Circuit
groups.lead: Each pathway grants one of these planes at level 7: the Bridge, the Celestial Bureaucracy; the River of Life, Elysium; the Mountain, the Middle World; the River of Death, Asphodel; the Tree, Valhalla. Any of them can also be learned with The Circuit at level 13.

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: The Blessed Dead
parts.text: *Celestial.* Allies within 10 feet of it can't have the Charmed or Frightened condition. **Command:** *Rest Easy.* One ally within 5 feet of it ends the Charmed, Frightened, or Poisoned condition on itself.

parts.label: Influence: Peace
parts.text: The creature gains Temporary Hit Points equal to twice your Wisdom modifier, and it can end one of these conditions on itself: Charmed, Frightened, Poisoned, or Stunned.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: Radiant damage.

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: Einherjar
parts.text: *Celestial.* It can take the Help action to help an ally attack a creature within 30 feet of the spirit. **Command:** *War Cry.* One ally within 30 feet that can hear it has Advantage on its next attack roll before the end of its next turn, and gains Temporary Hit Points equal to your Wisdom modifier.

parts.label: Influence: One More Blow
parts.text: The creature, an ally, can immediately take a Reaction to make one attack with a weapon or an Unarmed Strike. If it has 0 Hit Points, it first regains Hit Points equal to your Wisdom modifier. Let in on a creature at 0 Hit Points, One More Blow is a healing Influence and costs two Favors; otherwise it costs one.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: Slashing damage.

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: Gray Shade
parts.text: *Undead.* It has Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks in Dim Light or Darkness. **Command:** *Gray.* One creature within 5 feet of it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be unable to have Advantage on D20 Tests until the start of your next turn.

parts.label: Influence: Apathy
parts.text: The creature makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, it can take an action or a Bonus Action on its turn, not both, and it can't take Reactions.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: Necrotic damage.

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: Clerk
parts.text: *Construct.* It recalls perfectly anything it has seen or heard since you called it, and it can copy a page of writing in a minute. **Command:** *Filed.* One ally within 5 feet of it gains a +2 bonus to AC until the start of your next turn.

parts.label: Influence: Certainty
parts.text: When the creature rolls a 9 or lower on a d20 for anything but a Death Saving Throw, it can treat the roll as a 10.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: Force damage.

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: The Pilgrim
parts.text: *Every type at once.* It counts as every creature type, for better and worse. It understands and speaks every language, and it has Advantage on saving throws against spells and other magical effects. **Command:** *Concordance.* One creature within 5 feet of it can't be moved against its will until the start of your next turn.

parts.label: Influence: Balance
parts.text: The creature's D20 Tests can't have Advantage or Disadvantage, and it can't be moved against its will.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: Force damage.

groups.name: The Borderlands
groups.lead: Before level 20, only The Circuit teaches these four.

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: Howler
parts.text: *Aberration.* Hostile creatures within 10 feet of it have Disadvantage on saving throws to maintain Concentration. **Command:** *Howl.* Each creature of your choice within 10 feet of it must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or have the Deafened condition until the start of your next turn.

parts.label: Influence: Howling
parts.text: The wind takes the creature. If it's hostile, it makes a Strength saving throw; on a failed save, it is pushed up to 15 feet in a direction you choose and has the Prone condition. If it's willing, it is carried up to 30 feet in a direction you choose without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: Thunder damage.

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: Furnace
parts.text: *Fiend.* It has Resistance to Fire damage, and it sheds Bright Light in a 10-foot radius. **Command:** *Heat.* One creature within 5 feet of it must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or have Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.

parts.label: Influence: Cold Bargain
parts.text: The creature's next attack roll has Advantage, and if it hits, it deals an extra 4d6 Fire damage. The creature takes 1d6 Fire damage when the Influence takes effect.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: Fire damage.

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: Harmonious Guard
parts.text: *Celestial or Construct (your choice when you call it).* Once per round, when an ally within 5 feet of it fails a saving throw, it can take a Reaction to let the ally reroll the save; the ally must use the new roll. **Command:** *Keep Time.* One ally within 5 feet of it adds 1d4 to its next saving throw before the start of your next turn.

parts.label: Influence: Harmony
parts.text: The creature and one other ally within 10 feet of it each add 1d4 to their attack rolls and saving throws.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: Force damage.

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: Twin Worker
parts.text: *Celestial or Construct (your choice when you call it).* It is proficient with every kind of Artisan's Tools. When it takes the Help action, two creatures gain the benefit instead of one. **Command:** *Lend a Hand.* One ally within 5 feet of it has Advantage on its next ability check before the end of its next turn.

parts.label: Influence: Shared Labor
parts.text: The creature and one ally within 5 feet of it each have Advantage on their next attack roll or ability check.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: Bludgeoning damage.

groups.name: The Dominions
groups.lead:
These Revelations reach the quiet corners, never the seats of power; calling on the Jade Emperor's palace, the deepest circle of the Nine, or a demon lord's layer takes Reach Beyond, and Attention always follows.

A Dominion's spirit is a local. A Revelator who calls a devil from Cocytus has signed no contract and owes no one, and the devil reports to no lord. It comes because the Revelator knows where it lives, the way a naturalist knows where a hawk nests.

revelations.name: The Seven Heavens: The Sphere of the Moon

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: Lantern of the Moon
parts.text: *Celestial.* It sheds Bright Light in a 20-foot radius. Creatures in that light gain no benefit from the Invisible condition, and a Shapechanger there shows its true form to you. **Command:** *Moonlight.* One ally in its light ends the Blinded or Deafened condition on itself, or ends one curse on itself; a creature can be freed of a curse this way only once per Long Rest.

parts.label: Influence: Moon's Mercy
parts.text: The creature regains 2d8 Hit Points and ends one curse or one of these conditions on itself: Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Frightened, Paralyzed, Poisoned, or Stunned. While the Influence lasts, it has Resistance to Necrotic damage.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: Radiant damage.

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: Stygian Devil
parts.text: *Fiend (Devil).* It has Resistance to Cold damage and is unharmed by Extreme Cold. **Command:** *Chill.* One creature within 5 feet of it must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or have its Speed halved and Disadvantage on Dexterity saving throws until the start of your next turn.

parts.label: Influence: The Hush
parts.text: The creature makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it can't speak, so it can't cast spells with Verbal components, and it has the Deafened condition.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: Cold damage.

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: Wanderer of the Gates
parts.text: *Fiend (Demon).* It knows where any portal it can see leads. **Command:** *Step Through.* It teleports up to 30 feet, or it swaps places with a willing creature within 30 feet of it.

parts.label: Influence: Relocate
parts.text: If the creature is willing, it teleports up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. If it's hostile, it makes a Charisma saving throw; on a failed save, you teleport it up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: Force damage.

groups.name: The Far Circuit
groups.lead: Each pathway grants one of these planes at level 15: the Bridge, Acheron; the River of Life, Eden; the Mountain, Svarga; the River of Death, Tartarus; the Tree, Limbo. No other pathway reaches them before level 20.

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: Beast Spirit
parts.text: *Beast.* It has Advantage on Wisdom (Perception) and Wisdom (Survival) checks, and it can follow a creature's trail by scent for up to a day after the creature passed. **Command:** *Flank.* The next attack roll an ally makes before the start of your next turn against a creature within 5 feet of the spirit has Advantage.

parts.label: Influence: The Garden's Plenty
parts.text: The creature's Speed increases by 10 feet, and it has Advantage on attack rolls against any creature that one of its allies is within 5 feet of.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: Slashing damage.

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: Gandharva
parts.text: *Celestial.* One of the musicians of Indra's court. Music follows it; it can play any instrument. **Command:** *The Gandharva's Song.* One creature within 5 feet of it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have Disadvantage on Wisdom saving throws until the start of your next turn.

parts.label: Influence: Valor
parts.text: Each of the creature's weapon or spell hits deals an extra 1d8 Radiant damage.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: Radiant damage.

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: Flux
parts.text: *Aberration.* It can take the shape of any Tiny object, and as a Utilize action it can reshape unworked earth or stone in a 5-foot Cube. **Command:** *Unmake.* One creature within 5 feet of it loses Resistance to one damage type of your choice until the start of your next turn.

parts.label: Influence: Reshape
parts.text: The creature gains Resistance to one damage type of your choice for 1 minute. A creature can benefit from only one Reshape at a time.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder damage, your choice each time you hit.

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: Jailer
parts.text: *Fiend.* It knows if a creature within 30 feet of it is under a magical compulsion or imprisonment. **Command:** *Hold.* One Large or smaller creature within 5 feet of it must succeed on a Strength saving throw or have the Grappled condition (escape DC equals your spell save DC); while Grappled this way, it can't teleport or leave the plane it's on. The Jailer can have only one creature Grappled at a time.

parts.label: Influence: Bound
parts.text: The creature makes a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, it has the Restrained condition.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: Bludgeoning damage.

parts.label: Spirit Aspect: Iron Soldier
parts.text: *Construct.* It holds the line: it can't be moved against its will or knocked Prone, and each ally within 5 feet of it has a +1 bonus to AC. **Command:** *Close Ranks.* One ally within 5 feet of it can't be moved against its will or knocked Prone until the start of your next turn.

parts.label: Influence: Shield Wall
parts.text: The creature gains a +2 bonus to AC, and each ally within 5 feet of it gains a +1 bonus to AC.

parts.label: Planar Strike
parts.text: Piercing damage.

data.name: Danae
data.blurb: Cha full caster. The fae, and the Hidden’s courts.

traits.value: *Choose 2:* Arcana, Deception, History, Intimidation, Nature, Persuasion, Religion, or Sleight of Hand

*Choose 2:* Calligrapher's Supplies, Cartographer's Tools, Gaming Set, Glassblower's Tools, Herbalism Kit, Jeweler's Tools, Mason's Tools, Musical Instrument, Navigator's Tools, Painter's Supplies, Weaver's Tools, or Woodcarver's Tools
*Choose A or B:* (A) Leather Armor, 2 Daggers, Quarterstaff, Arcane Focus (crystal), Explorer's Pack, and 16 GP; or (B) 50 GP.

rows.Class Features: The Elder Cycles, The Door Opens

features.name: Spellcasting
features.text:
Danae learn their spells through dream. Each night, the Hidden speaks to them deep in sleep, and when they wake, they know what magic to prepare.

**Cantrips.** You know three cantrips of your choice from the Danae spell list. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one of your cantrips with another cantrip of your choice from the Danae spell list. When you reach Danae levels 4 and 10, you learn another cantrip of your choice from the Danae spell list, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Danae Features table.

**Cantrip Damage.** When you cast a Danae cantrip that rolls only one damage die, add your Charisma modifier to the damage it deals to one target. Once your cantrips roll two or more dice (from level 5), the extra dice take its place.

**Spell Slots.** The Danae Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

**Prepared Spells of Level 1+.** You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose four level 1 spells from the Danae spell list. The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Danae levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Danae Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional spells from the Danae spell list until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

If another Danae feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Danae spells for you.

**Changing Your Prepared Spells.** Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of the spells there with other Danae spells for which you have spell slots.

**Spellcasting Ability.** Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your Danae spells.

**Spellcasting Focus.** You can use an Arcane Focus, or any tool from the Danae's tool list or your subclass's tool that you have proficiency with, as a Spellcasting Focus for your Danae spells: the work of your hands is where the Hidden's weaving of what comes to pass comes through. This book calls that weaving the Wyrd, the old English word; every people that spins or weaves has its own.

features.name: The Sight
features.text: You see the Hidden's layer over the world. You can see thresholds between worlds within 30 feet of yourself. (A threshold is a fixed place where the waking world touches another realm, such as the Hidden; the DM decides where they lie. By default, any place the Hidden are known to gather, such as a fairy hill, a great tree or a ford, holds one, and a border village has one within a day's walk.) You also know when a creature or an object you can see within 30 feet of yourself is under an illusion or a shape-changing effect, or has the Fey creature type, and whether it is a Hidden creature. You gain proficiency in the Insight and Perception skills (if you already have proficiency in either, choose another skill from the Danae's skill list), and you know Sylvan, the Hidden's own speech.

features.name: Warps
features.text:
Once you see the true shape of reality, you can bend its space.

As a Bonus Action, you warp a 5-foot Cube you can see within 60 feet of yourself into one of the shapes below. The warp lasts for 1 minute, until you dismiss it (no action required), or until you unravel it. You can make a number of warps equal to the number in the Warps column of the Danae Features table, and you regain all expended warps when you finish a Short or Long Rest. A warp you keep in place through a rest stays expended until it ends.

Warps don't require Concentration, and they don't choose sides: a warp affects every creature alike, unless its season says otherwise. Warps can't overlap: no part of a warp's space can be part of another warp's space. A warp is a visible thing: a creature that can see its space can tell that the space is wrong, though not what the warp does until it's inside. When a warp calls for a saving throw, the DC equals your spell save DC.

- **Stretch.** Every foot of movement inside the warp costs 2 extra feet. This doesn't stack with Difficult Terrain: inside a Stretch, each foot costs 3 feet either way.
- **Gate.** Your Gates are linked in a chain, in the order you made them; the last leads back to the first. A Gate must rest on a surface. A creature that moves into a Gate of its own will steps out of the next one in the chain, in its space or the nearest unoccupied space to it. Stepping through costs no movement and doesn't trigger the Gate the creature arrives in. A Gate doesn't send on a creature put into it any other way (moved against its will, or caught in a Gate made on it). When you make a Gate and have no other Gate in place, you make two, linked, for one warp: put the second on another surface you can see within 60 feet of yourself. Later Gates join the chain. If a Gate ends, the chain closes around the gap: the Gate before it leads to the Gate after it. A Gate left alone leads nowhere.

**On a Creature.** You can make a warp in a space where creatures are standing. Each creature in the Cube makes a Dexterity saving throw.

- **On a success,** the creature moves to the nearest unoccupied space outside the warp. This move doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks, and the warp doesn't affect the creature.
- **On a failure,** the creature stays where it is, and the warp doesn't affect it yet. If it is still in the warp at the start of its next turn, it is treated as having just entered: the warp and its season (see The Half) affect it then. If it leaves the warp or is moved out before then, they don't.

You can make a warp on a creature only once on each of your turns.

**Unraveling.** Some features let you unravel a warp. To unravel a warp, you either end one of your warps that is in place or expend one you haven't used yet; either way, the feature takes effect. A feature that tells you to expend a warp uses one you haven't used yet.

**Magic and Travel.** Warps are magical effects: *Detect Magic* reveals them, and *Dispel Magic* ends one as if it were a level 1 spell. Passing through a Gate, or any warp that takes a creature from one space to another without crossing the space between, is teleportation; a push or a fall is not. A creature can travel through your warps this way (Gates, and a Crossing Danae's Doors and Seams) only once per turn.

**Arriving by Teleport.** A creature teleported into a warp's space enters the warp, just as if it had walked in, but a Gate it arrives in doesn't send it on. If the creature couldn't stand in that space (it's solid stone, or the warp hangs over a drop), it arrives in the nearest unoccupied space where it can stand instead, outside the warp. A creature going through a Crossing Danae's Doors follows the Doors' own rules.

features.name: Denial
features.text:
You refuse the outcome others would have for you, and change things accordingly.

When a creature you can see hits you with an attack roll while you aren't wearing Medium or Heavy armor or using a Shield, you can take a Reaction and unravel one of your warps to deny it. You gain a bonus to AC against that attack, which can turn the hit into a miss: +3, rising to +4 at Danae level 9 and +5 at level 17.

How reality rearranges itself follows your nature, and from level 3 your subclass:

| | The blow is denied by |
|---|---|
| Before level 3 | a flicker of the Hidden: a scent of rain, a wrong-colored light, and the blow goes wide |
| Binding | a thread that catches the weapon an inch short |
| Changing | a hidden current pulling at them |
| Crossing | the air folding, and the blow arriving somewhere you aren't |
| Naming | a word: the blow is named a miss |
| Shaping | stone or crystal rising across the skin |

features.name: The Half
features.text:
You lean toward one half of the Hidden's year. Choose the light half or the dark half. The light half's seasons are spring and summer; the dark half's, autumn and winter. Your Half is yours, not the calendar's: it never changes with the date or the tide.

**Seasons.** You learn your half's two seasons. When you make a warp, you can give it one season you know. A creature that enters a seasoned warp for the first time on a turn, or starts its turn there, is subject to its season, making any saving throw against your spell save DC. A creature is subject to the season of only one of your warps per turn: the first that takes it.

| Half | Season | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Light | **Spring** | *Strength saving throw.* On a failed save, you move the creature up to 15 feet horizontally in a direction of your choice. A willing creature can instead teleport up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. |
| Light | **Summer** | The creature takes 1d6 Fire damage. Creatures you choose when you make the warp are immune. The damage increases by 1d6 when you reach Danae levels 5 (2d6), 11 (3d6), and 17 (4d6). |
| Dark | **Autumn** | *Wisdom saving throw.* On a failed save, choose one: the creature has the Charmed condition, with you as the charmer, until the start of its next turn, or it has Disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes before the end of your next turn. |
| Dark | **Winter** | *Constitution saving throw,* made only when the creature enters the warp, not when it starts its turn there. On a failed save, the creature's Speed is 0 and it can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn. |

features.name: Flee
features.text:
When you take damage and are Bloodied afterward but not at 0 Hit Points (whether or not you were Bloodied before), you can take a Reaction to step half out of the world. Unravel one or more of your warps, in place or not yet used (a subclass's warps count). You're **Away** for 1 minute, and you gain Temporary Hit Points: your Danae level, plus 5 for each warp you unraveled. A level 2 Danae who unravels three warps gains 2 + 15 = 17. These Temporary Hit Points replace any you already have.

Being Away ends early when you have none of its Temporary Hit Points left, when you have the Incapacitated condition, or when you end it (no action required). While you're Away, you keep your mind and your magic: you cast spells and keep Concentration as normal, and in addition:

- **Half Here.** Attack rolls against you have Disadvantage.
- **Flicker.** Once on each of your turns, you can teleport up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space you can see (no action required).

**Readjust.** When you stop being Away, you come back not quite when you left: at the end of the current turn, you can teleport up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Danae Subclass
features.text: Your method shows itself: the way the Hidden works through you. You gain a Danae subclass of your choice: Binding, Changing, Crossing, Naming, or Shaping. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Danae levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Danae level or lower.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Danae levels 8, 12, and 16.

features.name: Fae Weaving
features.text:
The Wyrd flows through your hands, giving you what you need in the moment.

Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can weave fae material into the world with a tool you have proficiency with from the Danae's tool list or your subclass's tool. You create up to a number of nonmagical objects equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Each must be something that tool could make, Medium or smaller, not a consumable (food, a potion, an oil, a poison, or the like) and not ammunition, and worth no more than 10 GP × your Danae level. A tool that makes nothing under the crafting rules weaves the small things of its trade: a Gaming Set weaves dice, cards, and boards; a Musical Instrument, strings, reeds, and pipes; Thieves' Tools, picks, keys, and wires. The objects are real and work as the real thing, but anyone who handles one feels that it is strange. They come undone when you next finish a Long Rest or when you use this feature again.

**Fairy Gold.** The objects are fairy gold: any of them turns to dross when it changes hands for value, and none can be used as a Material component that has a cost.

features.name: The First Cycles
features.text:
Your warps can be 5-foot or 10-foot Cubes, and you learn two more shapes:

- **Tilt.** You choose which way is down within the warp when you make it. A creature that enters the warp for the first time on a turn, or starts its turn there, makes a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, it is thrown 10 feet that way, stopping if it strikes something solid, and has the Prone condition; a creature thrown upward then falls. A willing creature can instead walk through the warp with down where you chose it: up a wall or across a ceiling, as if it were floor. When the warp ends, down is down again, and a creature left in the air falls.
- **Pocket.** The warp is bigger inside than out. A creature enters it by moving into its space; a creature that fails its save when the Pocket is made on it (On a Creature) is inside at the start of its next turn, if it hasn't left. A creature inside can leave by spending 5 feet of movement to appear in an unoccupied space next to it. Up to eight Medium creatures fit inside it, whatever its size (a Small or Tiny creature counts as one, a Large creature as four, and a Huge or larger creature can't enter; nor can a creature that wouldn't fit beside those already inside), and anything inside has Total Cover against anything outside, and the reverse. When a Pocket ends, each creature inside it appears in the nearest unoccupied space.

**The Way Back.** You learn the way home: you regain the use of Flee when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Reading the Season
features.text: The Hidden settles in you, and you begin to read people as it reads them, by their weather. As a Bonus Action, choose a number of creatures you can see within 30 feet of yourself, up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). The DM tells you each one's temper and what lies under it (Tempers, in "The Hidden, in the rules"). Each of them is **read** by you for 1 hour. You have Advantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks against a creature you've read, and on Charisma (Deception, Intimidation, or Persuasion) checks against it that play to its temper. Other features of yours refer to creatures you've read.

features.name: Open Book
features.text: You can cast *Detect Thoughts* without expending a spell slot a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. A creature you've read has Disadvantage on its saving throw against the spell.

features.name: The Door Ajar
features.text: While you're Away, when you teleport with Flicker, you can leave a warp of any shape you know in the space you left. It follows every rule for your warps (it can't overlap another, it lasts 1 minute, it can carry a season you know, and it counts as one of your warps in place), except that it costs no Bonus Action and no warp.

features.name: Thresholds
features.text: Your Sight expands, allowing you to see paths into the Hidden Realm itself. You can spend 1 minute at a threshold you can see with The Sight to open it, casting *Plane Shift* without expending a spell slot or needing its Material component. The spell targets you and up to eight willing creatures, it can take you only to or from the Hidden, and you arrive at the threshold's other side. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Loop
features.text:
You learn another warp shape:

- **Loop.** The warp's edges meet. When a creature tries to leave the warp by any means, moving or teleporting, or is moved out of it against its will, it makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, it steps back in from the opposite side. The movement it spent leaving is lost (as is any spell slot or use the teleport cost), and it can't try to leave that Loop again until its next turn. A creature that succeeds isn't affected by that Loop again.

features.name: The Middle Cycles
features.text: You learn the other half's two seasons. A warp still holds only one season.

features.name: Name the Season
features.text: As a Magic action, you can choose a creature you've read that you can see within 30 feet of yourself. It makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, you turn its temper to another season of your choice for 1 hour; its mood follows, its attitude toward you shifts one step in the direction you choose (Hostile to Indifferent, or Indifferent to Friendly, or the reverse), and it doesn't know it was touched. On a successful save, it knows something tried. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: The Hill
features.text:
You learn another warp shape:

- **Hill.** Time inside the warp runs at the hill's pace. A creature that starts its turn inside the warp must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or, until the start of its next turn, its Speed is halved, it can't take Reactions, and on its turn it can take either an action or a Bonus Action, not both. When a creature leaves a Hill after failing a save against it, it doesn't remember what happened while it was inside.

features.name: Blasé
features.text:
The Hidden doesn't let its own be led. You have Immunity to the Charmed and Frightened conditions.

**Of the Court.** The Hidden know you now for what you are. A Hidden creature that remembers treats you as a guest of standing until you give it cause not to: it offers you hospitality before it offers you harm, and it tells you its terms before it holds you to them. In the Hidden Realm itself, you can't become lost, and you always know the way back to the threshold you came in by.

features.name: The Elder Cycles
features.text: You can call the whole year at once. As a Bonus Action, choose a point within 60 feet of yourself. Every creature of your choice in a 30-foot-radius Sphere centered there is subject to all four seasons, making each saving throw separately. A season's effect that would last until the start of a creature's next turn lasts until the end of its next turn instead. To resolve it quickly, each creature rolls its Constitution and Wisdom saving throws together, then its Strength saving throw (summer's damage needs no saving throw). Move the creatures that failed against spring last. This isn't a warp's season: it doesn't count against the limit of one warp's season a turn, and a creature can still be subject to one of your warps' seasons on the same turn. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: The Door Opens
features.text:
When you go Away, you can read up to a number of creatures you can see within 30 feet of yourself equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one), as part of the same Reaction, as if you had used Reading the Season; the DM can tell you their tempers when the fight allows. While you're Away, the door you carry stands open, and you gain these benefits:

- **The Storm.** At the start of each of your turns, choose a season you know. Each creature of your choice in a 15-foot Emanation originating from you is subject to it, and a creature you've read has Disadvantage on any saving throw against it. This counts as one of your warps' seasons, so a creature it takes can't be taken by a warp's season on the same turn. A season's effect that would last until the start of a creature's next turn lasts until the end of its next turn instead.
- **The Glamour Drops.** Each creature you've read that starts its turn within 30 feet of you and can see you makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC (you can spare any of them). On a failed save, it has the Charmed condition, with you as the charmer, until the start of its next turn: it can't bring itself to touch you, and must choose another target if it attacks.

The Storm takes the place of the warps Flicker leaves behind (The Door Ajar): while the door stands open, Flicker still moves you, but leaves no warp.

features.name: Second Sight
features.text: The Sight opens all the way. You have Truesight with a range of 60 feet. When you use Reading the Season, or read creatures as you go Away (The Door Opens), you can read any number of creatures you can see within 60 feet of yourself.

features.name: Epic Boon
features.text: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Fate is recommended.

features.name: Twist of Fate
features.text:
When you roll Initiative, you regain up to two expended warps, and you can then make up to two warps (no action required). Each warp you make this way expends a warp, as usual.

In addition, when a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself fails a saving throw, you can take a Reaction to turn the moment: it succeeds instead. Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclasses.name: Binding
subclasses.lead: You learn the arts of binding yourself and others, whether with word, thread, or root.

features.name: Binding Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Danae level specified in the Binding Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Danae Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Command*, *Dissonant Whispers*, *Warding Bond*, *Zone of Truth* |
| 5 | *Bestow Curse*, *Magic Circle* |
| 7 | *Compulsion*, *Phantasmal Killer* |
| 9 | *Dream*, *Planar Binding* |

features.name: Courtly Grace
features.text: You carry yourself as the most elevated of fae nobles. You gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: Deception, Intimidation, Performance, or Persuasion. You have Advantage on Charisma checks you make against a creature that is knotted by you.

features.name: Knots
features.text:
Your warps can be knots. As a Bonus Action, you tie a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself to another creature or to a fixed point within 30 feet of it (the ground, a tree, a door), and speak a geis into the knot. Each unwilling creature you tie makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. If they all succeed, no knot is tied, though the warp is still expended. If you were tying two creatures together and only one succeeds, the other is tied to the ground where it stands instead. A geis binds each unwilling creature in the knot; a willing creature is tied but not bound. An unwilling knotted creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, and the knot comes undone on a success. While knotted, it has Disadvantage on saving throws against your warps, its save to end this knot included. Choose the geis:

- **Stay.** It can't willingly move more than 30 feet from what it's tied to.
- **Spare.** It can't willingly target what it's tied to with an attack or a harmful effect.
- **Heed.** It has Disadvantage on attack rolls against anything but what it's tied to. When it attacks something else, it can break the geis instead of taking the Disadvantage.

*Breaking a Geis.* A knotted creature can choose to break its geis when it is about to do what the geis forbids: to walk away, to strike, to turn. If it does, it first takes Psychic damage equal to 2d8 plus your Charisma modifier, and the knot comes undone; then, if it can still act, it does what it chose. The damage increases to 3d8 at Danae level 10 and 4d8 at level 14.

features.name: Kind Words
features.text:
Your words echo with the terrible grace of the Hidden.

When you tie a knot, you can speak to one creature in it that can hear and understand you, as part of the same Bonus Action. It makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, it has your choice of the Frightened or Charmed condition, with you as the source, until the end of its next turn. At the start of any of its turns, the creature can defy you (no action required): it takes the same Psychic damage as breaking a geis, and then the condition ends.

You speak Kind Words once for each knot you tie.

features.name: Heartstrings
features.text: Creatures have Disadvantage on saving throws against your Kind Words. When a creature knotted to another creature fails its save against your Kind Words, you can choose to have the other affected too, without a saving throw; it counts as affected by your Kind Words.

features.name: Handfast
features.text: Outside combat, you can spend 10 minutes tying a binding between two or more willing creatures who make a promise to each other in your presence: a marriage, a contract, an apprenticeship, a truce, a sworn friendship. This costs no warp and isn't a knot for your other features. While the binding holds, each creature in it knows when another breaks the promise, and knows roughly which direction the others lie in, at any distance on the same plane. The binding holds until every creature in it agrees to untie it, or until you untie it. You can keep a number of bindings equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one); tying another unties your oldest.

features.name: Oath
features.text: As a Magic action, choose a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself that is knotted by you or that your Kind Words have affected within the last minute, and name a promise: to yield, to flee, to stand aside, to tell the truth, or not to harm a creature you name. It makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC; a willing creature can choose to fail. On a failed save, the promise binds it for 1 hour. The first time it breaks the promise, it takes 6d10 Psychic damage, and you know. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Thrall
features.text: As a Magic action, you take hold of a creature knotted by you that you can see. It makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC, with Disadvantage if it has the Charmed or Frightened condition from you. On a failed save, it is under your control until the end of your next turn, as the *Dominate Monster* spell, but the effect doesn't require Concentration. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

subclasses.name: Changing
subclasses.lead: Fate flows through and around you, and you learn to guide the stream.

features.name: Changing Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Danae level specified in the Changing Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Danae Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Augury*, *Bane*, *Bless*, *Enhance Ability* |
| 5 | *Beacon of Hope*, *Clairvoyance* |
| 7 | *Death Ward*, *Divination* |
| 9 | *Commune*, *Contact Other Plane* |

features.name: Lots
features.text:
Your warps can be lots. As a Bonus Action, you ready one: you roll the coin across your knuckles, shake the die, palm the card. A readied lot counts as a warp and, like your other warps, lasts for 1 minute or until you cast it.

When a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself fails or succeeds on a D20 Test, you can take a Reaction to cast a readied lot on it, and call it:

- **Fair,** when the creature fails. It rolls another d20 and uses the higher roll.
- **Foul,** when the creature succeeds. It rolls another d20 and uses the lower roll.

A lot you cast is spent.

features.name: Flow of Fate
features.text: The stream of fate runs under everyone near you, and you can pull it aside for them as easily as for yourself. When a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself is hit by an attack roll, you can use Denial for it instead of for yourself, unraveling one of your readied lots; the creature gains the bonus to AC against that attack. Denial's armor restriction applies to you, not to the creature you protect.

features.name: Small Mercies
features.text: Outside combat, when you or a companion goes looking for something ordinary you need (a dropped key, a cheap item a market might stock, a carter going your way, someone who knows the pass), the DM tells you where it turns up, if it can be found anywhere nearby. You can also tell when a game, a lottery, a drawing of lots, or a wager is rigged (marked cards, loaded dice, a fixed draw) by watching one round of it; you don't learn how, only that the house is cheating fate. Once you find something you went looking for, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest; telling a rigged game has no limit.

features.name: Losing Streak
features.text: When you call foul and the creature fails the check or saving throw or misses with the attack roll, you regain one expended warp. Once you regain a warp this way, you can't do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Road Luck
features.text: While you travel overland or by water with companions, the road's small mishaps don't befall your company unless the DM wants one for the story: no thrown shoe, cracked axle, spoiled flour, or missed tide. Further, when your company's way is uncertain (a fork, a fog, two inns), you can ask the DM which choice the year favors, and the DM answers "this one," "that one," or "neither." Once you ask, you can't ask again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Double or Nothing
features.text: When you ready a lot, you can ready a second as part of the same Bonus Action, expending a warp for each. When you cast a lot on an attack roll and the attack hits, the same call carries to the damage: the attacker rerolls the damage dice and uses the higher total (fair) or the lower (foul).

features.name: Lucky Charm
features.text: Gamblers, sailors, soldiers, midwives, brides, and anyone else who lives by chance can tell what you are after a few minutes in your company. They want you to blow on their dice, touch their nets, and stand at the back of the wedding. You have Advantage on Charisma checks to win over such people, and in any town you can support a Modest lifestyle by being lucky at people, without other work.

features.name: Loaded
features.text: When you cast a lot, instead of calling fair or foul, you can choose the number the roll uses, whether the creature failed or succeeded (if the creature rolled more than one d20, the roll uses only the number you choose). The number counts as rolled: a chosen 20 is a natural 20 (a Critical Hit on an attack roll), and a chosen 1 is a natural 1. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Coincidence
features.text: Outside combat, you can let the stream bring you a coincidence. Tell the DM what you need. The DM introduces it in the next scene or soon after, in the form the story allows: the person you were looking for is at the next table, a letter arrives a day early, the ship you missed is still in port because its captain lost at cards. The DM decides the form, and a coincidence never conjures what couldn't plausibly be there. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclasses.name: Crossing
subclasses.lead: A warded door means nothing to you when the wall beside it will do. Walls, floors, and roofs are only more doors, for you and for whoever you bring.

features.name: Crossing Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Danae level specified in the Crossing Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Danae Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Arcane Lock*, *Feather Fall*, *Knock*, *Silence* |
| 5 | *Gaseous Form*, *Nondetection* |
| 7 | *Freedom of Movement*, *Private Sanctum* |
| 9 | *Passwall*, *Teleportation Circle* |

features.name: Doors
features.text:
Your warps can be Doors. As a Bonus Action, you open a pair of linked Doors on solid surfaces you can see within 60 feet of yourself: a wall, a floor, a ceiling, the side of a cart. The pair counts as one warp. Each Door is a 5-foot square, or a 10-foot square from Danae level 5, and a creature fits through it only if the creature's space is no wider than the Door. A creature that moves into one Door of its own will steps out of the other, facing away from its surface; a Door doesn't send on a creature put into it any other way. When a feature refers to a warp's space, a Door's space is the space in front of it, as wide as the Door and 5 feet deep. A Door can open in the floor under a willing creature, which drops through.

*A Door of Your Own.* Your Doors are openings no one has warded. Iron and salt on a house's doors, windows, and chimney don't stop you, or anyone who comes through with you, from passing through a Door you open in its wall, floor, or roof (see "Iron and salt" in the Introduction). Your Gates and other teleportation get no such exception until Liminality, at level 10.

*Inertia.* A creature that falls into a Door comes out of the other still moving. It travels up to the distance it had already fallen, in the direction the far Door faces, before it falls normally or strikes something. When it lands or strikes something, it takes damage as for one fall of the whole distance it fell and traveled, and has the Prone condition if it takes any.

*Keyhole.* One of your Doors can open on a surface you can't see, if it's within 30 feet of yourself and on the far side of a wall, door, floor, or ceiling no more than 5 feet thick. You know whether the space beyond is open before you commit to it.

*Latch.* Once on each of your turns, when you pass through a pair of your Doors that are no more than 30 feet apart, you can latch them behind you: they close, and you regain the warp they used. Doors you leave open for your friends still cost their warp.

*Fellow Travellers.* When you go through one of your Doors, up to a number of willing creatures equal to your Proficiency Bonus within 5 feet of you can go through with you, arriving in unoccupied spaces within 5 feet of the far Door. For each of them, this counts as its one trip through your warps that turn.

features.name: Back Ways
features.text: You gain proficiency in the Stealth skill (if you already have it, choose another skill instead). You have a Climb Speed equal to your Speed, and your long jumps carry you 10 feet farther. After you spend a day in a settlement, you know its back ways: you can find a route between any two places in it that avoids its main streets, watch posts, and toll gates, if such a route exists. After you spend an hour in a building, you know every way into and out of it that a person could use (doors, windows, chimneys, drains, the servants' stair), even the ones its owner has forgotten, and where its walls are thin enough for a Door.

features.name: Seams
features.text: Every warp that fills a space is a Gate for you, whatever its shape: when you enter one of your warps, you can step out of any other (once per turn, as for all travel through your warps). While you're in one of your warps, you can take the Hide action as a Bonus Action on a turn you haven't made an attack roll, and you can hide there without cover and even while an enemy can see you. Hiding this way ends when you leave the space of your warps, unless you leave by traveling through one of them.

features.name: Where No One Follows
features.text: When you travel through one of your warps, you don't provoke Opportunity Attacks for the rest of that turn, and you can close the way behind you: until the start of your next turn, no creature can enter the warp you came out of except you and those who came through with you.

features.name: Misplace
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, you can unravel one of your warps and choose a creature or an object you can see within 60 feet of yourself. An object can't be armor or clothing a creature is wearing or an object a creature is attuned to.
- **A creature** makes a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC; a willing creature can choose to fail. On a failed save, it is teleported into the space of another of your warps within 60 feet of yourself, or the nearest unoccupied space, and that warp's season, if any, takes it at once.
- **An object** that a creature is holding or carrying lets that creature make a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the object appears in your hand or in the space of one of your warps. An object no one is holding or carrying gets no save.

features.name: Liminality
features.text: Your Keyhole reaches through up to 10 feet of wall, door, floor, or ceiling. Iron and salt never stopped your Doors (A Door of Your Own). From this level they don't stop your Gates either, and other wards don't stop your Gates or Doors: your Gates and Doors work through effects that block teleportation or planar travel in a place (a ward, a circle, a hallowed or forbidden area), other than an *Antimagic Field*. An effect that stops a particular creature from teleporting (the Hidden Killer's Cold Iron, Name It and ward, the Iron Bell magic item, a Faebreaker's grip) still stops that creature. Creatures that pass through your Gates and Doors don't trigger *Alarm*, *Glyph of Warding*, or similar warding magic, and need no invitation: an effect that keeps out uninvited creatures doesn't stop them. On foot, you're bound by such effects like anyone else (iron and salt at a door among them): the wall is your way in.

features.name: Outside
features.text: When an attack roll hits you or you fail a saving throw, you can take a Reaction and unravel one of your warps to step outside reality: the attack or effect does nothing to you. Until the start of your next turn, you can't be seen, targeted, or affected by anything, and you can't affect anything, though you keep Concentration. At the start of your next turn, you step back in, in the space you left or in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of it. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclasses.name: Naming
subclasses.lead: You have learned the Names of all things, and you carve them into wood, to command things and to burn them.

features.name: Naming Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Danae level specified in the Naming Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Danae Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Arcanist's Magic Aura*, *Identify*, *Illusory Script*, *Locate Object* |
| 5 | *Glyph of Warding*, *Tongues* |
| 7 | *Fire Shield*, *Locate Creature* |
| 9 | *Legend Lore*, *Scrying* |

features.name: Define
features.text:
Your Names are cut into wooden staves, in the ogham *feda* or in the letters of your own people's charms. As a Bonus Action, you define a creature, an object, or a place you can see within 60 feet of yourself, cutting its Name into a stave. Cutting a Name expends no warp, and a stave isn't one of your warps in place (you can't unravel it). A stave lasts until you finish a Long Rest or release it (no action required). You can keep a number of staves equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one); cutting another releases your oldest.

- **Named Creature.** You know its creature type, its Resistances, Immunities, and Vulnerabilities, and which of its saving throws has the lowest bonus. It can't hide from you, and the Invisible condition gives it no benefit against you. It also makes a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, it has Disadvantage on saving throws against your warps (Call included) while the stave lasts. On a successful save, the stave is still cut and you still learn what it tells you, but the creature has no Disadvantage against your warps, and you can't cut its Name again until you finish a Long Rest.
- **Named Object.** You can name only an object you have held, and only one object at a time; naming another releases the first. As a Bonus Action, you can summon it to your hand from anywhere on the same plane, unless another creature is holding or wearing it.
- **Named Place.** You always know the direction and distance to it.

*Ask the Name.* When you cut a Name, you can ask the DM one question about the thing you named, the kind of thing its Name would know: what it really is, who made it or owns it, where it has been, what was done there, what it wants. The DM answers truthfully, in a few words or a single image. You can ask a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. You can ask about any one creature, object, or place only once per Long Rest. A Named creature that succeeds on its Charisma saving throw keeps its answer to itself.

features.name: Call
features.text: You must have a warp in place within 60 feet of yourself. As a Bonus Action, you can speak the Name of a Named creature you can see, expending a warp, and choose one of your warps in place within 60 feet of yourself. The creature makes a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC; a willing creature can choose to fail. On a failed save, it is teleported into that warp's space, or the nearest unoccupied space to it.

features.name: Quick Cut
features.text: When you cut a Name, you can also make a warp as part of the same Bonus Action, expending a warp for it as usual.

features.name: Wrong Name
features.text: You know when a creature tells you a false name, for itself or for a person, place, or thing you can see.

features.name: Rename
features.text:
As a Magic action, you rename a Named creature, object, or place for 1 minute. It doesn't change: the renaming does only what the option you choose says, and nothing else about the thing is different. A creature, or an object a creature is holding or wearing, makes a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC to resist (the holder makes it for the object); a willing creature can choose to fail, and you can rename yourself. Choose one:

- **Creature: Kind.** Effects that detect creatures by type, or that keep out, admit, or ward against creatures of a type (*Detect Evil and Good*, *Hallow*, *Magic Circle*, *Protection from Evil and Good*, a glyph or ward keyed to a type), treat it as a creature type of your choice. Nothing else does: damage, what a spell can target, and what an effect does once it applies all use its true type. Wards against the Hidden (iron and salt among them) answer to this too, though being Hidden isn't a creature type (see the box in the Introduction): you can also name a Hidden creature not Hidden, and it passes those wards as if it weren't, so you can walk yourself or a friend through a warded door.
- **Object: Purpose.** It is named another kind of object, and it serves only as that. Choose one: *Shut* (a door, gate, lid, or window named a wall can't be opened, short of breaking it); *Open* (a lock named open is unlocked); *Harmless* (a weapon or piece of ammunition named a feather deals no damage); or *Plain* (it looks, feels, and sounds like another nonmagical object of the same size or smaller, a cup named a crown, or a crown a cup, though *Detect Magic*, *Identify*, and The Sight see it as it is). A renamed object never gains magical properties, never counts as a Material component with a cost, and isn't treasure.
- **Place: Threshold.** A space up to a 10-foot Cube is named a threshold to the Hidden, which The Sight can see and Thresholds can open. This renaming lasts 10 minutes instead of 1.
- **Place: Home.** A space up to a 30-foot Cube is named your home. A creature you haven't invited can't willingly enter it.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Lasting Staves
features.text: Your staves no longer end when you finish a Long Rest; they last until you release them. A kept stave keeps its Named creature's Disadvantage against your warps with it.

features.name: Unmake
features.text: As a Magic action, you burn the stave of a Named creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself. It makes a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, for 1 minute the world forgets what it is: it loses all its Resistances and Immunities, including Immunities to conditions; effects that rely on its creature type don't apply to it; and it takes 4d10 Fire damage at the start of each of its turns as its Name burns. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. On a successful save, it takes 4d10 Fire damage once. The stave is consumed either way. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclasses.name: Shaping
subclasses.lead: You see the true shape of reality and alter it to your whims.

features.name: Shaping Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Danae level specified in the Shaping Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Danae Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Floating Disk*, *Ice Knife*, *Levitate*, *Shatter* |
| 5 | *Meld into Stone*, *Tiny Hut* |
| 7 | *Fabricate*, *Stoneskin* |
| 9 | *Animate Objects*, *Creation* |

features.name: Stones
features.text: Your warps can be stones. A stone turns its Cube into solid ground, a wall (Total Cover), or a bridge, or opens a 5-foot-deep pit beneath its space. It is real, not an illusion; it has AC 15 and 30 Hit Points per 5-foot Cube. You can't make a stone on a creature (except a pillar or a pit, once you have Deep Ground at level 6), or make one that would leave a creature with no unoccupied space it could reach. Anything precious made this way is fairy gold (see Fae Weaving) and can't be made permanent.

features.name: Quick Weaving
features.text: As a Bonus Action, you can expend a warp to weave one object as Fae Weaving describes, without waiting for a rest and even before you have that feature. It lasts for 1 minute. After a minute's look at a building, a wall or a bridge, you know roughly how old it is and where it is weakest.

features.name: Deep Ground
features.text:
Your stones gain two shapes, a ramp or stair and a pillar that rises under a creature, lifting it 10 feet (when the stone ends, the pillar sinks back, lowering anything on it to the ground), and your pit can now open beneath a creature, which falls into the 5-foot-deep pit and has the Prone condition (when the stone ends, the ground rises back, lifting anything in the pit to the surface). A pillar or a pit can be made on a creature, following Warps' rule for that: the creature is lifted or falls only if it fails the Dexterity saving throw. Each stone takes only one shape.

With 1 hour of work, you can make a stone permanent; it no longer counts as a warp, so the warp it used comes back when you next finish a Short or Long Rest. You can have a number of permanent stones equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one); making another ends your oldest.

features.name: Dream Made Real
features.text: When you cast an illusion spell of level 1 or higher, you can make one object or surface in it real for as long as the illusion lasts. It must be Large or smaller and nonmagical, it can't deal damage, and it can't be made in a creature's space or enclose one. It is solid, bears weight, and blocks movement, and it is fairy gold. It can be a working thing, and it works as the real thing would: a rowboat that floats, a cart that rolls, a ladder with its winch, a locked door with its key.

features.name: Quarry
features.text: As a Magic action, you can place up to twelve 10-foot-Cube stones at once within 60 feet of yourself, in any shapes you know, ignoring the once-per-turn limit on making warps on creatures. They don't expend warps, and they last 1 hour; with 8 hours of work, the whole shape can be made permanent, and it counts as one of your permanent stones. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

multiclass.gains: Hit Point Die and training with Light armor
multiclass.text: You must have a Charisma score of 13 or higher. Gain the following traits from the Core Danae Traits table: Hit Point Die and training with Light armor. Gain the Danae's level 1 features, which are listed in the Danae Features table, except The Sight's skill proficiencies. For multiclass spell slots, add all your Danae levels, as you would Wizard levels. If you have levels in another class, you regain expended warps only when you finish a Long Rest.

new_spells.name: The Dwam
new_spells.text: You turn the Hidden's regard on a place. Each creature in a 20-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point you choose within range makes an Intelligence saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 8d6 Psychic damage and is in a daze for 1 minute: it subtracts 1d6 from each attack roll it makes. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and isn't in a daze.
